P2200.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2200.description: P2200 is the general electrical fault reported for the front NOx sensor on bank 1, the unit ahead of the SCR catalyst. Such sensors carry their own control unit, which checks the probe wiring and reports the result over CAN. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML) sets P2200 as a Type A fault once an open-circuit status keeps arriving for more than 0.5 s or 10 s, depending on calibration. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels use it for shorts or opens on the probe lines and for memory checksum errors inside the sensor controller. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI reacts to an error message or a validity ratio of at least 0.5. P2201 covers plausibility, P2202/P2203 a value out of range, P229E the downstream sensor. Dosing loses its feedback and the MIL comes on.

causes.label: Internal fault in the NOx probe or its attached control unit
Damaged cable between probe and sensor control unit (heat, chafing)
Moisture or corrosion in the sensor connector
Unstable supply or ground at the sensor control unit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx value in live data from the upstream sensor
SCR or emissions warning, possibly followed by inducement countdown

P2201.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2201.description: Here the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 is electrically intact, yet its reading is not believable. Manufacturers test this in different ways. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI compares the reading with modelled engine-out NOx (deviation beyond 60 percent), checks a slow fall from 100 to 60 percent (over 4.5 s) and an offset outside +50/-30 ppm. Ford runs a self-test after shutdown and flags an offset above about 20 ppm low or 40 ppm high. GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) watches internal pump-current stability, Type B over two trips. Ford TSBs 24-2136/24-2148 fix 2020-2023 6.7L trucks with a new sensor and software; Volvo and Mack warn that the code often results from another fault and ask for a conversion test first. P229F is the downstream twin.

causes.label: Aged or poisoned NOx sensing element with offset or slow response
Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor letting in outside air
Fault elsewhere (EGR, fuelling, DEF dosing) that shifts real NOx output
Control software calibration (Ford 6.7L 2020-2023, TSB 24-2136/24-2148)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored together with SCR efficiency codes such as P20EE
Increased AdBlue consumption or SCR warning

P2202.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2202.description: P2202 means the raw NOx value sent by the upstream sensor on bank 1 has dropped below the lowest figure a working sensor can report. Since the probe talks over CAN, the check concerns the transmitted value rather than a wire voltage. GM's Duramax diesels (6.6L LML and 3.0L LZ0) use a limit of minus 90 ppm, the LZ0 as Type B after two trips with dew point reached and supply in range; VW's 2014 Touareg TDI uses minus 105 ppm. GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists P2202 among codes cured by an LZ0 software update on 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500 pickups. A clearly negative value usually points to a drifting element or an internal sensor error. P2203 is the upper limit; P22A0 the same for sensor 2.

causes.label: NOx sensing element drifted low or internally faulty
Engine software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)
Damaged probe lead or connector between element and sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Live data shows a negative NOx value upstream
SCR dosing may switch to a fallback strategy

P2203.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2203.description: P2203 flags a raw NOx value from the upstream sensor on bank 1 that lies above anything the engine can actually emit. The limits differ: GM sets 1,500 or 2,500 ppm on the 6.6L Duramax (LML) and 2,500 ppm on the 3.0L LZ0 (Type B, two trips), VW 1,655 ppm on the 2014 Touareg TDI. On 2023 and 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500 pickups with the LZ0, GM bulletins 23-NA-193 and 24-NA-094 trace the code to software and prescribe an ECM update. Volvo and Mack class P2203 on the inlet sensor as a likely sensor failure and replace that sensor alone. P2202 is the lower limit, P2201 a plausible-looking but wrong reading, P22A1 the downstream counterpart. The MIL is on; SCR control loses a reliable input.

causes.label: Upstream NOx sensor reading high due to internal failure
ECM software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0, bulletins 23-NA-193 and 24-NA-094)
Sensing element contaminated by oil ash or DEF deposits

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Implausibly high upstream NOx value in live data
Possible over-dosing of AdBlue or SCR efficiency codes

P2204.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2204.description: P2204 describes an upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 whose signal path works most of the time but keeps dropping out. Smart NOx sensors report the state of their measuring circuit (open wire, short or no error) to the engine computer over CAN; when such fault messages come and go faster than a steady circuit fault would allow, this code fits. No manufacturer publicly documents thresholds for P2204, so the logic is calibration-specific; CARB generally requires continuous detection of circuit-continuity faults on NOx sensors. Look for loose pins, heat-damaged cable near the exhaust and water in the connector. P2200 is the steady circuit fault, P2202/P2203 a value out of range. Expect a MIL and SCR warnings that may disappear and return.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminals at the NOx sensor connector
Harness near the exhaust damaged by heat or vibration
Intermittent internal fault in the sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on, sometimes going out again
NOx value in live data dropping out briefly
SCR warning that comes and goes

P2205.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2205.description: The ceramic element of a NOx sensor only measures once its built-in heater has brought it to several hundred degrees. P2205 reports a break on the heater control side of the upstream sensor on bank 1. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML) sets it after the sensor has reported an open heater for over 10 s with at least 11 V; on the 3.0L LZ0 it is an open load on the heater control pin. Both are Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip. Volvo and Mack treat P2205 on the inlet sensor as a probable sensor failure, and GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists it for an LZ0 software update on 2024 pickups. P2206 and P2207 are shorts low and high, P220E heater power out of range, P22A3 the downstream sensor.

causes.label: Heater element in the NOx probe burnt through
Broken conductor in the lead between probe and sensor module
Software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Upstream NOx sensor never becomes ready
SCR warning on the display

P2206.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2206.description: A NOx sensor needs its ceramic element heated to several hundred degrees before it can measure. P2206 means the heater control circuit of the first (upstream) NOx sensor on bank 1 reads low, typically a short to ground or a driver output stuck low. CARB requires diesel OBD to detect heater circuit opens and shorts that conflict with the commanded state. GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) lists it as NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low; Volvo and Mack trucks treat P2206 on the inlet sensor as an internal sensor failure and replace the sensor. P2205 is the general heater circuit fault, P2207 the high side, P2208-P2211 the heater sense circuit. The SCR system loses NOx feedback.

causes.label: Internal heater or control-unit fault in the NOx sensor
Heater wiring chafed to ground near the exhaust
Moisture or corrosion in the sensor connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR or emissions warning on the display
Usually no change in driveability

P2207.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2207.description: P2207 is the high-side counterpart of P2206: the heater control circuit of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 shows a voltage that is too high for the commanded state, typically an open heater element or a short to supply voltage. CARB requires the diesel OBD system to flag such circuit faults that contradict the command. GM lists P2207 as NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High for the 2024 Silverado/Sierra 3.0L diesel (LZ0). Without heating the sensor never becomes ready, so SCR dosing runs without NOx feedback. P2205 is the general heater circuit code, P2206 the low side, and P2208-P2211 concern the heater feedback circuit. P22A5 is the same fault on sensor 2.

causes.label: Heater element inside the NOx sensor burnt open
Open circuit or short to voltage in the heater wiring
Loose or heat-damaged connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx readiness or SCR efficiency faults may follow

P2208.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2208.description: Besides the control line, the NOx sensor heater has a sense or feedback path through which the controller checks how the heater actually responds (current, resistance or element temperature). P2208 marks a general fault in this sense circuit of the upstream sensor on bank 1. GM calls it NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit (3.0L LZ0 diesel); Volvo and Mack class P2208 on the inlet sensor as a sensor failure that requires replacement. CARB demands heater performance monitoring within the supplier's limits. P2209 is the plausibility check of the same feedback, P2210/P2211 low or high values, P2212 dropouts; P2205-P2207 concern the control side. MIL on, driveability normal.

causes.label: Internal fault in the NOx sensor or its control unit
Damaged wiring between sensor element and sensor control unit
Water ingress in the connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor reports no valid value

P2209.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2209.description: P2209 is the performance check of the NOx sensor heater: the feedback is electrically present but shows that the element does not reach or hold operating temperature as expected. VW's 2014 TDI specification books (Passat, Touareg) set it when NOx control has not become active more than 180 s after the dew point was passed. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary uses P2209 as NOx signal readiness, judged by the ratio of actual to expected sensor on-time. GM names it Heater Feedback Performance. CARB requires both heater performance and NOx sensor activity monitoring. P2208 is the circuit fault, P2210/P2211 low or high values. MIL after confirmation, no limp mode.

causes.label: Aged NOx sensor element that heats up too slowly
Low supply voltage or poor ground to the sensor
Prolonged cold or wet exhaust delaying dew-point release

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor not ready for long periods after start
Possible follow-up SCR efficiency faults

P220A.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220A.description: A smart NOx sensor draws its own operating power, mostly for the probe heater. P220A means the supply reaching the upstream sensor on bank 1 is outside its window. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels flag above 16.5 V or below 8.5 V; GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) flags below 9.9 V while the engine runs, Type B after two trips. On the 6.6L LML, GM feeds the sensor from a DC/DC booster in the glow plug module and sets P220A when that module reports its output shorted or overloaded (Type B). VW's 2014 Touareg TDI uses a 1.5 V deviation. Volvo and Mack advise checking supply wiring, fuses and relays rather than the sensor. P220B is the downstream sensor, P220C/P220D bank 2. The sensor stays inactive.

causes.label: Blown fuse, faulty relay or poor ground in the sensor supply
Supply wire chafed, corroded or with high resistance
Supply booster in the glow plug control module (GM 6.6L LML)
Weak battery or charging-system voltage out of range

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Upstream NOx sensor shows no value or no communication
Other NOx sensor codes stored at the same time

P220B.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220B.description: P220B concerns the second NOx sensor on bank 1, the one behind the SCR catalyst whose reading proves how well NOx is being converted. Its operating voltage is outside the allowed band. Ford applies the same 8.5 to 16.5 V window as for the front sensor; GM's 3.0L LZ0 flags under 9.9 V (Type B), and VW's 2014 Touareg TDI compares battery and sensor supply, faulting a gap above 1.5 V. GM's 2018 Equinox and Terrain with the 1.6L diesel (LH7) could log P220B through a software issue; PIP5615A points to bulletin 19-NA-009 and an ECM calibration. Volvo and Mack class it as a supply problem, not a sensor failure. Without this sensor the catalyst efficiency check cannot run. P220A is the front sensor.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or ground fault in the downstream sensor supply
Supply wire to the rear sensor damaged under the vehicle
ECM calibration (GM 1.6L LH7 2018, PIP5615A / 19-NA-009)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Downstream NOx sensor shows no value
SCR efficiency monitor stays incomplete

P220C.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P220C.description: P220C is reserved for an engine with a separate exhaust path per cylinder bank, each with its own NOx sensors, and reports that the upstream sensor on bank 2 is not getting a proper supply voltage. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the diesel pickups and trucks examined (Ford, GM, VW, Volvo/Mack) merge both banks into one SCR line and only use the bank 1 codes. By analogy with P220A, a fault would mean the supply sits outside a window like Ford's 8.5 to 16.5 V, or the supplying module reports a short. Smart sensors send their supply status over CAN, so the engine computer learns it from the sensor itself. Check fuse, relay, ground and wiring for that bank. P220D is the downstream sensor on bank 2.

causes.label: Fuse, relay or ground fault in the bank 2 sensor supply
Supply wiring to the bank 2 upstream sensor damaged
System voltage out of range (battery or alternator)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx value from the bank 2 upstream sensor

P220D.title: NOx Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P220D.description: P220D covers the last position in this group: the downstream NOx sensor on bank 2, after that bank's own SCR catalyst, has a supply voltage outside its window. It only exists on engines whose two banks keep separate aftertreatment, which none of the publicly documented diesel applications do; no manufacturer lists the code with thresholds. Ford's bank 1 rear sensor code P220B uses 8.5 to 16.5 V, a useful reference. A dead rear sensor means the efficiency monitor for the bank 2 catalyst cannot finish. CARB requires NOx sensor diagnostics to catch wiring breaks and readings beyond range. P220C is the upstream sensor on the same bank, P220B the rear sensor on bank 1. Check supply fuse, ground and connector first.

causes.label: Supply fuse, relay or ground fault for the bank 2 rear sensor
Corroded connector exposed to road spray behind the catalyst
Internal fault in the supply stage of the sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR efficiency monitor for bank 2 not completed

P220E.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P220E.description: P220E says the heater of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 is not behaving as commanded. Ford's 6.7L and 3.0L diesels bundle several checks under it: an open heater found by the sensor hardware, a short to positive (over 5 V on the heater), a short to ground (0 V), and a duty cycle that differs from the expected one by more than 20 percent. Ford TSBs 24-2136 and 24-2148 cover 2020-2023 F-Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with P220E alongside P2201 and P2209, fixed with a new sensor plus PCM and TCM software. Volvo and Mack state that P220E with failure type 93 usually calls for a new inlet sensor. P2205-P2207 are the plain heater circuit faults, P220F the downstream sensor.

causes.label: Aged heater element in the upstream NOx probe
Sensor and PCM software (Ford 6.7L 2020-2023, TSB 24-2136/24-2148)
Heater wiring or ground with high resistance or shorts

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Upstream NOx sensor slow to become ready after start
Often stored with P2201 or P2209

P220F.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P220F.description: P220F is the heater check of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1, the one after the SCR catalyst. Ford's diesel summary (it titles the code as a heater sense circuit fault) flags a heater current under 0.4 A, a short to battery or to ground, or a heater duty cycle more than 20 percent away from the expected value. Volvo and Mack use P220F with failure type 93 for their outlet sensor and recommend replacing only that sensor when the code is confirmed. Because the rear sensor confirms catalyst efficiency, a cold sensor delays or blocks the SCR monitor. P220E is the upstream counterpart; P22A3-P22A5 are the plain heater circuit faults of sensor 2. The MIL comes on, while the engine runs normally.

causes.label: Heater of the downstream NOx probe weak or failed
Heater wiring of the rear sensor shorted or with high resistance
Water or salt in the rear sensor connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
SCR efficiency monitor not completing

P2210.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2210.description: P2210 means the heater feedback signal of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 sits below its permitted range. Typical electrical causes are a short to ground in the sense line or a failed measuring stage in the sensor electronics. GM lists the code as NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit Low for the 2024 Silverado/Sierra 3.0L diesel (LZ0). CARB requires the OBD system to detect heater circuit faults that conflict with the commanded state. P2211 is the opposite direction, P2208 the general sense-circuit fault, P2209 a plausible but poor heating result, and P2206 a low reading on the control side. The sensor then delivers no usable NOx value; the MIL comes on.

causes.label: Fault in the sensor element or its control unit
Sense line shorted to ground
Corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx reading in live data

P2211.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2211.description: P2211 flags a heater feedback signal above its permitted range on the upstream NOx sensor of bank 1. An open sense line, a short to supply voltage or an interrupted heater element that the electronics reads as maximum resistance are the usual reasons. GM lists it as NOx Sensor Heater Feedback Circuit High for the 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) in the 2024 Silverado/Sierra. Under CARB rules such circuit faults must be detected regardless of operating conditions. P2210 is the low direction, P2208 the general fault, P2209 the performance check and P2207 the high fault on the control side. The NOx sensor stays unready, SCR control falls back on modelled values, and the MIL lights up.

causes.label: Interrupted heater element in the NOx sensor
Open sense line or short to voltage
Loose or heat-damaged connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
NOx sensor stays not ready

P2212.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2212.description: Besides driving the heater, the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1 has a sense path that reports back how the heater actually responds; GM measures heater resistance on a separate HTemp pin. P2212 means this feedback keeps dropping out or jumping instead of failing for good. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2212; GM's 3.0L LZ0 tables cover only the steady cases (P2208 open, P2210 short to ground, P2211 short to power). CARB requires heater circuit faults that contradict the commanded state to be caught. Typical causes are a loose contact or cracked lead that opens with heat or vibration. P2209 is a plausible but poor heater response; P2205-P2207 concern the control side. The MIL may come and go.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact in the NOx sensor connector
Cracked conductor in the probe lead that opens with heat or vibration
Intermittent fault in the sensor module's heater measurement

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on, possibly intermittent
Upstream NOx value briefly invalid

P2213.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
P2213.description: P2213 mirrors P2200 for the second cylinder bank: the NOx sensor serving bank 2 ahead of its SCR catalyst reports a general electrical fault. That presumes an engine whose banks feed separate aftertreatment lines. No manufacturer documents P2213 publicly; even V8 diesels such as GM's 6.6L Duramax, Ford's 6.7L and the Cummins 5.0L in Nissan's Titan XD route both banks into a single SCR line and use bank 1 codes only. As a guide, GM's LML logs P2200 when the smart sensor keeps signalling an interrupted wire for 0.5 or 10 s, and Ford adds probe-line shorts and checksum errors inside the sensor controller. CARB requires circuit faults on NOx sensors to be caught. P2214 to P2217 cover the other bank 2 signal faults.

causes.label: Internal fault in the bank 2 NOx probe or its sensor control unit
Heat-damaged or chafed lead between probe and sensor control unit
Water or corrosion in the bank 2 sensor connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No NOx value from the bank 2 sensor in live data
SCR warning, possibly with an inducement countdown

P2214.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2214.description: Under J2012, P2214 is the plausibility fault of the bank 2 NOx sensor: wiring intact, reading not credible. No maker uses it that way in public documents. Hino does use the number differently: on its J08E inline six (Hino 238, 258, 268 and 338 conventional models, 2011 to 2016) P2214 belongs to NOx sensor 2 behind the SCR catalyst. Hino bulletin SB-14-029 first checks DEF concentration (31.8 to 33.2 percent), exhaust leaks, temperature and airflow sensors and the dosing injector, then re-tests at a steady 45 to 50 mph after a regeneration. SB-15-038 and SB-16-002 link P2214 and P2201 to NOx heater elements cracked by condensation and add DCU software. For a real bank 2 sensor, P2201 logic applies (VW: 60 percent deviation).

causes.label: Aged or poisoned NOx element reading with offset or slow response
Sensor heater cracked by condensation (Hino 2015-2016, SB-15-038/SB-16-002)
Diluted DEF or faulty dosing injector distorting the NOx reading
Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored with P2201 or SCR efficiency code P20EE
Higher DEF consumption or SCR warning

P2215.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2215.description: P2215 says the NOx value transmitted for bank 2 falls below the smallest figure a healthy sensor can deliver. Because smart NOx sensors talk over CAN, the limit is a concentration in ppm, not a wire voltage. No manufacturer publishes this bank 2 code; the diesels on record send both banks through one SCR system and use P2202 instead. Those bank 1 limits give the scale: GM's 6.6L and 3.0L Duramax flag readings below minus 90 ppm (on the LZ0 only after the dew point is reached, Type B over two trips), VW's 2014 Touareg TDI below minus 105 ppm. A strongly negative value usually comes from a drifted element or a fault inside the sensor electronics. P2216 is the high limit, P2213 the general circuit fault.

causes.label: NOx element of the bank 2 sensor drifted low
Fault in the measuring electronics of the sensor module
Damaged lead between probe and sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Negative NOx value for bank 2 in live data
DEF dosing switches to a substitute strategy

P2216.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2216.description: P2216 is set when the NOx concentration reported for bank 2 exceeds anything the engine could plausibly emit. It belongs to engines with an SCR line per cylinder bank; none of the documented diesels is built that way, and no manufacturer lists P2216 publicly. The bank 1 code P2203 shows what such a check looks like: GM trips at 1,500 or 2,500 ppm on the 6.6L LML and at 2,500 ppm on the 3.0L LZ0 (Type B, two trips), VW at 1,655 ppm on the 2014 Touareg TDI. An overreading probe can make the dosing controller inject too much DEF, risking ammonia slip, so the reading is discarded. Internal sensor failure is the most frequent reason. P2215 is the low limit, P2214 a believable but wrong value.

causes.label: Bank 2 NOx sensor reading too high due to internal failure
Sensing element fouled by oil ash or DEF crystals
Calibration error in the engine or dosing control software

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Implausibly high NOx value for bank 2 in live data
SCR efficiency codes may follow

P2217.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2217.description: P2217 describes a bank 2 NOx sensor whose measuring path fails only now and then: the reading drops out or the sensor briefly reports an electrical error, then recovers. A smart NOx sensor evaluates its own probe lines and sends status flags for open or shorted circuits alongside the value over CAN; flags that toggle point to this code rather than to the steady fault P2213. No manufacturer documents P2217, nor its bank 1 twin P2204, with thresholds, so the debounce logic is calibration-specific; CARB generally requires continuous detection of NOx sensor continuity faults. Typical causes are a loose terminal, a lead that cracks when hot, or water entering the connector. The warning lamp may come and go.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminals at the bank 2 sensor connector
Lead near the exhaust cracked by heat or vibration
Sporadic fault in the sensor module electronics

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Bank 2 NOx value briefly invalid in live data

P2218.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)
P2218.description: A NOx sensor cannot measure until its built-in heater has taken the ceramic cell to several hundred degrees, and the sensor electronics switches that heater itself. P2218 reports a break in the heater control path of the bank 2 sensor, either inside the probe or in the lead to the sensor module. No manufacturer documents the bank 2 version. The bank 1 code P2205 is well described: GM's 6.6L LML sets it when an open heater is reported longer than 10 s with the battery at 11 V or more, the 3.0L LZ0 on an open load at the heater control pin, both Type A with the MIL after one trip. Without heating, the bank 2 sensor never becomes ready. P2219 and P2220 are the shorted cases, P2221 the heater sense side.

causes.label: Heater element in the bank 2 NOx probe burnt through
Broken conductor between probe and sensor module
Pushed-back or corroded pin in the sensor connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Bank 2 NOx sensor never reports ready

P2219.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2219.description: P2219 means the heater control line of the bank 2 NOx sensor is pulled toward ground when it should not be, typically a heater lead chafed against the exhaust or a shorted output stage in the sensor electronics. The control unit then switches the heater off to protect itself. Bank 2 use is not documented by any manufacturer, as known SCR diesels combine both banks. For the bank 1 counterpart P2206, GM's 3.0L Duramax (LZ0) counts 80 failures in 160 samples taken every 25 ms, with relay voltage above 11 V and the dew point passed, and stores a Type B fault lighting the MIL after two trips. Volvo and Mack treat P2206 on their inlet sensor as a sensor failure. P2218 is the open circuit, P2220 the short to power.

causes.label: Heater lead of the bank 2 sensor chafed through to ground
Shorted heater or output stage inside the sensor
Salt water bridging pins in the connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Bank 2 NOx sensor stays cold and delivers no value

P221A.title: NOx Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 1)
P221A.description: P221A compares the two NOx sensors of bank 1, upstream and downstream of the SCR catalyst. When conditions should make both read alike, the gap between them is too large, so the system cannot tell which value to trust. Volvo and Mack list P221A among codes that often lead to needless sensor swaps; before replacement a NOx conversion test must show the inlet and outlet readings disagreeing by more than about 40 ppm shortly before engine shutdown, or the cause lies elsewhere. Nissan bulletin NTB16-048 covers early 2016 Titan XD trucks with the Cummins 5.0L V8: P221A with P229E and P22A7 is fixed by a new outlet sensor and ECM reprogramming. P2201 and P229F judge each sensor alone, P221B is bank 2.

causes.label: One of the two NOx sensors (often the outlet sensor) reading wrongly
Exhaust leak between the two sensors diluting the reading
ECM software (Nissan Titan XD 5.0L 2016, NTB16-048)
Faulty DEF dosing distorting the comparison

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored with P20EE or other SCR codes
Implausible NOx conversion values in live data

P221B.title: NOx Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P221B.description: P221B compares the NOx sensors before and after the SCR catalyst of bank 2. When operating conditions should make them agree, their readings differ by more than the calibration allows, and the controller cannot decide which value is wrong. The code requires a separate SCR line on bank 2, which no publicly documented diesel has; no manufacturer lists P221B. The bank 1 twin P221A shows the practice: Volvo and Mack require a NOx conversion test before any part is changed and only accept a sensor fault if inlet and outlet readings differ by more than roughly 40 ppm shortly before shutdown, while Nissan bulletin NTB16-048 replaced the outlet sensor and reflashed the ECM on 2016 Titan XD trucks.

causes.label: One of the two bank 2 NOx sensors reading wrongly
Exhaust leak between the two sensors
Dosing that does not stop or leaks, distorting the comparison

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored with SCR efficiency codes
Inlet and outlet NOx values for bank 2 disagree in live data

P221C.title: Reductant Heater B Current Too Low
P221C.description: P221C reports that heater B of the DEF system draws too little current while switched on. GM and Ford both assign B to the heated pressure line that carries DEF to the dosing valve. GM's 2025 Duramax tables flag line heater current under 0.75 A with a PWM command above zero, 40 faulty readings spaced 0.1 s apart, Type A with the MIL after one trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary watches heater B continuously while it runs and decides within 2.2 s: below 3 A with more than 5 V supplied, line power below 1 W or lower than expected. GM's 2014 tables for the 6.6L LML judged conductance instead (0.28 S or less), Type B. An open or burnt line heater is the usual find; P221D is the high-current partner.

causes.label: Heating element in the DEF pressure line open or burnt
Corroded or loose connector at the heated line
Missing heater supply (fuse, relay or harness)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF line may freeze in winter, dosing starts late
DEF system warning, inducement possible if unresolved

P221D.title: Reductant Heater B Current Too High
P221D.description: P221D is stored when heater B, the electrically heated DEF pressure line at GM and Ford, takes more current or power than its design permits. That usually means a partly shorted element or a lead touching ground, and the controller cuts the heater to save its driver. GM's 2025 Duramax tables trip above 15 A, counted over 40 samples of 0.1 s while the vehicle is active, Type A with the MIL on the first trip and recovery only in the next drive cycle. Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags line heater power above the expected value within 2.2 s of continuous monitoring. On the 2014 6.6L LML, GM read the line heater conductance and set the code at 0.92 S or more, Type B. P221C is the low-current partner, P20BF a low control circuit.

causes.label: Partly shorted heating element in the DEF pressure line
Heater lead chafed to ground
Water in the line heater connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip (GM)
Line heater switched off, DEF may stay frozen in cold weather

P221E.title: Reductant Heater C Current Too Low
P221E.description: P221E says DEF heater C pulls too little current while commanded on. Which element is C depends on the system. In GM's 2025 Duramax tables heater 3 is a second tank heater; the code needs a PWM command above zero and trips under 0.75 A after 40 readings taken every 0.1 s, a Type A fault with the MIL after one trip. GM's 2014 tables for the 6.6L LML gave the letter to the heater in the supply (pump) module instead: conductance of 0.14 S or less, checked once per trip with the battery at 11 V or more, Type B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary has a heater C only with a supply voltage check (P20C2) and does not list P221E. In frost the thawing of DEF around that heater is slow. P221F is the high-current partner, P20C1 the open control circuit.

causes.label: Heater C element open or burnt (tank or supply module, by system)
Corroded or wet connector at the tank or pump unit
Heater supply missing (fuse, relay, harness)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Slow DEF thawing in cold weather, dosing starts late

P221F.title: Reductant Heater C Current Too High
P221F.description: P221F flags excessive current through DEF heater C, pointing to a partial short in the element or its lead. GM's 2025 Duramax tables, where heater 3 is the second tank heater, set the code above 15 A over 40 samples of 0.1 s whenever the vehicle is active, Type A with the MIL after one trip, and zero all heater PWM commands while any heater fault is present. In GM's 2014 tables for the 6.6L LML, C denoted the supply module heater, and high conductance (0.46 S or more in one table, 0.35 S in the other) set a Type B fault once per trip. Ford's 2023 diesel summary does not use P221F. A shorted heater draws more than its driver tolerates, so the area it serves stays unheated. P221E is the low-current partner.

causes.label: Partly shorted heater C element
Heater lead chafed to ground at the tank or pump unit
Water or DEF crystals in the heater connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip (GM)
DEF heating disabled, possible frozen-DEF warnings in winter

P2220.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2220.description: P2220 is the high-side counterpart of P2219: on the bank 2 NOx sensor, the heater control line carries battery voltage when the heater should be off or regulated, so the element may overheat or the output stage cannot switch. A pinched lead touching a feed wire or a failed driver inside the sensor are the usual causes. The bank 2 code is not documented by any manufacturer. GM's 3.0L LZ0 describes the bank 1 version P2207 as a short to battery at the heater control pin, judged on 80 of 160 samples with over 11 V on the powertrain relay and confirmed as Type B after two trips. P2218 is the open circuit and P2224 a high signal on the heater sense side. Until repaired, SCR control for bank 2 runs without NOx feedback.

causes.label: Heater control lead shorted to a supply wire
Failed heater driver inside the bank 2 sensor module
Heat-damaged connector with pins bridged

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Bank 2 NOx reading missing or invalid

P2221.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 2)
P2221.description: Alongside the heater drive, a NOx sensor has a sense path that tells the electronics how the heater is really behaving, usually by measuring its resistance, which tracks cell temperature. P2221 reports a general fault in that sense circuit on the bank 2 sensor. Public documentation exists only for the bank 1 code P2208: GM's 3.0L LZ0 checks the separate HTemp pin for an open load, 80 failures in 160 samples at over 11 V, Type A with the MIL after one trip, and notes that its Continental sensors debounce electrical faults internally for 1.5 s. No manufacturer lists the bank 2 version. Without valid feedback the sensor cannot regulate its temperature. P2222 to P2225 are the specific sense faults.

causes.label: Fault in the heater measurement of the bank 2 sensor
Open sense conductor between probe and sensor module
Corrosion in the sensor connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Bank 2 NOx sensor not ready

P2222.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P2222.description: With P2222 the heater feedback of the bank 2 NOx sensor is electrically present, yet what it reports does not match the heating command: the cell warms too slowly or settles at the wrong resistance. No manufacturer documents this bank 2 code. Two bank 1 descriptions show the approach. GM's 3.0L LZ0 (P2209) compares raw heater resistance with its target and fails a deviation over 3 percent in 50 of 100 samples, only after 45 s of good supply and 180 s past the dew point, Type B. Ford's diesel summary uses the matching rear sensor code P220F for heater current below 0.4 A or a duty cycle more than 20 percent off. An aged heater or weak supply is typical. P2221 is the general sense fault.

causes.label: Aged heater in the bank 2 NOx probe with drifted resistance
Low supply voltage or poor ground at the sensor module
Heater wiring with added resistance

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Bank 2 NOx sensor slow to become ready after a cold start
SCR monitor for bank 2 delayed

P2223.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P2223.description: P2223 indicates that the heater sense line of the bank 2 NOx sensor sits at or near ground potential, so the electronics reads an impossibly low value for heater resistance. A sense conductor rubbed through to the exhaust bracket or a shorted measuring input inside the sensor module are the usual explanations. No manufacturer publishes the bank 2 code. For bank 1, GM's 3.0L LZ0 tables carry the equivalent P2210 as a grounded HTemp pin, judged on 80 failed of 160 samples with the powertrain relay above 11 V, Type B, so the MIL waits for a second trip. With no usable feedback the sensor cannot hold its working temperature. P2224 is the opposite polarity, P2219 a low fault on the control side.

causes.label: Sense lead of the bank 2 sensor shorted to ground
Shorted measuring input in the sensor module
Water ingress in the connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
No valid NOx value from bank 2

P2224.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 2)
P2224.description: P2224 is logged when the heater sense signal of the bank 2 NOx sensor is too high, which the electronics sees as a short to supply voltage or as an interrupted heater reading near infinite resistance. The bank 2 code appears in no public manufacturer document. GM documents the bank 1 version P2211 for the 3.0L LZ0 as an HTemp pin shorted toward supply: 80 failed of 160 samples, powertrain relay above 11 V, sensor bus relay switched on, Type B over two trips. Since the sensor module cannot judge cell temperature, it holds back its NOx value and SCR control for that bank falls back on modelled emissions. P2223 is the low direction, P2220 a high fault on the control side, P2225 a sporadic sense fault.

causes.label: Heater element in the bank 2 probe open, read as maximum resistance
Sense lead shorted to a voltage source
Fault in the sensor module input stage

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Bank 2 NOx sensor stays unready

P2225.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P2225.description: P2225 covers a heater sense circuit on the bank 2 NOx sensor that fails only for moments: the feedback drops out or jumps, then returns to normal, which a steady open or short code would not describe. No manufacturer documents thresholds for P2225 or for its bank 1 twin P2212. GM's 3.0L LZ0 tables handle only the persistent faults on the HTemp pin (P2208, P2210, P2211) and mention that the Continental sensors debounce electrical errors for 1.5 s internally, so very short glitches may never reach the engine computer. Smart sensors flag heater faults over CAN. Look for a cracked conductor that opens when hot, a loose terminal or moisture. The warning lamp may switch on and off between drives.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact in the bank 2 sensor connector
Cracked sense conductor that opens with heat or vibration
Sporadic fault in the heater measurement of the sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Bank 2 NOx value briefly invalid

P2226.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P2226.description: P2226 is the general circuit code for barometric pressure sensor A, the sensor that tells the engine computer the outside air pressure for air-charge, fuel and boost calculations. Ford's OBD summary for 2024-2025 gasoline engines shows how the code appears in current software: every BARO fault is reported as P2226 plus a failure-type byte, -16 for a low voltage (formerly P2228), -17 for high (P2229), -92 for a plausibility error (P2227) and -1F for an erratic signal (P2230). The same list makes all four block auto start-stop. On Ford gasoline engines the sensor sits on the PCM circuit board. A plain P2226 without failure type is rare; sensor B has its own family from P222A. Expect the warning light and a default pressure value.

causes.label: Fault of the barometric sensor built into the engine control module
Damaged wiring or loose connector on an external BARO sensor
5 V reference supply of the sensor pulled down by another faulty sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Auto start-stop no longer works
Failure-type suffix (-16, -17, -92, -1F) shown with the code on newer scan tools

P2227.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2227.description: P2227 means the barometric reading is electrically fine but does not fit the other pressure signals. Ford's 2012 summary compares BARO, throttle inlet and manifold pressure after at least 10 s engine-off; the sensor that disagrees with the other two is blamed. While driving at low airflow BARO must stay within 5.5 inHg of throttle inlet pressure. Ford's 2023 diesels set P2227 for a reading below 50 kPa held for 1 s. GM's 2018 diesel tables run the same three-way check at idle and before start, plus a 50-115 kPa window, as Type B. GM bulletins 22-NA-007 (Cruze 1.4 turbo) and 23-NA-002 (Silverado/Sierra 2.7 L) trace P2227 with P0299 to ice in the charge air cooler; the fix is new ECM software plus a baffle.

causes.label: Ice or sludge in the charge air cooler on turbo engines in severe cold (GM 22-NA-007, 23-NA-002)
BARO sensor reading with an offset or drift
Faulty boost or manifold pressure sensor that skews the comparison
Engine control software that needs an update

symptoms: Check engine light
Reduced power or hesitation in very cold weather on turbo engines
P0299 or misfire codes stored alongside

P2228.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P2228.description: P2228 sets when the voltage from barometric pressure sensor A stays below the lowest value a real atmosphere could produce. Ford's gasoline summaries (2012 and 2020-2023) use under 2.0 V, which would mean an altitude above 15,000 ft, for 5 s; on these engines the sensor is mounted on the PCM circuit board. Ford's 2023 diesels flag under 0.25 V (about 6 kPa) after 0.5 s. GM's 2018 diesel tables attribute it to a grounded or broken signal line on a pull-down input: below 35.5 % of the 5 V supply (equal to 50 kPa) in 320 of 400 readings, Type B with the MIL after two trips. In Ford's 2024 software the same fault appears as P2226-16. P2229 is the high counterpart. The engine runs on a substitute pressure, so drivers mostly see only the lamp.

causes.label: Signal wire of an external BARO sensor shorted to ground or open
Defective sensor inside the PCM (Ford, Mazda and others), PCM replacement
Low or missing 5 V reference to the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Auto start-stop deactivated
Scan tool shows an implausibly low barometric pressure

P2229.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P2229.description: P2229 reports a barometric sensor A voltage above anything plausible for outside air. Ford's gasoline engines judge more than 4.4 V, an altitude below -1,000 ft, over 5 s; the 2023 diesels use 4.85 V (115 kPa) after 0.5 s. GM's 2018 diesel tables look for contact with a voltage source: over 94.1 % of the 5 V range (115.1 kPa) in 320 of 400 readings, Type B. Mazda bulletin 01-008/20 shows a less obvious cause on the 2018-2020 Mazda6 2.5 turbo: the BARO sensor lives inside the PCM and breathes through a filter hole on its underside. Wax sprayed into the engine bay can seal that hole, so the trapped air builds pressure as the PCM heats up. Mazda replaces the PCM with a reshaped bracket. Ford's 2024 software reports P2226-17 instead; P2228 is the low counterpart.

causes.label: Breather filter of a PCM-internal BARO sensor clogged (e.g. engine-bay wax, Mazda 01-008/20)
Signal wire of an external sensor shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Internal fault of the sensor or the control module

symptoms: Check engine light, often only after the engine bay has heated up
Auto start-stop deactivated
Scan tool shows barometric pressure far above the real value

P222A.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P222A.description: P222A is the general circuit code for a second barometric pressure sensor, B. Only some engines carry one. GM's tables for the 3.0 L twin-turbo V6 (LGW, 2018) and for 2023-2024 twin-throttle engines monitor such a sensor B, but they report its circuit faults with the more specific codes P222C (low) and P222D (high) and do not use P222A. No maker documents P222A publicly. Read it as an unspecified electrical fault of sensor B, comparable to P2226 for sensor A, which Ford now stores with a failure-type byte that tells the type of fault. CARB requires circuit monitoring of every input sensor used by an emission-relevant function. Check wiring, connector and the 5 V supply; the engine usually keeps running on sensor A or a model value.

causes.label: Damaged wiring or corroded connector at sensor B
Barometric pressure sensor B defective
Fault in the shared 5 V sensor supply

symptoms: Check engine light
Usually no noticeable change in how the engine runs

P222B.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P222B.description: P222B means sensor B delivers a clean signal whose value is wrong. GM documents two strategies. On the 3.0 L LGW (2018) and a 2016 engine family the ECM estimates outside pressure from boost pressure, airflow and rpm while driving; sensor B fails if it deviates by more than 20 kPa, or 25 kPa once more than 1.24 miles have passed since the last update. With the engine stopped for over 10 s, B must sit between 50 and 115 kPa, and if MAP, boost and BARO A agree within 10 kPa while B is further away, B is singled out. Both run as Type B over 320 of 400 readings. On GM's 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine, sensor B measures ahead of the bank 2 throttle and is checked against ambient pressure for 2 s.

causes.label: Sensor B reading with offset or stuck at one value
Leak or restriction in the intake path that distorts the comparison
Boost or manifold pressure sensor fault affecting the estimate

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Usually no driveability change

P222C.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P222C.description: P222C flags a sensor B voltage that has dropped too low, as with a signal wire touching ground. GM's 2018 tables for the 3.0 L LGW set the code below 40 % of the 5 V range, equal to about 50.9 kPa, counted in 320 of 400 readings taken every 12.5 ms; it is a Type B fault with the MIL after two trips. GM's 2023-2024 tables for a twin-throttle engine use the pressure value itself: below 50 kPa for 2 s. In GM software the fault bundle for ambient pressure sensor 2 covers exactly P222C and P222D, which tells which sensor letter B refers to there. Compared with sensor A (P2228), the circuit is separate, so sensor A keeps working. P222D is the high-voltage counterpart, P222B the plausibility check.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground
5 V reference to sensor B open or shorted
Sensor B internally defective

symptoms: Check engine light
Scan tool shows a very low reading for the second barometric sensor

P222D.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P222D.description: P222D is stored when sensor B reports an excessive voltage. GM's 2018 tables for the 3.0 L LGW name contact with a supply voltage or a broken line: on that input a broken wire drives the signal up, not down. The limit is 90 % of the 5 V range, about 115 kPa, met in 320 of 400 readings; Type B, MIL after two trips. GM's 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine evaluates the raw pressure of the sensor ahead of the bank 2 throttle and fails it above 115 kPa held for 2 s. Since an open line lands here, a disconnected connector after repair work is a typical find. P222C covers the low side, P2229 the same fault on sensor A. The engine keeps running on the remaining sensors.

causes.label: Connector of sensor B unplugged or signal wire broken
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Sensor B internally defective

symptoms: Check engine light
Second barometric reading stuck near the top of its range

P222E.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P222E.description: P222E catches a sensor B signal that jitters. Outside air pressure changes slowly, so GM measures noise directly: every 12.5 ms the difference to the previous reading is taken, and the absolute differences over 80 consecutive readings are added up into a so-called string length. If that total exceeds 100 kPa, the one-second sample counts as failed; four failures in five samples set the code as Type B, MIL after two trips. GM uses this in the 2018 tables for the 3.0 L LGW and in a 2016 engine family. The fault differs from P222C/P222D, where the voltage sits steadily outside its limits, and from P222B, where a smooth signal shows the wrong value. Loose pins, chafed wires and electrical interference are the usual suspects.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminal at sensor B or the ECM
Chafed wire with intermittent contact
Electrical interference, for example from a poorly grounded component nearby

symptoms: Check engine light that may come and go
Second barometric value jumping on the scan tool

P222F.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
P222F.description: P222F is meant for engines with two barometric sensors whose readings should agree but drift apart, without the software being able to say which of the two is wrong. No maker documents this code publicly. GM, the one maker that publishes tables for a sensor B, resolves the comparison differently: it pulls in manifold and boost pressure as further references, singles out the deviating sensor and stores P222B for sensor B or P2227 for sensor A. Ford likewise uses a three-sensor vote for P2227. A pure A/B comparison has no tiebreaker, which explains why the code is rarely seen. CARB requires rationality checks of input sensors. Both sensors, their supply and any leaks in the lines feeding them should be checked.

causes.label: One of the two barometric sensors has drifted
Supply or ground offset shifting one sensor's signal
Blocked port or breather of one sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
The two barometric readings differ clearly on the scan tool

P2230.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2230.description: P2230 flags a barometric pressure (BARO) signal that is electrically present but jumps or drops out for short moments instead of sitting permanently low or high. The engine computer uses BARO for air-charge, fuelling and boost calculations. Ford's 2020-2023 gasoline OBD summary lists P2230 with P2227-P2229 among the BARO faults that inhibit auto start-stop. GM bulletins for 2014-2017 trucks and SUVs with the 5.3/6.2 L V8 and for the 2012-2013 Equinox/Terrain 2.4 L trace P2230 to engine harness wires chafed through. Exact thresholds are not published. P2228/P2229 are steady low/high signals, P2227 a plausibility fault. Drivers usually notice only the warning light; start-stop may stay off.

causes.label: Engine harness chafed against an engine component (e.g. vacuum pump pulley, cam cover)
Loose or corroded pin at the BARO sensor or ECM connector
Barometric pressure sensor with an internal contact problem

symptoms: Check engine light, often coming and going
Auto start-stop inactive
Other sensor codes stored at the same time if a shared harness is damaged

P2231.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2231.description: P2231 means the engine computer sees the heater supply of the upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 leaking into the sensor's signal path - typically an internal short in the sensor or two neighbouring wires touching in the harness. VW's 2014 specification books for the Passat and Tiguan set it when the front sensor signal changes by more than 190 microamps, i.e. the measured sensor current is distorted. CARB requires circuit faults of every fuel-control oxygen sensor to be detected. P2232/P2233 cover sensors 2 and 3 of bank 1, P2234 the first sensor of bank 2. Because the mixture feedback can no longer be trusted, the engine may run on open-loop fuelling with higher consumption and emissions.

causes.label: Internal short between heater and sensing element in the oxygen sensor
Heater and signal wires melted or chafed together (exhaust heat, routing)
Moisture or contamination bridging pins in the sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption due to open-loop fuelling
Rough idle or hesitation in some cases

P2232.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2232.description: P2232 reports that the heater supply of the oxygen sensor behind the catalyst on bank 1 is bleeding into that sensor's signal line. A switching sensor only produces up to about 1 V, so the ECM watches its signal at the instant the heater is switched off. GM's tables for the 2005 2.8/3.6 V6, the 2008 3.6 LLT and the 2024 set 24OBDG07 flag a jump of more than 2 V within 0.04 s of heater turn-off in more than 4 out of 6 events, with the MIL after two trips. The Saab 9-5 (2010, 2.0 turbo) checks whether signal and heater voltage rise and fall together and treats the fault as Type B. P2231 is the front sensor, P2235 the rear position on bank 2. Mixture control continues, but catalyst monitoring loses its rear signal.

causes.label: Internal leakage between heater and sensing element of the rear oxygen sensor
Signal and heater wires fused or chafed together near the exhaust
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Catalyst monitor not completed or catalyst code stored alongside

P2233.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2233.description: P2233 is the heater-to-signal short for sensor 3 on bank 1, a third oxygen sensor that some engines fit after a second catalyst or between two catalyst bricks. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's checks for the rear-sensor codes P2232/P2235 show how such a fault is normally caught: the signal leaps by more than 2 V within 0.04 s whenever the heater is switched off. Jaguar Land Rover's 2015 bulletin for the 3.0 supercharged V6, which carries three sensors per bank, lists many sensor 3 faults but none of this type. CARB requires circuit faults of every monitored oxygen sensor to be detected. P2236 is the bank 2 counterpart. A third sensor serves only monitoring, so the car drives normally with the warning lamp on.

causes.label: Internal leakage between heater and sensing element of sensor 3
Sensor 3 wiring melted or chafed along the exhaust or underbody
Corroded underbody connector of the third sensor

symptoms: Check engine light without noticeable driving change
Emissions inspection failed because of the stored code

P2234.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2234.description: P2234 means the heater of the front air-fuel sensor on bank 2 couples into its measuring circuit. On a wide-band sensor the disturbance is small, so the check is finer than on rear sensors. GM's 2005 tables for the Bosch-equipped 2.8/3.6 V6 look for a signal step of 0.08-0.2 V appearing no later than 0.05 s after each heater switching edge; 18 such steps in a 10 s window count as a failure, the sensor must have been fully hot for 10 s, and the MIL follows after two trips. Jaguar Land Rover lists P2234 among the bank 2 front-sensor codes of the 2014-2016 LR4, Range Rover and Range Rover Sport 3.0 V6 and blames thermal shock from water hitting the hot element; the sensor is replaced. P2231 is the same fault on bank 1. Closed-loop fuelling on bank 2 may drop out.

causes.label: Front sensor element cracked by thermal shock (water on the hot sensor)
Heater and signal wires of the bank 2 sensor touching in the harness
Moisture in the sensor connector bridging heater and signal pins

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption when bank 2 runs without lambda control
Other bank 2 front-sensor codes stored at the same time

P2235.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2235.description: P2235 concerns the post-catalyst oxygen sensor on bank 2, found on V engines with a catalyst per bank. The ECM sets it when switching off the heater makes the sensor voltage spike. GM runs the check only once the sensor is past its dew-point phase and the modelled exhaust has been above 250 °C for 90 s (and below 800 °C); the failure threshold, as for P2232, is a jump above 2 V within 0.04 s in more than 4 of 6 switch-offs. It appears in the 2005 2.8/3.6 V6 tables, the 2008 3.6 LLT tables and the 2024 set 24OBDG07, each with the MIL after two trips. Because the fault is tied to one sensor position, swapping banks is a quick plausibility check before parts are ordered. P2232 is bank 1, P2234 the front sensor of bank 2.

causes.label: Internal leakage between heater and sensing element of the bank 2 rear sensor
Sensor wires damaged by heat or chafing near the bank 2 catalyst
Water ingress in the rear sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Bank 2 catalyst monitor not completed

P2236.title: O2 Sensor Signal Circuit Shorted to Heater Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2236.description: P2236 would be set if the heater of the third oxygen sensor on bank 2 leaked into its signal wire. Such a sensor sits furthest downstream and exists only on engines with two catalyst stages per bank. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and Jaguar Land Rover's 2015 list for its V6 with sensors 3 on both banks does not use it either. The mechanism matches P2232/P2235: the heater is pulsed with battery voltage while the sensor signal stays below about 1 V, so any coupling shows up as a voltage step when the heater switches; GM uses more than 2 V within 0.04 s. CARB requires every monitored oxygen sensor circuit to be checked. P2233 is bank 1. Driving is unaffected; the lamp and a failed inspection are the consequences.

causes.label: Internal leakage between heater and sensing element of sensor 3 on bank 2
Long underbody wiring to the rear sensor chafed or heat-damaged
Road salt corrosion in the sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light with normal driving behaviour
Readiness for catalyst or oxygen sensor monitor not set

P2237.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2237.description: P2237 points to an open pump-current line (IP or APE) on the front wide-band sensor of bank 1. With that wire broken the output freezes near its stoichiometric value of roughly 1.5 V and lambda stops moving. Ford sets it on Bosch sensors when 20 s of fuel-control steps and reference-current pulses shift lambda by 0.05 or less; NTK interface chips report the open line directly. VW's 2014 books look for 1.49-1.51 V while the lambda controller deviates by more than 0.10 or fuel has been cut for over 3 s, and Saab's 9-5 2.0 turbo (2010) logs it as Type B. Software updates cure false or damaging cases on VW Jetta/Beetle 2.0 (2013-14, plus a new sensor) and Hyundai Kona 1.6 T-GDI (2024-25). P2238/P2239 are low/high, P2240 is bank 2.

causes.label: Broken pump-current wire or pushed-back pin between sensor and ECM
Pump cell of the wide-band sensor damaged, for example by catalyst-heating strategy or thermal shock
Engine software that sets the code falsely (update available for some models)

symptoms: Check engine light
Lambda reading stuck at 1.0 in live data
Higher fuel consumption in open-loop fuelling

P2238.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2238.description: P2238 is the low-side fault of the pump-current circuit of the front wide-band sensor on bank 1. Saab's 9-5 2.0 turbo (2010) shows a concrete test: on overrun with the injectors shut off, pure air should drive the signal well above its stoichiometric level, and if it stays below 1.7 V for 3 s the code sets as Type B. GM's 2005 V6 tables use the same fuel-cut check but book it under P2237. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander lists P2238 as a two-trip code. Ford does not use it at all: a pump-current wire shorted to ground lands in P0131 there. P2237 is the open circuit, P2239 the high-side fault, P2241 the same on bank 2. Typical findings are a grounded IP wire or a sensor that can no longer pump oxygen.

causes.label: Pump-current wire chafed through to ground
Aged or contaminated sensor that no longer reads lean in fuel cut-off
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Lambda value does not rise during coasting in live data

P2239.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2239.description: P2239 is the high-side counterpart for the pump-current circuit of the bank 1 front wide-band sensor. On the Saab 9-5 2.0 turbo (2010) it sets when, in closed loop with the mixture deliberately enriched, the signal still sits at 1.48-1.51 V for 1 s, meaning the sensor ignores a change it should report; it is a Type B code. GM's 2005 V6 tables check a similar window (1.48-1.52 V while target lambda lies outside 0.97-1.03) under P2237. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander also lists P2239 as a two-trip code. Ford files this wire touching battery voltage under P0132 instead. A short to the heater supply can overload the sensor interface, so the wiring deserves a check before a new sensor goes in. P2238 is low, P2242 bank 2.

causes.label: Pump-current wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Wide-band sensor with internal short or stuck output
Damaged sensor interface in the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Lambda reading frozen near 1.0 regardless of load
New sensor fails again quickly if the wiring short is not found

P223A.title: Reductant Heater E Control Circuit
P223A.description: P223A covers the control circuit of a fifth DEF heating element, heater E. Unlike heaters A to D, which each have four codes for open, performance, low and high, heater E gets only this one code, so any electrical fault of its driver or wiring ends up here. No maker documents P223A publicly. As a reference, GM's 2025 Duramax tables check comparable heater outputs by watching the low-side driver voltage and load current: a fault seen while heating forces the output off so the exact failure can be pinpointed, and heater circuits there are Type A. Which element carries the letter E depends on the system; most published SCR designs stop at three or four heaters. In frost an unheated section may stay frozen, so dosing and SCR monitoring suffer.

causes.label: Open or shorted wiring or connector of heater E
Heating element E burnt out or shorted
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

symptoms: Check engine light and SCR warning
DEF dosing delayed or blocked in freezing weather

P223B.title: Reductant Heater F Control Circuit
P223B.description: P223B reports a fault in the control circuit of heater F, the sixth heating element of an SCR system. Like its neighbour P223A for heater E, it is a single catch-all code covering open lines and shorts alike. No maker documents P223B publicly, and the published systems show why: Ford's 2023 diesel summary names heaters A to C only (with A and B checked at peak heating power for under 3 A at more than 5 V), and GM bulletin 21-NA-149 lists the heater D codes P20C5 and P20C8 for the 3.0 L LM2 Duramax. Six zones would only appear on layouts with many separately heated lines or tanks. CARB requires every emission-relevant output to be checked for circuit faults. Expect an SCR warning and, in winter, the risk of a frozen line that ends in reduced power.

causes.label: Damaged wiring or corroded connector of heater F
Heating element F open or shorted
Missing supply from the heater relay or fuse

symptoms: Check engine light and SCR warning
Reduced power warning after a cold-weather DEF fault

P223C.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P223C.description: P223C judges whether the pump current of the bank 1 wide-band sensor makes sense while the engine is coasting with fuel cut off. In that state the sensor sees almost pure air and, as Bosch's LSU 4.9 data show, must drive a clearly positive current. GM's tables (2016, 2018, 2019) start the test after 5 s of fuel cut-off and stop it at 12 s, with the reference cell above about 600 °C. Three windows count as faulty: current too large (above 5.0 mA, or 4.18 mA with the Delphi interface), close to zero (within ±0.3 or ±0.1 mA), or negative (below -0.10 mA). Each window has its own counter, e.g. 40 failures in 160 samples at 25 ms; the code is Type B. GM notes that it also catches open pump, reference-cell and reference-ground circuits. P223D is bank 2.

causes.label: Aged or poisoned wide-band sensor with wrong pump current in air
Open pump-current, reference-cell or reference-ground wire
Exhaust leak or misfire that distorts the gas at the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Usually no noticeable change in driving behaviour

P223D.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P223D.description: P223D applies the pump-current plausibility test to the front wide-band sensor of bank 2 on V engines. GM's 2016 and 2018 tables describe it for engines with a Continental interface chip: during a fuel cut-off window between 5 s and 12 s, a reading above 5.0 mA, within ±0.3 mA of zero, or below -0.10 mA is counted, and 40 hits in 160 samples in any window set the code as Type B. The test is skipped while bank 2 heater faults (P0050-P0052) or P0155 are active, because a cold element pumps poorly. The Bosch LSU 4.9 data sheet shows why the check works: pump current is zero at lambda 1, negative when rich and positive when lean, so air must give a clear positive value. P223C is the bank 1 version; P2240, P2247 and P2254 isolate open wires.

causes.label: Worn bank 2 wide-band sensor that no longer pumps correctly in air
Interrupted pump-current or reference circuit of the bank 2 sensor
Sensor heater too weak to keep the element at temperature

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Often no driveability complaint

P223E.title: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 1)
P223E.description: P223E checks the internal resistance of the reference (Nernst) cell in the bank 1 wide-band sensor. That resistance falls as the ceramic heats up, so the ECM uses it as a thermometer; Bosch specifies 300 ohms nominal for the LSU 4.9 at operating temperature. GM's tables (2016-2019) convert the value supplied by the interface chip into an element temperature and flag anything below 700 °C or above 1,000 °C in 80 % of samples (64 of 80 in 2018, 128 of 160 in 2016/2019), starting 20 s after heater warm-up; the code is Type B. GM bulletin 16-NA-266 covers 2016-2017 ATS, CTS, CT6, Camaro, Malibu and Envision with the 2.0 turbo LTG: a voltage spike inside the ECM sets P223E or P0132 and also blocks remote start, cured by reprogramming. P223F is bank 2, P0135 the heater itself.

causes.label: Aged sensor whose reference cell resistance has drifted
Heater not holding the element at temperature (heater, wiring or control)
ECM calibration fault on GM 2.0 turbo LTG (bulletin 16-NA-266)

symptoms: Check engine light after two consecutive drives
Remote start refuses to start the engine (GM LTG models)

P223F.title: O2 Sensor Reference Resistance Out Of Range (Bank 2)
P223F.description: P223F is the reference-cell resistance check for the front wide-band sensor of bank 2. GM's 2016 and 2018 tables translate the measured resistance into element temperature and count readings below 700 °C or above 1,000 °C; 64 of 80 samples (2018) or 128 of 160 (2016) at 25 ms set a Type B code. The monitor waits for heater warm-up plus 20 s and is blocked while the bank 2 heater codes P0050-P0052 or P0155 are present, so a pure heater fault shows up there first. A reading that is too cold despite a working heater points to a sensor whose ceramic has aged and become high-resistance; too hot suggests overheating, for example from misfire. Bosch's LSU 4.9 data sheet gives 300 ohms as the nominal cell resistance. P223E is bank 1, P223D the pump-current check of the same sensor.

causes.label: Bank 2 sensor ceramic aged and high-resistance
Weak heater supply or high resistance in the heater wiring
Sensor overheated by misfire or very high exhaust temperature

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Bank 2 lambda control slow to become active after a cold start

P2240.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2240.description: P2240 is the open pump-current circuit of the front wide-band sensor on bank 2, so it only exists on V engines and boxers. Ford's summaries (2012 and 2020-2023) introduced it to replace P0154; detection works as on bank 1, by lambda failing to react to reference-current pulses or by the NTK interface chip. VW's 2014 Touareg and CC books flag 1.49-1.51 V combined with a lambda controller offset above 0.07 or a controller at its limit. GM's 2005 V6 adds a fuel cut-off test (signal below 1.7 V for 2 s). FCA reflashes the PCM for P2240 on the 2025 Ram 1500 and Wagoneer with the 3.0 Hurricane (bulletins 18-071-26, 18-082/083-26), and Jaguar Land Rover lists it among the 3.0 V6 sensor faults caused by water shock.

causes.label: Open pump-current wire or loose pin at the bank 2 sensor connector
Bank 2 front sensor damaged by water or thermal shock
PCM calibration that sets the code without a hardware fault (FCA 2025 Hurricane)

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 lambda value stuck at 1.0 in live data
Higher fuel consumption

P2241.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2241.description: P2241 reports the pump-current circuit of the bank 2 front wide-band sensor at too low a level, typically a grounded wire or a sensor that cannot pump enough oxygen. No manufacturer publicly documents P2241 with thresholds. The bank 1 twin P2238 is described by Saab for its 2.0 turbo, where the signal must climb past 1.7 V on overrun with the injectors off; a V engine would run the same logic per bank. Ford instead files a grounded pump-current wire under P0151 and keeps P2240 for the open line. CARB demands that fuel-control sensors be checked for broken or shorted circuits and for implausible readings, with separate codes where practical. P2240 is the open circuit, P2242 the high-side fault on bank 2. Bank 2 fuelling falls back to open-loop values.

causes.label: Bank 2 pump-current wire shorted to ground
Aged bank 2 front sensor with weak pump cell
Fault in the ECM sensor interface for bank 2

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 2

P2242.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2242.description: P2242 flags the pump-current circuit of the bank 2 front wide-band sensor as too high, usually a short to the heater feed or battery voltage, or a signal locked at its midpoint although the mixture is being changed. No manufacturer publicly documents P2242 with thresholds. Saab describes the bank 1 version P2239 for its 2.0 turbo: 1.48-1.51 V held for 1 s while closed loop enriches the mixture. Ford's 2020-2023 summary routes any short to battery on a wide-band sensor wire to P0152 instead. CARB requires fuel-control sensors to be checked for wiring faults and implausible readings. P2240 is the open circuit, P2241 the low fault, P2239 the same fault on bank 1. Since a voltage short can kill a replacement sensor, the bank 2 harness should be checked first.

causes.label: Bank 2 pump-current wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Internal short in the bank 2 wide-band sensor
Damaged sensor interface in the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 lambda value stuck near 1.0
Replacement sensor fails again if the short remains

P2243.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2243.description: P2243 flags an open reference voltage line on the front wide-band sensor of bank 1, i.e. the Nernst-cell lead (RE/UN on Bosch sensors, VS on NTK). Ford's OBD summaries set it on Bosch parts when the sensor voltage sits above 4.7 V or below 0.2 V for 10 s; on NTK parts the interface chip reports the break itself. GM's 2005 V6 tables and the 2010 Saab 9-5 2.0 turbo use the same voltage window with cell resistance above 570 ohms, as a two-trip Type B code. On the 2004-05 Saturn Vue 3.5 V6 the pump-cell voltage must swing both above 4.8 V and below 3.4 V fifty times. Honda bulletin 14-002 ties it on 2010-11 V6 models to a broken sensor tip, often with P0420/P0430; Ford reflashes the 2020 Explorer 2.3 (20-2217). P2247 is bank 2, P2245/P2246 low/high.

causes.label: Broken reference voltage (Nernst cell) wire or pushed-back pin between sensor and ECM
Sensing element cracked or tip broken off, for example by thermal shock
Corroded or loose sensor connector
Engine software that sets the code falsely (update available for some models)

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 1
Catalyst efficiency code P0420 alongside it if a sensor fragment damaged the converter

P2244.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2244.description: P2244 stands for a plausibility fault on the reference voltage side of the bank 1 upstream wide-band sensor: the Nernst-cell signal is electrically intact and within limits, but behaves in a way that does not fit the operating state, for instance offset or too slow. No manufacturer documents P2244 publicly. Ford treats this lead only as an open circuit (P2243) and books shorts on any sensor wire under P0131/P0132; GM, Saab and VW likewise publish only the open-circuit code. Bosch specifies the Nernst cell at a nominal 300 ohms and a load of at most 250 microamps, so ageing or contamination shows up as a shifted reading. CARB requires fuel-control sensors to be checked for implausible values as well as circuit faults. P2243 is the open line, P2245/P2246 low/high, P2248 bank 2.

causes.label: Aged or contaminated wide-band sensor (oil ash, silicone, coolant)
High resistance in the reference voltage wire or connector
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor distorting the reading

symptoms: Check engine light
Slightly higher fuel consumption
Possible failed emissions test

P2245.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2245.description: P2245 reports that the reference voltage side of the upstream air-fuel sensor on bank 1 reads too low, usually because the wire touches ground or the sensor has shorted internally. GM's tables for the Saturn Vue 3.5 V6 (L66, 2004-05) define it precisely: with the engine running for over 85 s, the heater active and the element signal between 3.2 and 4.6 V, a pump-cell circuit voltage below 1.5 V for 0.5 s stores the code in the first drive cycle. Jaguar Land Rover lists P2245 among the front-sensor codes in bulletin LTB00671 (2014-16 3.0 supercharged V6), where water caused thermal shock and the sensor is renewed. GM's 2018 Duramax table 18OBDG04 counts it among faults that invalidate the front sensor signal. P2243 is the open line, P2246 high, P2249 bank 2.

causes.label: Reference voltage wire shorted to ground (chafed against exhaust or body)
Sensor element damaged internally, for example by water hitting the hot ceramic
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 1
Uneven idle or hesitation in some cases

P2246.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2246.description: P2246 means the reference voltage line of the bank 1 front wide-band sensor reads too high, typically from a short to battery or heater voltage or a short inside the sensor. No manufacturer publishes a threshold for P2246. GM's 2018 Duramax table 18OBDG04 names it, together with P2245, P2252 and P2253, as a fault that makes the front sensor signal unusable, but gives no setting criteria. Ford logs any wide-band lead that is shorted to supply voltage as P0132 and keeps P2243 for the open line, so Ford vehicles do not use this code. Bosch limits the Nernst cell to a 250 microamp load, which is why an external voltage on this wire can damage the sensor or the interface. CARB requires circuit faults of fuel-control sensors to be detected. P2245 is the low fault, P2250 bank 2.

causes.label: Reference voltage wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Internal short between heater and Nernst cell in the sensor
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption
Repeat failure of a new sensor if the wiring short remains

P2247.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2247.description: P2247 is the bank 2 version of P2243: the Nernst-cell reference line of the upstream wide-band sensor on the second cylinder bank is open. Ford's summaries trip it on Bosch sensors after 10 s outside 0.2-4.7 V and on NTK sensors via the interface chip, replacing the older P0150. VW's 2014 Touareg book names it an open Nernst-voltage circuit with limits of 0.25 and 4.80 V, while GM's 2005 V6 tables call it Type B. Field cases include Honda bulletin 14-002 (2010-11 V6 models, broken sensor tip, usually with P0430), Jaguar Land Rover LTB00671 (2014-16 3.0 supercharged V6, water shock) and a 2025 Ram 1500 3.0 engine software update (FCA 18-071-26). P2243 is bank 1, P2249/P2250 the low/high faults, P2254 the open ground line on bank 2.

causes.label: Broken reference voltage (Nernst cell) wire or loose pin on the bank 2 sensor
Cracked element or broken sensor tip after thermal shock
Engine software that sets the code falsely (update for some models)

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 2
Catalyst efficiency code P0430 if a sensor fragment damaged the converter

P2248.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2248.description: P2248 is meant for a reference voltage signal on the bank 2 upstream wide-band sensor that is present but implausible, as opposed to an open or shorted line.
