No manufacturer documents P2248 publicly, and the published diagnostic tables of Ford, GM, Saab and VW cover the bank 2 Nernst-cell line only with the open-circuit code P2247, while Ford routes shorts to P0151/P0152. A drifting reading usually stems from an aged or poisoned sensor element or extra resistance in the circuit, which Bosch's 300-ohm nominal cell value makes measurable. CARB requires upstream sensors to be monitored for out-of-range and implausible output. P2244 is the bank 1 counterpart, P2247 the open line, P2249/P2250 low/high. Mixture control on bank 2 becomes less accurate.

causes.label: Aged or contaminated wide-band sensor on bank 2
High resistance in the reference voltage wire or connector
Exhaust leak ahead of the bank 2 sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Slightly higher fuel consumption
Possible failed emissions test

P2249.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2249.description: P2249 indicates that the reference voltage circuit of the front air-fuel sensor on bank 2 is pulled too low, most often by a grounded wire in the harness or a fault inside the sensor. The only public manufacturer criteria come from GM's tables for the Saturn Vue 3.5 V6 (L66, 2004-05), a Honda-built engine: after more than 85 s of running with the sensor heater active and the element signal at 3.2-4.6 V, a pump-cell circuit voltage under 1.5 V for half a second stores the code and lights the MIL in that drive cycle. The same table uses P2245 for bank 1. Ford, VW and GM's Bosch-equipped V6 tables do not list P2249. CARB requires circuit faults of fuel-control sensors to be detected. P2247 is the open line, P2250 high, P2255 the low fault of the ground line.

causes.label: Reference voltage wire shorted to ground on the bank 2 sensor harness
Internal short in the bank 2 air-fuel sensor
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 2
Possible failed emissions test

P224A.title: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P224A.description: P224A concerns the heater of the upstream NOx sensor on bank 1, the one before the SCR catalyst. Its electrical resistance rises with temperature, so the sensor electronics use it to hold the ceramic element at working heat. The code says that resistance is outside its allowed band, pointing to an aged or damaged element or a contact problem. No maker documents P224A publicly. GM performs the same test on the 3.0 L LZ0 Duramax (2025) but reports it as P2209: the measured resistance may differ from the target by no more than 3 %, judged on 50 of 100 readings once the supply has been above 10.8 V for 45 s and the dew point was passed 180 s earlier, Type B. A sensor with this fault reads NOx unreliably; P224B is the downstream sensor.

causes.label: Heating element of the NOx sensor aged or cracked
Corroded or loose contacts in the sensor connector
Unstable supply voltage to the sensor module

symptoms: Check engine light
SCR efficiency or NOx plausibility codes may follow

P224B.title: NOx Sensor Heater Resistance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P224B.description: P224B is the heater resistance fault of the second NOx sensor on bank 1, mounted after the SCR catalyst. This sensor tells the control unit how much NOx is left after dosing, so its readings feed the catalyst efficiency monitor and the closed-loop dosing correction. If the heater's resistance leaves its expected band, the element may be running too cold or too hot. No maker documents P224B publicly. GM's 2025 tables for the 3.0 L LZ0 Duramax check the post-catalyst sensor heater against a 3 % resistance window as well, but file it under P22A7, the sensor 2 heater sense performance code, Type B. Hella describes the integrated heater as the part that keeps the sensor at operating temperature regardless of exhaust conditions. P224A is the upstream counterpart.

causes.label: Heating element of the downstream NOx sensor aged or damaged
Corrosion in the sensor connector exposed to road spray
Element cracked by water droplets hitting the hot sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
SCR efficiency monitor delayed or failing

P224C.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P224C.description: P224C points to an open or otherwise faulty control circuit of shutoff valve A, the solenoid on a CNG or LPG tank that releases gas only when the engine runs on the alternative fuel. Such valves are normally closed. GM's 2015 bi-fuel Impala (bulletin PI1330) fits a high-pressure cut-off solenoid to the tank and energizes it in CNG mode while the engine cranks or runs; Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG documentation feeds its tank valve through the inertia switch and the ALT fuel relay. Neither publishes codes for the valve. No maker documents P224C publicly, and the CNG upfitter TransEco even files an open circuit under P224E. With the valve dead, bi-fuel cars carry on with gasoline; dedicated gas vehicles may not start.

causes.label: Broken wire or unplugged connector at the tank valve
Solenoid coil of the valve open
Supply interrupted by relay or tripped inertia switch

symptoms: Check engine light
Vehicle will not switch to gas operation or falls back to gasoline

P224D.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P224D.description: P224D means tank shutoff valve A is electrically switched but the system behaves as if it stayed shut. Software can only infer that from a pressure response: once the valve is commanded open, line or rail pressure should climb toward the regulated value, which GM gives as 468-896 kPa for the bi-fuel Impala and Ford as about 724 kPa for its 2003 CNG trucks. Ford's control module also closes the tank valve itself if gas pressure sinks under 517 kPa. No maker documents P224D publicly; some code lists call it Range/Performance instead of Stuck Off. Possible reasons are a seized plunger, a closed manual tank valve or an empty tank. Bi-fuel vehicles return to gasoline, dedicated ones lose power or stall.

causes.label: Manual tank valve closed or tank nearly empty
Valve plunger stuck closed, e.g. by contamination
Supply voltage too low to pull the solenoid open
Faulty gas pressure sensor misreporting the response

symptoms: Check engine light
Engine switches back to gasoline or will not run on gas
Gas fuel gauge shows content although no gas is delivered

P224E.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
P224E.description: P224E sets when the control line of tank shutoff valve A reads too low. The DTC list of CNG upfitter TransEco Energy for its alternative fuel control module (AFCM v1.4) blames the line touching ground or being interrupted, turns on the MIL in both dedicated and bi-fuel setups and lets the system keep operating normally rather than forcing a fallback. The same list uses P2A24 and related numbers for valves B to E. Ford's own Boss 302S code list also contains P224E. On a normally closed valve such as the one on GM's bi-fuel Impala, a grounded control wire may keep the solenoid from switching as intended. P224F is the high side, P224C the general open circuit. Gas lines must stay sealed during wiring repairs.

causes.label: Control wire of the tank valve chafed through to ground
Open circuit, which some modules report under this code
Shorted solenoid coil in the valve

symptoms: Check engine light
Gas operation unavailable or interrupted

P224F.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
P224F.description: P224F reports a control circuit of tank shutoff valve A that reads too high, typically a wire touching battery voltage. In TransEco Energy's AFCM fault list the cause is given as shorted to power, the MIL is lit and the gas system keeps working under the failure mode strategy. That matters because a valve held open by an external voltage can no longer be closed by the control unit: Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG system relies on closing the tank valve when gas pressure falls below 517 kPa, and GM's bi-fuel Impala keeps its cut-off solenoids energized only while the engine turns. Ford's Boss 302S list carries P224F too, though mislabelled as Low. P224E is the low side; CARB requires both directions to be monitored.

causes.label: Control wire of the tank valve shorted to battery voltage
Output stage in the alternative fuel control module stuck on
Wiring mistake after a conversion or repair

symptoms: Check engine light
Tank valve may stay open after switching off

P2250.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2250.description: P2250 signals that the reference voltage line of the upstream wide-band sensor on bank 2 is too high, as happens with a short to the heater feed or battery voltage, or a breakdown inside the ceramic. No manufacturer documents P2250 publicly, and no bulletin in the NHTSA index names it. Ford sends any wide-band wire shorted to supply voltage to P0152 and uses P2247 only for the open line, so Ford engines never store it. Because Bosch allows the Nernst cell only a 250 microamp load, an outside voltage on this lead can ruin a replacement sensor unless the wiring is repaired first. CARB requires fuel-control sensors to be monitored for circuit faults, with distinct codes where practical. P2246 is the bank 1 counterpart, P2249 the low fault, P2247 the open circuit.

causes.label: Reference voltage wire of the bank 2 sensor shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Internal short between heater and Nernst cell
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption
Repeat failure of a new sensor if the wiring short remains

P2251.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2251.description: P2251 points to an open negative current control line, i.e. the reference or virtual ground (VM on Bosch, COM on NTK) of the bank 1 upstream wide-band sensor. Ford detects it on Bosch parts by a sensor voltage stuck in a narrow band, or by a reference-current pulse that still moves lambda; NTK chips report the break directly. GM's 2005 V6 and Saab's 2010 9-5 look for 1.47-1.53 V with cell resistance above 570 ohms and exhaust below 900 °C (Type B); VW's 2014 Passat book uses a 950-ohm limit. GM calls it low reference circuit. Bulletins: ECM reflash for the 2020-22 Corvette (22-NA-019) and 2013-14 Dart 2.4 (18-011-14), new sensor for 2016-18 Range Rover TDV6 (LTB01191) and 2025 Wrangler (23-019-25). P2254 is bank 2, P2252/P2253 low/high.

causes.label: Broken reference ground wire or pushed-back pin between sensor and ECM
Internal open circuit in the wide-band sensor
Engine software that sets the code falsely (reprogramming for some models)

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 1
Possible rough running or failed emissions test

P2252.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2252.description: P2252 means the negative current control side of the bank 1 front air-fuel sensor reads too low, typically because that line or the sensor cell is shorted to ground. GM's tables for the Honda-built 3.5 V6 in the Saturn Vue (L66, 2004-05) describe it as a sensor-cell short: once the engine has run for 85 s with the heater working and the element signal between 3.2 and 4.6 V, a sensor-cell voltage under 0.3 V for 0.5 s stores the code in the first drive cycle; P2255 is the bank 2 twin. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander service manual update lists P2252 as a two-trip code, and GM's 2018 Duramax table 18OBDG04 counts it among faults that invalidate the front sensor signal. Ford instead books such shorts as P0131. P2251 is the open line, P2253 the high fault.

causes.label: Reference ground or sensor-cell wire shorted to ground (chafed against exhaust or body)
Internal short in the air-fuel sensor
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 1
Possible hesitation or uneven running

P2253.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2253.description: P2253 reports that the negative current control side of the bank 1 upstream air-fuel sensor reads too high. On the Honda-built 3.5 V6 of the 2004-05 Saturn Vue (L66), GM's tables treat it as an open sensor-cell circuit: with the heater operating and the element signal above 4.6 V, a sensor-cell voltage over 6.0 V for 5 s sets it, and P2256 does the same on bank 2. A short to the heater or battery feed can drive the signal high in the same way. Mitsubishi lists P2253 as a two-trip code for the 2022 Outlander, and GM's 2018 Duramax table 18OBDG04 names it as a front sensor fault without giving limits. Ford logs high-side shorts on wide-band wires as P0132 instead. P2251 is the open ground line in Ford terms, P2252 the low fault.

causes.label: Open sensor-cell wire or connector contact, letting the signal float high
Wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Internal defect in the air-fuel sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 1
Repeat failure of a new sensor if a wiring short remains

P2254.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2254.description: P2254 concerns the negative current control line - also called reference ground, virtual ground or COM - of the wide-band air-fuel sensor ahead of the catalyst on bank 2. Ford's OBD summaries (2012 and 2020-2023) set it for an open line: with Bosch sensors the PCM briefly injects a reference current and flags the line if lambda barely moves, within about 10 s; with NTK sensors the interface chip reports the open line directly. VW's 2014 Passat and CC books set it when the front signal sits at 1.47-1.52 V while the cell resistance exceeds 950 ohms. P2251 is the same fault on bank 1, P2255/P2256 are low/high faults. Closed-loop mixture control on bank 2 is lost.

causes.label: Broken reference ground wire or pushed-out pin between sensor and ECM
Internal open circuit in the wide-band sensor
Corroded sensor connector with high contact resistance

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption from open-loop fuelling on bank 2
Possible rough running or failed emissions test

P2255.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2255.description: P2255 reports that the negative current control line (reference ground) of the bank 2 upstream wide-band sensor reads too low, typically a short to ground. No manufacturer publicly documents P2255 with thresholds. Ford's OBD summaries assign shorts to ground on any wide-band sensor line to P0151 and use P2254 only for an open line, and VW's 2014 specification books likewise list only P2254. The code therefore appears mainly where the sensor interface separates short-circuit faults by line. CARB requires circuit and out-of-range faults of fuel-control sensors to be detected and, where feasible, stored as separate codes. P2252 is the bank 1 counterpart, P2256 the high-side fault. Mixture control on bank 2 becomes unreliable.

causes.label: Reference ground wire shorted to ground (chafed against exhaust or body)
Internal fault in the wide-band sensor
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption
Possible hesitation or uneven running

P2256.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2256.description: P2256 means the negative current control line (reference ground) of the bank 2 upstream wide-band sensor reads too high, typically a short to battery or heater voltage. No manufacturer publicly documents P2256 with thresholds. Ford's OBD summaries send a short to battery on any wide-band sensor line to P0152 and reserve P2254 for the open line; VW's 2014 books also list only P2254 for this circuit. CARB requires fuel-control sensors to be checked for circuit continuity and out-of-range values, with separate codes where feasible. P2253 is the bank 1 counterpart, P2255 the low-side fault, P2254 the open circuit. A short to voltage can damage the sensor or the interface, so the wiring should be checked before a new sensor is fitted.

causes.label: Reference ground wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Internal short in the wide-band sensor
Fault in the sensor interface of the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Higher fuel consumption
Repeat failure of a new sensor if the wiring short remains

P2257.title: AIR System Control A Circuit Low
P2257.description: P2257 concerns the control circuit of the secondary air (AIR) pump or its relay, which blows fresh air into the exhaust during cold starts so the catalyst lights off sooner. The code sets when that circuit reads low. GM's 2018 tables (LWE section) watch the low-side driver of the AIR pump control: a resistance of 0.5 ohm or less to controller ground, detected as low voltage with the driver switched off, in 20 of 25 samples of 250 ms with at least 11 V on the powertrain relay, Type B; some controllers also log P0418. VW's 2014 specification books for the CC and Touareg flag a relay control voltage between 0 and 3.26 V. P2258 is the short to power, P0418 the open circuit. Affected cars mainly emit more during warm-up.

causes.label: Relay control wire shorted to ground
Secondary air relay with a shorted coil
Water ingress in the relay or pump connector

symptoms: Check engine light
Secondary air pump silent during cold start
Secondary air flow codes such as P0411 may follow

P2258.title: AIR System Control A Circuit High
P2258.description: P2258 reports that the line controlling secondary air (AIR) pump A or its relay sits at too high a level, usually because it is shorted to battery voltage or the driver cannot pull it down. The pump only runs briefly after a cold start to heat the catalyst faster, so the fault mainly raises warm-up emissions. GM's 2018 tables (LWE section) check it while the low-side driver is switched on: 0.5 ohm or less between signal and supply, in 20 of 25 samples of 250 ms, Type B with the MIL after two trips. VW's 2014 book for the Touareg 3.0 TSI (CGFA) gives a signal current of 0.60 to 2.40 A as criterion. Ford names P2258 beside P0412 as a secondary air fault that disables its catalyst temperature model. P2257 is the low counterpart; P2259/P2260 belong to circuit B.

causes.label: Control wire of the AIR pump relay chafed through and touching a battery-voltage feed
Secondary air relay with shorted coil or welded contacts
Moisture or corrosion in the relay or pump connector bridging terminals
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: MIL on, often without any noticeable change in driving
Secondary air pump silent after a cold start
Higher hydrocarbon emissions during warm-up, possibly a failed emissions test

P2259.title: AIR System Control B Circuit Low
P2259.description: P2259 is the low-level fault of the second secondary air control circuit, B. A second circuit exists where an engine uses two AIR pumps, two relays or a separately switched air valve; circuit A keeps its own codes P2257/P2258. A low reading usually means the control wire has contact with ground. If the relay is switched to ground by the ECM, such a short can energise it permanently, so the pump or valve keeps running after the warm-up phase and may overheat. No manufacturer publishes a threshold for circuit B; GM merely names P2259 in the keyword list of its connector-check bulletin PIP5094 for 2014 and older models. For circuit A, GM's 2018 tables judge the low-side driver over 20 of 25 samples as a Type B fault. CARB requires that secondary air systems be monitored. The engine itself runs normally.

causes.label: Control wire of circuit B chafed against the body or engine and shorted to ground
Relay or air valve B with a shorted winding
Corroded connector at relay B or the air valve

symptoms: MIL on
Secondary air pump audible for longer than usual or while warm
Blown fuse of the secondary air pump after a long run

P225A.title: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225A.description: P225A concerns the front NOx sensor of bank 1, the one ahead of the SCR catalyst. Modern NOx probes come with their own control unit that holds a sensor-specific calibration and reports finished values over CAN; this code means the stored calibration data of that unit cannot be read or fails its check. Ford's 2014 PCM code table carries P225A as a MIL code, but no manufacturer publishes the test or a threshold. Ford's 2023 diesels report memory errors inside the NOx sensor module under P2200 instead. CARB requires NOx sensor faults to be caught when the sensor can no longer serve as a feedback or monitoring input. P225B is the same fault on the downstream sensor. Usually the sensor assembly is replaced, as its memory cannot be repaired.

causes.label: Internal memory or checksum fault in the NOx sensor control unit
Replacement sensor with a part number or calibration that does not suit the vehicle
Supply voltage dropout or poor connector contact while the module was storing data
Engine or aftertreatment control unit software that misreads the sensor data

symptoms: MIL on, usually without any change in how the engine runs
SCR dosing runs without valid feedback, so NOx emissions may rise
Follow-up NOx catalyst efficiency codes possible

P225B.title: NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225B.description: P225B is stored when the control unit of the downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 cannot provide valid calibration data from its memory. That sensor sits behind the SCR catalyst and is what the engine computer uses to judge how well urea dosing reduces NOx, so a sensor without trustworthy calibration leaves the catalyst monitor blind. Ford lists P225B as a MIL code in its 2014 PCM code table; a description of the check is not public from any manufacturer. Smart NOx sensors of the Continental type keep an OEM-specific calibration in their attached module, which is why a part for another vehicle can trip such a code. P225A is the upstream counterpart, while P229E to P22A1 cover the electrical faults of this downstream sensor.

causes.label: Corrupted or unreadable calibration memory in the downstream NOx sensor module
Sensor installed with the wrong part number or an OEM calibration for another application
Moisture or corrosion at the sensor module connector disturbing its supply

symptoms: MIL on with no driveability complaint
SCR efficiency monitor does not complete or reports P20EE
Possible emissions test failure because readiness stays incomplete

P225C.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225C.description: P225C says the upstream NOx sensor of bank 1 reports more NOx than is plausible. Volvo describes its test on US17+OBD19 trucks: during engine motoring with zero fuel the engine makes no NOx, so the inlet sensor must fall below 50 ppm within about 10 s; each failure lights the MIL, which needs three clean drive cycles to go out. Volvo admitted false settings and told dealers not to replace the sensor. Mack and Volvo (KC-107) demand a NOx conversion test first; inlet and outlet should agree within 40 ppm before shutdown. Isuzu cured P225C on 2021 F-Series 5.2L trucks with a DCU update. FCA found most returned sensors from 3.0 EcoDiesel Ram and Jeep models fault-free and points to intake or EGR leaks, soot-clogged sensor ports and skewed MAF or coolant readings.

causes.label: Engine or DEF control unit software that flags the sensor too eagerly
Leak in the charge air path or an EGR valve stuck partly open
Air mass or coolant temperature signal that skews the NOx model
Upstream NOx sensor with a genuine positive offset

symptoms: MIL on, often without any noticeable driving fault
Code returns after the NOx sensor has been replaced
Higher DEF consumption or SCR efficiency codes in some cases

P225D.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P225D.description: P225D is the opposite case to P225C: the upstream NOx sensor of bank 1 reads too little NOx or refuses to rise when the engine should be producing it. Volvo and Mack list P225D among NOx codes where the sensor is very unlikely to be at fault, because the probe is simply measuring fresh air; their guide says not to replace it. FCA uses P225D on the 3.0 EcoDiesel, from 2014 Ram 1500 and Grand Cherokee flash bulletins to 2020 Ram 1500 updates, and its 2021 case file for Wrangler, Gladiator and Ram 1500 reports mostly fault-free returned sensors; it names charge air or EGR leaks, fuel contamination that soots up the sensor ports and skewed MAF or coolant inputs. A low-reading sensor hides real NOx, so SCR control and the catalyst monitor lose accuracy.

causes.label: Charge air, intake or exhaust leak that lets the sensor see diluted gas
Sensor ports clogged with soot, for example after fuel contamination
Low-pressure EGR valve partly stuck open
Outdated engine control software that a published flash corrects

symptoms: MIL on
Code persists after a new NOx sensor
Possible related intake, EGR or MAF codes

P225E.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225E.description: P225E points at the downstream NOx sensor of bank 1, behind the SCR catalyst, reading persistently high. Because that sensor sees what is left after urea dosing, a high value can be a sensor offset or genuine NOx slipping through a weak catalyst, poor DEF or a faulty dosing valve. Volvo and Mack therefore put P225E in the group where either sensor or the aftertreatment itself may be the cause: their replacement guide and bulletin KC-107 require a NOx conversion test or the aftertreatment analysis in PTT before any part is changed, and for P225E they also send technicians to the DEF dosing valve diagnosis. No public bulletin from a passenger car maker covers P225E. P225C is the same fault upstream; P225F is the low-reading downstream case.

causes.label: Real NOx slip from a weak SCR catalyst, poor DEF quality or a faulty dosing valve
Downstream NOx sensor with a positive offset
Control software that evaluates the sensor incorrectly

symptoms: MIL on, often together with P20EE
Increased DEF consumption or DEF quality warnings
Power reduction possible if SCR efficiency codes follow

P225F.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Signal Biased/Stuck Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P225F.description: P225F is set when the downstream NOx sensor of bank 1 reports less NOx than expected or does not move away from a low value. A sensor behind the SCR catalyst that reads too low makes the catalyst look better than it is, so the efficiency monitor can no longer be trusted. The only public manufacturer source is the Volvo and Mack NOx sensor replacement guide for US10 and newer trucks: it lists P225F next to P225D among codes whose description mentions the NOx sensor although the sensor is rarely the cause, notes that the probe is reading fresh air, and tells technicians not to replace it. Leaks in the exhaust ahead of the sensor and harness faults are the more likely culprits. P225D is the upstream case; P225E the high-reading counterpart.

causes.label: Exhaust leak upstream of the downstream sensor drawing in outside air
Chafed or corroded wiring between sensor module and probe
Downstream NOx sensor with reduced sensitivity

symptoms: MIL on
SCR efficiency cannot be confirmed, readiness may stay open

P2260.title: AIR System Control B Circuit High
P2260.description: P2260 flags secondary air control circuit B sitting at too high a level, as with a short to the supply or a driver output that cannot switch. Circuit B drives the second pump, second relay or a separate air valve, depending on the engine. Where the ECM grounds the relay to switch it, a short to power means the relay can never pull in: pump or valve B stays idle, and the catalyst on that side heats up more slowly after a cold start. No manufacturer documents its threshold for circuit B; GM only lists P2260 among the codes in its connector bulletin PIP5094 (2014 and older). For circuit A, GM's 2018 tables treat 0.5 ohm or less between signal and supply, with the driver on, as a Type B fault, which shows the type of check involved. P2259 is the low-level counterpart, P2258 the same fault on circuit A.

causes.label: Control wire of circuit B shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Relay or air valve B with an open coil, depending on how the driver is diagnosed
Output stage for circuit B in the engine control module defective

symptoms: MIL on
Second secondary air pump or valve does not operate after a cold start
Increased cold-start emissions, possibly with a secondary air flow code on one bank

P2261.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A - Mechanical
P2261.description: P2261 means bypass valve A of the turbocharger or supercharger, also called the recirculation valve, does not work mechanically. When the throttle snaps shut it should let charge air flow back to the compressor inlet so the compressor does not surge. GM's 2018 tables look for a valve stuck closed in coast-down: with the valve commanded open and at least 1,200 rpm, a high-pass filtered airflow signal above 30 g/s or a filtered boost slope above 500 kPa/s reveals surge; 8 failures in 10 tests give a Type B fault. GM bulletin 16-NA-020 (2016 Encore/Malibu 1.4/1.5 L) blames a sticking valve, 23-NA-033 (2023 Equinox/Terrain) an ECM whose short-circuit detection reacted to back voltage, and Kia campaign SC230 (2022 Seltos 1.6 T-GDI) a kinked recirculation hose. A flutter or rattle on lift-off is typical.

causes.label: Bypass/recirculation valve sticking closed or with a torn diaphragm
Kinked, collapsed or wrongly routed recirculation or control hose
Electrical fault at the valve solenoid or its connector that prevents opening
Engine control module output reacting wrongly (software or hardware)

symptoms: Fluttering, chuffing or rattling noise from the turbo when lifting off the throttle
MIL on
Slightly delayed boost after gear changes

P2262.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Pressure A Not Detected - Mechanical
P2262.description: P2262 says boost pressure A does not appear at all although the charging system should be producing it, and the cause appears to be mechanical rather than a sensor fault. The control unit sees the pressure after the compressor stay near ambient or close to manifold pressure. VW's 2014 book for the supercharged Touareg 3.0 TSI uses the ratio of boost to manifold pressure and flags it below a band of 1 to 1.25. Volvo technical journal 31319 (2016 four-cylinder B4204T23) traced P2262 together with P02CD to a fresh-air hose that had slipped off the air filter housing at the MAF; a spring clamp prevents a repeat. Unlike P0299, which measures a shortfall against the target, P2262 stands for boost missing altogether; P2263 rates overall control performance and P226B the opposite extreme. Acceleration feels flat, and many engines limit torque.

causes.label: Intake or charge-air hose disconnected or split, so the compressor cannot build pressure
Wastegate or bypass stuck open, corroded or with a broken linkage
Damaged turbocharger or supercharger (bearing wear, broken drive, wheel damage)
Boost pressure sensor or its hose blocked or detached

symptoms: Clear loss of power, no turbo or supercharger pull
MIL on, often with a reduced-power mode
Hissing or whistling from the intake if a hose has come off

P2263.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Boost System Performance
P2263.description: P2263 means boost pressure measured in the intake manifold stays too far from the target set by the closed-loop boost control. CARB requires diesel OBD to detect underboost, overboost and slow response of the boost control. On the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel the allowed underboost deviation runs from 35 to 85 kPa with injection quantity and speed, and the code sets as Type A once the condition holds for 15 s; GM's 2018 diesels need 400 failures in 500 samples and name leaks after the compressor or in the manifolds, and exhaust obstructions, as targets. Ford's 2023 diesels count deviations above 35 kPa at 1500 rpm or more, typically over 100 s. The Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) waits for more than 200 s out of range and stores it as Type C. GM's Cruze bulletin found a charge-air cooler duct pulled off the throttle body, with P0299, P2002 and P2463 alongside. The engine usually limits torque.

causes.label: Charge-air hose or cooler duct leaking or pulled off
Variable-geometry vanes or actuator sticking
Restricted exhaust, for example a heavily loaded particulate filter
Boost pressure sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Power loss or limp mode
Hissing or whistling from the charge-air system
Black smoke under load

P2264.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit
P2264.description: P2264 is the general circuit code for water-in-fuel sensor A, the probe in the diesel filter or separator that detects water by its conductivity. GM's 2018 diesel tables explain a neat self-test: after the ignition has been off for more than about 8 h, a healthy sensor briefly signals water during the first 0.3 to 1.8 s after power-up. If that pulse is missing in 10 of 14 samples of 100 ms, P2264 sets as a Type C code that turns on the Service Vehicle Soon lamp rather than the MIL; versions exist for sensors wired to the ECM and to the fuel tank zone module. Ford's 2014 PCM table also lists the code. With the circuit faulty, the warning for real water no longer works, so the separator should be drained by hand until it is fixed. P2265 to P2268 split the fault further.

causes.label: Water-in-fuel sensor that no longer performs its power-up self-test
Corroded or loose connector at the filter housing, exposed to road spray
Open or damaged wire between sensor and ECM or tank zone module
Incompatible sensor fitted during a filter change

symptoms: Service lamp or message on, engine runs normally
No warning if water actually collects in the separator

P2265.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2265.description: P2265 means the signal from water-in-fuel sensor A is electrically present but does not behave plausibly, for example a self-test response that comes at the wrong time or a value that sits between the expected dry and wet states. No manufacturer documents P2265 publicly. A comparable check appears in GM's 2018 diesel tables under P2264: after a long ignition-off period the sensor has to signal water for a short moment right after power-up, and a missing response is judged as a fault. The probes measure conductivity between two electrodes in the water sump of the filter, so a film of dirt, biodiesel residue or a partly corroded probe can push the reading into an implausible zone. The code usually lights only a service or water warning; draining and cleaning come before replacing parts.

causes.label: Sludge, emulsion or deposits coating the sensor electrodes
Sensor electronics drifting so the output lies between dry and wet
Corroded terminals adding resistance to the signal circuit

symptoms: Water warning or service lamp that comes and goes
Water warning stays on even after the filter has been drained

P2266.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Low
P2266.description: P2266 is set when the signal line of water-in-fuel sensor A stays below its valid range, typical of a grounded signal wire or of a conductive path that should not be there. Ford documents the code on 2017 and 2018 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7L diesel built up to 15 March 2018: bulletin 18-2133 links P2266, P2269 and P1140 with a lit water-in-fuel lamp to water entering connector C3080 at the sensor, which sits between tank and frame rail. The procedure checks the sensor across pins 1 and 2 for 795 to 815 kOhm, replaces it if out of range, then dries and wraps the connector. As water itself conducts, a wet plug can fake both a low circuit and a water alarm. P2267 is the high side, P2264 the general circuit code.

causes.label: Water intrusion into the sensor connector bridging signal and ground
Sensor with internal resistance outside specification
Signal wire chafed against the frame and shorted to ground

symptoms: Water-in-fuel lamp on although no water is in the separator
Often stored together with P2269

P2267.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit High
P2267.description: P2267 reports that the signal of water-in-fuel sensor A sits above its valid range, which usually indicates an open signal or ground path, a disconnected sensor or a short to a voltage source. Stellantis has a case file for 2025 and 2026 Ram 2500 to 5500 trucks with the Cummins 6.7L: after the fuel filter module has been drained, the warning lamp may stay on with P2267 and P2269. Instead of replacing parts, technicians drain both filter stages, remove the sensor, wipe residue off its probes, refit it at 3 Nm and prime the system with the lift pump. That points to the sensor reacting to leftover contamination as well as to wiring. P2266 is the low-side counterpart, P2268 the intermittent version.

causes.label: Residual contamination on the probes after draining the filter
Unplugged sensor or open signal or ground wire
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage
Defective water-in-fuel sensor

symptoms: Water-in-fuel lamp stays on after draining
Often appears together with P2269

P2268.title: Water in Fuel Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2268.description: P2268 is reserved for a water-in-fuel sensor A circuit whose signal drops out or jumps for short moments instead of staying at a fault level. No manufacturer documents P2268 publicly. The neighbouring codes show where such faults arise on real trucks: Ford traced P2266 on 6.7L Super Duty models to water entering the sensor connector, and Stellantis linked P2267 on Cummins Ram trucks to residue on the probes after draining. Both effects can come and go with temperature, vibration or fuel sloshing in the filter, which is the typical picture of an intermittent circuit. The sensor itself is a simple pair of electrodes, so the search starts at connector, terminals and harness clips. P2266 and P2267 are the steady low and high faults.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at the filter housing losing contact under vibration
Wire chafing intermittently near the frame or filter bracket
Moisture in the plug that changes with temperature and spray

symptoms: Water warning flickers or appears briefly while driving
Code stored as history with no fault present at the workshop

P2269.title: Water in Fuel Condition - Sensor A
P2269.description: P2269 is not a wiring fault but a statement about the fuel: sensor A has detected water. On diesels it means the separator is full; Ram's 2025-26 Cummins 6.7L trucks set it with the MIL, and Stellantis traced a persistent case to incomplete draining, fixed by draining and swapping the sensor's signal and ground pins (TSB 14-004-26). Ford tied P2269 on 2017-18 Super Duty 6.7L trucks to water in connector C3080 and, in other bulletins, to PCM software. GM uses P2269 on flex-fuel petrol engines: if the flex fuel sensor's frequency exceeds 185 Hz in 50 of 63 samples, the fuel's conductivity points to water; Type B in 2018, Type A in 2025. Drain or replace contaminated fuel promptly; water damages injection pumps.

causes.label: Water separator full and not drained at the service interval
Fuel from the tank or filling station containing water
Residual water after draining or a wet sensor connector faking the alarm
Engine control software needing an update

symptoms: Water-in-fuel lamp or message, on some vehicles also the MIL
Rough running, power loss or hard starting if water reaches the injection system
Reduced power on some engines to protect the injection system

P226A.title: Water in Fuel Lamp Control Circuit
P226A.description: P226A concerns the output that switches the water-in-fuel warning lamp, not the sensor. The control unit drives the lamp circuit and checks it electrically; an open lamp, a broken wire or a shorted driver lets it set this code. No manufacturer documents P226A publicly, and on current vehicles the cluster usually receives the warning as a bus message, so a discrete lamp line that could fail is found mainly on older or commercial diesels. The practical risk is that the driver is no longer warned when the separator fills, while the sensor itself keeps working and P2269 can still be stored. CARB treats the warning lamp as part of the driver information, not as an emission input, so this code normally does not turn on the MIL. Check bulb, socket, wiring and driver output.

causes.label: Burnt-out warning lamp or corroded lamp socket
Open or shorted wire between control unit and lamp
Faulty lamp driver in the control unit

symptoms: Water-in-fuel lamp does not light during the bulb check at ignition on
Lamp stays on permanently regardless of the filter state

P226B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Boost Pressure Too High - Mechanical
P226B.description: P226B reports boost from turbocharger or supercharger A rising too high for a mechanical reason, for instance a wastegate or bypass that will not open or a seized actuator linkage, rather than a sensor or wiring fault. VW's 2014 book for the supercharged Touareg 3.0 TSI sets it when boost passes 250 kPa. GM uses the code only for European calibrations: its 2018 diesel tables list P226B as an EOBD code in the boost-system fault groups, while the US software maps the same fault group to P2263. CARB requires boosted engines to detect overboost. Where P0234 judges a deviation above the target, P226B points to a mechanical cause; P2262 describes boost that does not appear at all. To protect the engine the ECM usually reduces torque, and some engines open a relief path.

causes.label: Wastegate flap seized closed by corrosion or carbon
Seized or misadjusted wastegate or VGT actuator linkage
Vacuum or pressure line to a pneumatic actuator leaking or blocked
Supercharger bypass valve not opening

symptoms: Sudden power cut or reduced-power mode under load
MIL on
Unusually strong surge of power just before the cut

P226C.title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Slow Response
P226C.description: P226C means the boost control actuator of turbocharger A does move, but too slowly, so boost lags behind changes in demand. Ford's 2023 diesel summary runs an intrusive check on the 3.0 L and 1.5 L at idle, once in each drive cycle: the variable vanes travel from closed to open, and within 7 s manifold pressure must change by at least 6.5 kPa at sea level (3.5 kPa at 8,000 ft). Mitsubishi's 2022 Eclipse Cross 1.5 turbo sets it when the wastegate angle stays more than 20 % off target for 5 s and then limits torque. FCA changed P226C on the 2014 Ram 6.7 L Cummins so that the MIL needs two trips instead of one; FCA case S2018000009 (Jeep) blames varnish in the VGT housing, Nissan NTB20-071 (Titan XD 5.0 diesel) a binding turbine control valve. P226F is the B side.

causes.label: Variable vanes or turbine control valve sluggish from soot, varnish or corrosion
Worn electric or pneumatic boost actuator, or a weak control solenoid
Damaged wiring or connector between actuator and control module
Control module software that needs an update (cold-weather false sets)

symptoms: Hesitant pull from low engine speed, turbo lag
MIL on, sometimes with a torque limit
More smoke on acceleration with diesel engines

P226D.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 1)
P226D.description: P226D means the bank 1 particulate filter offers so little flow resistance that its core is likely broken, burnt out or removed. CARB requires detection of a destroyed or missing substrate, or a filter replaced by a pipe. GM's diesel tables test the filtered resistance of the DPF during soot loading above 500 rpm and 10 l/s exhaust flow: 5 failures in 10 samples (2018) or 20 in 30 below 0.01 kPa per l/s (2025), Type A. GM adds that a loose or blocked pressure-sensor pipe gives the same result; PIP5664 and an ECM update dealt with false P226D on 2020 6.6L L5P trucks, as did Mack and Volvo for 2015-16 MP engines. Ford also uses P226D for petrol particulate filters (2024-25: normalised back pressure below 1.0 for 5 s); 2025 Maverick and Bronco Sport 2.0L had the wrong pressure sensor fitted.

causes.label: Filter core cracked, melted after an overheated regeneration, or removed
Differential pressure line disconnected, cracked, blocked or routed wrongly
Control software that sets the code without a hardware fault
Incorrect or faulty differential pressure sensor assembly

symptoms: MIL on
Visible soot at the tailpipe if the filter core is damaged
Often no driveability change; regeneration behaviour may be affected

P226E.title: Particulate Filter Deteriorated/Missing Substrate (Bank 2)
P226E.description: P226E reports a damaged or missing particulate filter core on bank 2, which only exists where each cylinder bank has its own filter. Ford documents it in its 2024-2025 OBD summary for petrol engines: the gasoline particulate filter check runs once the filter has been above 250 °C for 30 s and exhaust flow lies between 300 and 850 m³/h; if the lowest measured back pressure stays below the missing-brick threshold, a ratio under 1.0, for 5 s, P226E is stored for bank 2 and P226D for bank 1, with Mode 6 results under monitor ID $B3. No public bulletin covers P226E. CARB's missing-substrate rule for diesels follows the same idea. A pressure line problem can mimic a missing core, so check lines and sensor before condemning the filter.

causes.label: Bank 2 filter core cracked, melted or removed
Pressure sensing line of bank 2 loose, cracked or blocked
Back pressure sensor reading too low

symptoms: MIL on
Usually no noticeable change in driving behaviour

P226F.title: Turbocharger Boost Control B Slow Response
P226F.description: P226F is the slow-response fault of boost control B, meaning the actuator of a second turbocharger or of the second stage on twin-turbo, bi-turbo or sequential layouts. Which unit the letter B denotes is up to the manufacturer. The monitoring principle mirrors P226C: the control unit commands a change in vane or wastegate position and expects boost or manifold pressure to follow within a set time. No manufacturer documents P226F publicly. For the A side, Ford's 2023 diesel summary describes an idle test that sweeps the vanes and demands a pressure change within 7 s, and CARB requires diesel engines to detect slow boost response. Likely causes are a sluggish actuator, carbon or varnish in the B turbine housing, or a vacuum or wiring problem on that side. Boost builds hesitantly and the ECM may limit power.

causes.label: Boost actuator of turbocharger B sluggish or worn
Carbon or varnish restricting vanes or flap on turbocharger B
Leaking vacuum line or damaged wiring to actuator B

symptoms: Delayed boost in the speed range where the second charger takes over
MIL on, possibly with reduced power

P2270.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2270.description: P2270 concerns the oxygen sensor behind the catalyst on bank 1. When the mixture turns rich, this sensor should rise to a high voltage; if it stays low, the ECM treats it as biased or stuck lean and can no longer rely on it for catalyst monitoring or the post-catalyst trim. GM's 2018 four-cylinders add fuel during a coast-down and set the code if the signal is still under 760 mV once 55 g of air have passed (Type B, two trips); Ford fails a sensor whose highest voltage stays under 0.42 V. P2096 reports the trim correction, P0136 a sensor without activity. Documented triggers include oil on the sensor (Honda Pilot 2023 to 2025), an oil-soaked connector (Mazda CX-9), a bent terminal (GM 2013 trucks) and ECM software (Subaru WRX 2015 to 2016, Forester turbo).

causes.label: Rear oxygen sensor aged, contaminated or slow to reach rich voltage
Exhaust leak ahead of the rear sensor diluting the gas with air
Oil in the sensor connector or a bent terminal
Calibration issue fixed by an ECM update

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Catalyst and oxygen sensor readiness not completing
Usually no noticeable change in driveability

P2271.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P2271.description: P2271 is the opposite fault of the same bank 1 rear sensor: its voltage refuses to fall when the exhaust should be lean. It is usually checked during a deceleration fuel cut, when almost pure air passes the sensor. GM's 2018 four-cylinders set it if the signal is still above 100 mV after 25 g of air in fuel cut-off (Type B); GM's Bosch-based 2005 V6 looks for a reading above 0.2 V four seconds into the cut, VW's 2014 data books for CC and Tiguan use 0.15 V after 3000 mg of oxygen, and Ford added a fuel-cut stuck test from model year 2019. Causes are a sensor poisoned by coolant, oil or silicone, a signal wire touching voltage, or a front sensor misleading the ECM; Honda traced this on the 2007 to 2008 Acura TSX and replaced both sensors. P2097 and P0138 cover trim and circuit.

causes.label: Rear oxygen sensor contaminated by coolant, oil or silicone
Faulty front A/F sensor making the rear sensor look stuck rich
Signal wire chafed against a voltage source

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Catalyst monitor not completing

P2272.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2272.description: P2272 applies to V and flat engines with a separate catalyst and rear oxygen sensor on bank 2; that sensor fails to reach a rich reading when the ECM enriches bank 2. GM's 2016 tables (16OBDG05) set it if the voltage is still under 800 mV after 68 g of air during forced enrichment (Type B). GM's Bosch-based 2005 2.8 and 3.6 V6 first wait for 100 s below about 0.58 to 0.66 V, then ramp up the fuel and fail the sensor if it has not risen 10 s after the enrichment limit. Ford uses the same 0.42 V limit as on bank 1. Mazda found oil from a leaking oil pressure switch inside connector C-34 on the 2007 to 2015 CX-9, stored with P2A04, and fixed it with a new switch and a cleaned connector. If only bank 2 reports a fault, comparing its data with bank 1 narrows it down.

causes.label: Bank 2 rear oxygen sensor aged or contaminated
Engine oil in the sensor connector, for example from a leaking oil pressure switch
Exhaust leak on bank 2 ahead of the rear sensor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Catalyst monitor for bank 2 not completing

P2273.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P2273.description: P2273 means the rear oxygen sensor of bank 2 keeps a high voltage when the exhaust of that bank should be lean. GM's 2016 tables (16OBDG05) check this in fuel cut-off and set the code if the signal is above 100 mV after 9 g of air (Type B); GM's 2024 tables (24OBDG07) compare the lowest voltage during a commanded lean phase with 0.20 V over two trips. The Bosch-based 2005 GM V6 leans the bank after a long high-voltage phase and also fails the sensor above 0.202 V four seconds into a fuel cut. Ford treats bank 2 like bank 1 and uses fuel-cut events from model year 2019. Typical causes are a sensor fouled by oil or coolant on that side or a signal wire touching a supply line. P2099 is the post-catalyst trim of bank 2 at its rich limit; P0158 a voltage above the normal range.

causes.label: Bank 2 rear oxygen sensor fouled by oil or coolant
Signal wire touching a supply or heater line
Bank 2 front sensor misreading so that the bank actually runs rich

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Catalyst monitor for bank 2 not completing

P2274.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
P2274.description: Sensor 3 exists only where a bank has a third oxygen sensor, usually behind a second catalyst, so that sensor 2 sits between two bricks. P2274 says this last sensor on bank 1 stays lean when it should swing rich. VW's 2014 data books for the CC, Passat and Tiguan 2.0 TSI define it as a rear signal that does not oscillate and stays under about 0.62 to 0.65 V even after the ECM enriches the mixture by 27.9 %. Jaguar Land Rover lists P2274 with the bank 1 post-catalyst sensor codes of the 2014 to 2016 3.0 supercharged V6, blames thermal shock from water on the hot ceramic and fits a new sensor. CARB requires every secondary sensor to be checked for adequate output. P2270 is the same fault one position forward; P0142 and P0146 cover circuit faults and missing activity of sensor 3.

causes.label: Third oxygen sensor aged or cracked by thermal shock from water
Exhaust leak ahead of sensor 3 drawing in air
Damaged wiring or connector of sensor 3

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No noticeable change in driveability

P2275.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
P2275.description: P2275 is the rich-side fault of the third oxygen sensor on bank 1, the last one on systems with two catalysts in series: it keeps a high voltage while the exhaust should be lean. VW's 2014 data books for the CC, Passat and Tiguan check it in fuel cut-off, comparing the voltage with 0.15 V once 4500 mg of oxygen have passed, more than the 3000 mg used for sensor 2 because the extra catalyst stores oxygen first. Jaguar Land Rover includes P2275 among the bank 1 post-catalyst sensor codes of its 2014 to 2016 3.0 supercharged V6 and replaces water-damaged sensors. Fouling by oil, coolant or sealant and a signal wire touching voltage are other plausible causes. P2271 is the same fault at sensor 2; P0144 reports a voltage above the valid range rather than a stuck reading.

causes.label: Third oxygen sensor contaminated or damaged by water
Signal wire of sensor 3 touching a voltage source

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No noticeable change in driveability

P2276.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 2, Sensor 3)
P2276.description: P2276 needs three oxygen sensors on bank 2, so it only occurs on V or flat engines whose second bank carries a front, a mid-catalyst and a post-catalyst sensor. It reports that the post-catalyst sensor of bank 2 does not reach a rich reading. No manufacturer publishes a threshold for this exact code; Jaguar Land Rover lists it, with P2277 and the heater and circuit codes of that sensor, for the 2014 to 2016 3.0 supercharged V6 in the LR4, Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, where water on the hot element cracked the sensor. Ford's monitor runs the same switch-point test on sensors 2 and 3 and fails a rich peak below 0.42 V. CARB requires secondary sensors to be checked for sufficient output. If bank 1 is fault-free, compare both third sensors and look for an exhaust leak on bank 2.

causes.label: Bank 2 third oxygen sensor aged or cracked by water
Exhaust leak on bank 2 ahead of sensor 3
Damaged wiring or connector of sensor 3

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No noticeable change in driveability

P2277.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 3)
P2277.description: P2277 is the rich-side counterpart of P2276: the third, post-catalyst sensor on bank 2 does not drop to a lean reading. On such layouts the check normally runs during a fuel cut, when the second catalyst must fill with oxygen before the sensor can respond, so a slow or fouled element shows up here. No manufacturer publishes a threshold for P2277 itself; Jaguar Land Rover lists it among the bank 2 post-catalyst sensor codes of the 2014 to 2016 3.0 supercharged V6 and replaces water-damaged sensors. For reference, VW tests the bank 1 twin P2275 against 0.15 V after 4500 mg of oxygen, and Ford fails a sensor whose lean peak never drops below 0.48 V. A shorted signal wire or oil and coolant fouling are further causes. P2273 is the fault at sensor 2; P0164 a voltage above range.

causes.label: Bank 2 third oxygen sensor contaminated or water-damaged
Signal wire of sensor 3 touching a voltage source

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No noticeable change in driveability

P2278.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 3/Bank 2 Sensor 3
P2278.description: P2278 reports that the third oxygen sensors of the two banks are connected the wrong way round, so the ECM reads the bank 1 sensor as if it sat on bank 2 and vice versa. The check changes the exhaust of one bank only, for example by cutting its injectors or feeding air into one exhaust line, and watches which sensor answers. A DaimlerChrysler patent describes this test and the risk for control sensors: crossed sensors push one bank leaner and the other richer until both controllers hit their limits. At the third position the effect is milder, since these sensors mainly watch the catalysts, but faults would be blamed on the wrong bank. No manufacturer documents a test for this code publicly; CARB requires usable secondary sensor output. The usual cause is crossed connectors after repairs.

causes.label: Sensor 3 connectors of both banks plugged in crosswise after a repair
Harness routed to the wrong side or pins swapped in a connector
Wrong harness, ECM or calibration after a replacement

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Catalyst or sensor codes reported for the wrong bank

P2279.title: Intake Air System Leak (Bank 1)
P2279.description: P2279 means the ECM has concluded that air enters the engine without being measured or expected, for example because the air mass sensor, manifold pressure and throttle position no longer agree with its air model. Volkswagen and Audi use it widely. On the 2013 to 2016 Audi A6, A7 and A8 4.0 TFSI, a leaking pressure-regulating valve in the crankcase breather module set P2279 with P0507 and a metallic whistle at warm idle; a fabric-reinforced membrane fixed it. On 2.0 TFSI engines (BPY, CCTA and others) a check valve that did not seal under boost let pressure into the crankcase, logging P2279, P2187 and P1297 with oil leaking at the filler cap. For the 2.5 litre five-cylinder Volkswagen advises checking cam timing first, since a timing offset changes the air the engine draws. Diesels set it too: the Mercedes OM651 2.2 in the international Jeep Compass and Patriot logged it with limp mode and got a new air filter and software.

causes.label: Leaking crankcase breather or PCV pressure-regulating valve
Leak at intake manifold, hoses or seals after the air mass sensor
Camshaft timing offset
ECM calibration needing an update

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Whistling at idle, unstable or high idle speed
Limp mode on some engines

P227A.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit
P227A.description: P227A is the general circuit fault of barometric pressure sensor C, used when the control unit finds the signal missing or unusable without classifying it as too low or too high. Sensor C is not necessarily a separate ambient sensor: in GM's 2018 diesel tables the BARO C channel belongs to the turbocharger inlet pressure sensor, GM also uses it on the supercharged 6.2 L LT4, and on its 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine it reads pressure ahead of a throttle. No manufacturer documents P227A itself publicly; GM divides circuit monitoring of sensor C into P227C (low), P227D (high) and P227E (erratic). The matching general codes for sensors A and B are P2226 and P222A. With a substitute value the engine keeps running, but altitude and boost corrections lose accuracy.

causes.label: Loose connector, corroded pins or damaged wiring at sensor C
Sensor C itself failed
5 V reference or sensor ground shared with other sensors disturbed

symptoms: MIL on
Usually no noticeable change in driving; slight power loss at altitude possible

P227B.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P227B.description: P227B means sensor C supplies an electrically sound signal that does not agree with the other pressure readings. In GM's 2018 diesel tables sensor C is the turbocharger inlet pressure sensor: the ECM compares it with BARO and MAP at idle and in the window between key-off and the next start, and if only sensor C is out of line it gets the blame, as a Type B fault after 320 failures in 400 samples. With the engine stopped a reading below 50 or above 115 kPa also fails. On GM's 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine the pressure ahead of a throttle is checked against ambient pressure while running and while stopped, with 2 kPa tolerance plus allowances for modelled air-filter loss; the code sets after 2 s within one trip. P227C to P227E cover electrical faults of the same sensor.

causes.label: Sensor C drifting or with an offset
Sensor port blocked by dirt, oil or ice, or sensor not seated in its bore
Heavily clogged air filter shifting the pressure ahead of the compressor or throttle

symptoms: MIL on
Mostly no driveability change; occasionally reduced boost

P227C.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
P227C.description: P227C flags a voltage from pressure sensor C that is too low. GM's 2018 tables show two variants. On the diesel, where sensor C measures turbocharger inlet pressure and the input has a pull-up, only a short to ground pulls it below 39.4 % of 5 V (about 50.2 kPa); 320 failures in 400 samples make it a Type B fault. On the supercharged 6.2 L LT4 the limit is 40 % (50.9 kPa), and both a grounded and an open line count, as Type A with the MIL on the first trip. GM's 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine looks at the pressure value: below 50 kPa for 2 s, two trips. GM bulletin 22-NA-188 (1.3 L L3T and 2.0 L LSY turbo) links P227C after an ECM replacement to a redesigned MAF sensor that requires the matching calibration. P227D is the high counterpart.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground
Open signal or 5 V supply line on inputs that read an open circuit as low
Replacement control module without the calibration that matches the fitted sensor
Sensor C internally defective

symptoms: MIL on, on some engines immediately
Engine runs on a substitute value, at most slightly less power

P227D.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit High
P227D.description: P227D is the high-voltage counterpart of P227C. On GM's 2018 diesel the sensor C input has a pull-up, so both a short to the supply and a broken signal wire push it above 90.2 % of 5 V (about 115.4 kPa); after 320 failures in 400 samples it is a Type B fault. The supercharged LT4 uses 90 % (115 kPa) and attributes the code only to a short to power, here as Type A with the MIL on the first trip, because its input reads an open line as low. GM's 2023-2024 twin-throttle engine flags a reading above 115 kPa held for 2 s over two trips. Since the atmosphere cannot produce such a value at the sensor positions concerned, the ECM switches to a substitute, and corrections for altitude or boost become less exact.

causes.label: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Broken signal wire or sensor ground on inputs with pull-up
Sensor C internally defective

symptoms: MIL on
Little change in driving; possibly reduced boost or poorer altitude compensation

P227E.title: Barometric Pressure Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P227E.description: P227E covers a sensor C signal that jumps although every single value is in range. GM measures this as a string length: the absolute difference between each reading and the one taken 12.5 ms earlier is summed over 80 consecutive readings, and a sum above 152 kPa (2018 diesel) or 150 kPa (supercharged LT4) counts as a failure. Four failures in five one-second samples set the code, as Type B with two trips on the diesel and as Type A on the LT4. Loose terminals, chafed insulation, a cracked sensor housing or interference from nearby actuators are typical triggers. P227C and P227D catch steady shorts, P227B values that are smooth but wrong. The engine normally keeps running on a substitute pressure.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminals in the sensor C connector
Chafed wiring with intermittent contact
Interference from ignition or actuator wiring routed nearby
Sensor C with an unstable internal element

symptoms: MIL on, possibly coming and going
Occasional brief hesitation or uneven boost

P227F.title: Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 2)
P227F.description: P227F means the passage between the air filter and the mass air flow sensor of bank 2 is restricted or lets air in that has bypassed the filter. By today's wording the code belongs to engines with a separate air path and MAF per bank; P2280 is the bank 1 version. FCA nevertheless sets P227F on Ram 2500 and 5500 heavy-duty trucks: STAR case S2218000013 (2022) reports it together with a prompt to service the air filter, sometimes alongside P0299 or P226C, on vehicles below 3,000 miles. The reason was factory filters whose paper media carried too much oil; a fresh filter is the first step. On the same trucks FCA treats the bank 1 sibling P2280 as a two-trip fault. A restricted filter starves the engine of air, so boost and power fall, and diesels may smoke more.

causes.label: Air filter clogged with dust or soaked with too much oil
Intake opening blocked by snow, leaves or a collapsed duct
Loose clamp or cracked duct between filter box and MAF on bank 2
Faulty filter restriction or inlet pressure sensor

symptoms: MIL on, on some trucks with an air filter service message
Reduced power and boost under load
More black smoke on diesel engines

P2280.title: Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 1)
P2280.description: P2280 is the bank 1 code for restricted airflow or an air leak between the air filter and the MAF sensor. A blocked filter lowers the pressure ahead of the sensor and limits the air the engine can take in. A leak in this section matters less for fuel metering, since the air still passes the MAF, but it lets unfiltered air and dust reach the engine. FCA's heavy-duty Ram trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins diesel are the documented users: with 2016 software, bulletin 18-027-16 made P2280 wait for two trips instead of one before the MIL, and FCA tech tip 9003821 (2017) notes MIL events where oil-soaked intake filters were being replaced. FCA's older wording names the code without a bank. P227F is the bank 2 counterpart, P2281 covers the stretch from the MAF to the throttle.

causes.label: Air filter clogged or soaked with oil
Snow, ice or debris in the air inlet, or a collapsed intake duct
Cracked duct or loose clamp between filter box and MAF
Early software that flags the condition too readily

symptoms: MIL on
Less power and slower boost build-up under load
More smoke from diesel engines when accelerating

P2281.title: Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
P2281.description: P2281 points to air that escapes or enters between the MAF sensor and the throttle body, so the airflow the sensor reports no longer matches what reaches the cylinders. On turbocharged engines this section includes the compressor, the charge air cooler and their hoses: a loose clamp or split boot can blow off charge air under boost or draw in unmeasured air at idle. FCA is the documented user: across 2013 to 2026 Ram trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins diesel, flash bulletins such as 18-053-14 and 18-027-16 bring software meant to stop unwarranted MIL events for P2281. No manufacturer publishes the detection method or a threshold; an air-model comparison like Ford's speed-density check for P2282 is the likely principle. A real leak costs boost and power and leads to smoke on diesels. P2280 sits before the MAF, P2282 after the throttle.

causes.label: Loose clamp, split hose or leaking charge air cooler between MAF and throttle
Contaminated or drifting MAF sensor that misreports airflow
Engine software that sets the code without a real leak (update available)
Disconnected crankcase vent or other hose joined to this section

symptoms: MIL on
Hissing under boost and less power
Black smoke on diesels or rough idle on petrol engines

P2282.title: Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
P2282.description: P2282 means air enters the intake behind the throttle, so it reaches the cylinders without passing the throttle. Ford uses it as its PCV monitor on turbo engines with speed density: airflow worked out from manifold pressure is compared with airflow through the throttle, and a calculated leak of 1 lb/min or more for at least 5 s, with the throttle at 4 degrees or less, sets the code (2012, 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries). Ford designed the PCV inlet tube so that pulling it off leaves a large, detectable opening. Ford bulletins blame a stuck-open brake vacuum valve or tube on the 2.0 EcoBoost in the 2019-2020 Edge and Nautilus (TSB 20-2151), ice in the manifold of the 2020-2021 Escape hybrid (SSM 49654) and PCM software on the 2023 Maverick hybrid (TSB 23-2193). Land Rover found a detached brake vacuum pipe (LTB01186).

causes.label: Brake booster vacuum pipe detached or its check valve stuck open
Crankcase ventilation hose disconnected or cracked
Leaking intake manifold gasket, throttle body seal or vacuum hose
Iced manifold pressure sensor or software miscalculating the leak

symptoms: High or unstable idle speed
MIL on, sometimes with a hissing noise from the engine bay
Harder brake pedal if the brake vacuum line is affected

P2283.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2283.description: P2283 is the general circuit code for the injector control pressure (ICP) sensor. ICP describes the high-pressure engine oil that hydraulically actuated unit injectors (HEUI) use to pressurise fuel, as on Navistar-built Ford Power Stroke diesels; the sensor reports rail pressure so the injection pressure regulator can be closed-loop controlled. No manufacturer documents P2283 publicly. Ford's 6.0L summaries for 2003 and 2004 split the electrical check into P2285 (below 0.03 V) and P2286 (above 4.83 V), and Ford's 2014 PCM code table lists those two but not P2283. CARB requires diesel fuel-pressure control, explicitly including hydraulic fluid, to be monitored. Without a valid ICP signal the PCM substitutes a default value, so power and starting suffer.

causes.label: Failed ICP sensor, often with oil inside the connector
Damaged signal, reference or ground wire of the sensor
5-volt reference circuit pulled down by another sensor

symptoms: Low power and hesitation
Hard or long cranking, especially when hot
MIL on

P2284.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2284.description: P2284 means the measured injector control pressure does not follow what the PCM commands. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries (2003 and 2004) run the check continuously every 8 ms with the engine running: a fault is recorded once measured pressure stays more than 3.0 MPa above the target for longer than 7 s, the reverse case being P2290. Because the high-pressure oil pump is regulated through the IPR valve against the sensor reading, a biased sensor, a sticking regulator or an air-entrained oil supply can all open this gap. Ford also ran a 2003 owner programme replacing ICP sensors whose O-ring could shift and cause reduced power and rough idle. Unlike P2285/P2286 the circuit voltage is valid here; only its relation to the command is wrong.

causes.label: ICP sensor reading offset, including a shifted internal O-ring
Injection pressure regulator valve sticking or contaminated
Wrong, aerated or low engine oil disturbing pressure control
Oil wicking into the sensor connector

symptoms: Reduced power and rough idle
Engine runs on a substitute pressure value
MIL on

P2285.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2285.description: P2285 is set when the ICP sensor voltage falls almost to zero. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries for 2003 and 2004 define it precisely: below 0.03 V, checked every 8 ms without entry conditions, decided in under one second. Such a value cannot come from a working sensor on a 5-volt reference, so it points to an open signal wire, a short to ground, a lost reference voltage or an unplugged sensor. Ford lights the MIL for P2285 even on heavy federal trucks over 8,500 lb that otherwise run a reduced OBD calibration. On a HEUI engine the PCM then has to estimate rail pressure, so starting and response deteriorate. P2286 is the high-voltage counterpart; P2284 covers a valid signal that disagrees with the commanded pressure.

causes.label: Signal wire open or shorted to ground
Sensor disconnected or failed internally
Missing 5-volt reference supply

symptoms: MIL on immediately
Hard starting and reduced power

P2286.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2286.description: P2286 means the ICP sensor voltage has risen to the top of the range. In Ford's 2004 summary for the 6.0L Power Stroke the limit is above 4.83 V, checked every 8 ms and confirmed in less than one second; the 2003 edition already names the code alongside P2285. A reading that close to the 5-volt reference typically results from the signal wire touching the reference, a broken sensor ground or a sensor that has failed internally. Ford switches on the MIL for P2286 also on heavy federal trucks above 8,500 lb with their reduced OBD calibration, and its 2014 PCM code table marks the code as a MIL code. The engine runs on an estimated rail pressure until the fault is fixed. P2285 is the low counterpart, P2288 a real over-pressure condition.

causes.label: Open sensor ground circuit
Signal wire shorted to the 5-volt reference or another voltage
ICP sensor failed with output stuck high

symptoms: MIL on
Reduced power and possibly harsh running

P2287.title: Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2287.description: P2287 covers an ICP sensor signal that drops out or jumps for brief moments, too short or too irregular to be judged as a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents P2287 publicly; Ford's 6.0L summaries and its 2014 PCM table contain the steady electrical codes P2285 and P2286 but not this one. On HEUI diesels the sensor is mounted on the engine in a hot, oily environment, so oil creeping into the connector, fretting terminals and harness rubbing are the usual reasons for an unstable signal. Since the PCM regulates high-pressure oil from this reading, short dropouts can make the engine stumble or surge before a substitute value takes over. CARB counts such inputs among the components whose circuit faults must be monitored.

causes.label: Engine oil creeping into the sensor connector
Fretting or loose terminals at sensor or PCM
Harness rubbing on engine parts and shorting briefly

symptoms: Occasional stumble, surge or hesitation
Code returns without a fault visible in the workshop

P2288.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High
P2288.description: P2288 reports that the injector control pressure itself, not just its reading, has climbed above the allowed maximum while the engine runs. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries put the limit at 27.5 MPa in the 2003 edition and 29.5 MPa in 2004, sustained for more than 3 s. For comparison, Ford's high-pressure oil pump normally works between about 3 and 25 MPa on that engine. Excessive pressure means the injection pressure regulator fails to release enough oil to drain, because it sticks, its coil is driven wrongly or the control signal is stuck; a sensor reading high but still within circuit limits can also mislead. The PCM limits fuelling to protect the injectors and oil system. P2290 is the too-low case; P2289 the same check with the engine off.

causes.label: Injection pressure regulator valve stuck or contaminated
Fault in the regulator drive circuit holding it at high duty
ICP sensor reading higher than the actual pressure

symptoms: Reduced power with fuel limit active
Loud injection noise or knocking
MIL on

P2289.title: Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
P2289.description: P2289 is a plausibility test carried out with the engine stopped. On a HEUI diesel the high-pressure oil pump is driven by the engine, so once it stops, injector control pressure should drop to almost nothing. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries check this in engine-off mode: if the ICP reading stays above 10 MPa for more than 10 s (2003) or 12 s (2004), P2289 is stored. A real pressure that high without a running pump is unlikely, so the code mainly points to an ICP sensor with an offset or contamination, or to a signal circuit pulled up by a fault that stays within the electrical limits of P2286. Ford's 2014 PCM table marks it as a MIL code. P2288 is the counterpart with the engine running.

causes.label: ICP sensor with a positive offset or oil contamination
Partial short between signal and reference voltage
Faulty input stage in the PCM

symptoms: MIL on, possibly after the engine was switched off
Hard starting if the PCM trusts the false pressure value

P228A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228A.description: P228A is a protective shutdown code: the engine computer has stopped the engine because rail pressure could not be held even with fuel pressure regulator A at full authority. In GM's 2018 diesel tables regulator 1 (A) is the fuel metering unit on the high-pressure pump; the fault is logged when actual pressure lags the setpoint by more than 40 MPa while the commanded pump flow is already at its maximum, in 640 of 800 samples taken every 12.5 ms (about 8 s), as a Type A code. GM bulletin 18-NA-103 lists P228A and P228B next to P0087 when gelled winter diesel starves the in-tank pump. P228B is the same reaction for regulator B, P228C the milder control-limit warning. Expect a stall or no restart until supply is restored.

causes.label: Fuel supply starved (gelled or waxed diesel, clogged filter, failing in-tank pump)
Fuel metering unit on the high-pressure pump sticking or worn
High-pressure pump no longer reaching the required delivery
Leak in the high-pressure circuit or injector return

symptoms: Engine stalls while driving or shuts off shortly after starting
Long cranking or no restart
Check engine light on, often with P0087
Whining in-tank fuel pump in cold weather

P228B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown
P228B.description: P228B mirrors P228A but concerns fuel pressure regulator B, which in GM's 2018 diesel calibration is the rail pressure regulator valve that spills surplus fuel from the rail. The ECM shuts the engine down when rail pressure stays more than 40 MPa below target although it already commands that valve fully closed, judged over 640 of 800 samples at 12.5 ms and stored as Type A. A fully closed spill valve should trap everything the pump delivers, so a remaining deficit points to a valve leaking internally, a weak pump, a starved supply (GM bulletin 18-NA-103: gelled diesel, together with P228A and P0087) or excessive injector leakage. P229A is the non-shutdown deviation check of the same regulator.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve not sealing when closed
Fuel starvation from gelled diesel or a blocked filter
High-pressure pump delivering too little
Excessive injector leak-off

symptoms: Engine stops on its own and may not restart
Check engine light with low rail pressure codes
Loss of power just before the shutdown

P228C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P228C.description: P228C means rail pressure has stayed below target long enough that regulator A, the path that sets pump delivery, is judged to have used up its correction. GM uses it widely on gasoline direct injection: in table 25OBDG03A the pump fails to keep up for 10 s within a 12.5 s window, logged as Type A; on its 2018 diesels the margin is 13 MPa with the metering unit in closed loop (Type B), and table 24OBDG07 uses a 3 MPa gap held for 5 s. GM bulletins tie it to pump plungers sticking after heavy E85 use on 2.4, 3.0 and 3.6 L engines (18-NA-072, PIP5385) and to a wrong connector letting water into the bank 2 injector harness of the Corvette LT6 (24-NA-106). Reduced power is common; P228D is the overpressure case.
