causes.label: High-pressure pump or its control valve sticking or worn (e.g. after heavy E85 use)
Low-pressure supply too weak or contaminated fuel
Water or corrosion in the injector or pump wiring
Rail pressure sensor reading too low

symptoms: Reduced engine power message
Hesitation under load
Check engine light, sometimes clearing after a key cycle

P228D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P228D.description: P228D is the opposite of P228C: measured rail pressure stays above the setpoint for too long although regulator A should be cutting delivery. GM's gasoline table 25OBDG03A flags it when the high-pressure pump supplies more than requested for 10 of 12.5 s, as Type A; its 2018 diesel table uses minus 13 MPa with the metering unit in closed loop (Type B), and table 24OBDG07 minus 3 MPa for 7 s. Causes range from a pump control valve that will not shut off, via a pressure sensor reading wrong, to calibration: GM bulletin 17-NA-069 cures P228D on 5.3 L and 6.2 L V8s by reprogramming, and PACCAR bulletin E114 links it, with P0094, to defective unit pumps on MX-13 truck engines. Expect harsh running or derated power.

causes.label: Pump control or metering valve not reducing delivery
Engine control software needing an update
Rail pressure sensor reading too high
Defective unit or high-pressure pump (truck engines)

symptoms: Check engine light
Louder injection noise or rough idle
Reduced power in some cases

P228E.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P228E.description: P228E reports that the self-learned correction of fuel pressure regulator A has reached its lower bound. Ford, which still calls the part regulator 1, explains the logic in its 2023 diesel summary for the 3.0 L and 6.7 L Power Stroke: whenever requested rail pressure is at least 600 bar, the PCM keeps adapting the pressure controller, and if the adaptation factor drifts beyond a limit equivalent to roughly a 20 % error in rail pressure sensor slope, it stores P228E or P228F after about 10 s. Ford's 2014 PCM code table marks both as MIL codes. A learned value at the floor suggests a pressure sensor whose characteristic has shifted or a pump and regulator no longer matching their model. P228F is the upper bound, P229C the same test for regulator B.

causes.label: Rail pressure sensor characteristic drifted
Pressure regulator or metering valve worn, characteristic changed
High-pressure pump delivery deviating from its model

symptoms: Check engine light without noticeable drivability change
Occasional rough running or slower pressure response

P228F.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P228F.description: P228F is the upper counterpart of P228E: the learned correction for fuel pressure regulator A has run into its maximum. Ford's 2023 diesel summary applies one test to both codes on the 3.0 L and 6.7 L engines, with a limit near a 20 % rail pressure sensor slope error and about 10 s of monitoring at 600 bar or more. In heavy trucks, Volvo and Mack solutions K01029637 and K40914241 group P228F with P0087 and P016F for 11 L and 13 L common-rail engines; one cause they name is a damaged sealing lip on the second-stage filter that lets dirt reach the high-pressure side. Jaguar Land Rover message SSM 74588 lists P228F on the supercharged AJ126 petrol V6 together with high-pressure pump noise. Expect the MIL, possibly with rough running.

causes.label: Dirt in the high-pressure system, e.g. via a leaking fuel filter seal
High-pressure pump worn or noisy
Rail pressure sensor characteristic drifted
Low-pressure supply restricted

symptoms: Check engine light
Noise from the high-pressure pump
Uneven running in some cases

P2290.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low
P2290.description: P2290 belongs to the injector control pressure (ICP) family of hydraulically actuated unit injector (HEUI) diesels such as the Navistar-built Ford 6.0 L Power Stroke, where pressurised engine oil fires the injectors. Ford's 2003 and 2004 summaries run the check every 8 ms with the engine running and set it once actual ICP stays more than 3.0 MPa below the PCM's command for longer than 7 s; Ford's 2014 PCM code table marks it as a MIL code. Typical culprits are an injection pressure regulator that no longer seals, leaking high-pressure oil fittings or O-rings, a worn high-pressure oil pump, or low or aerated oil. Expect hard starting, low power and rough running. P2291 is the cranking variant, P2288 the overpressure case.

causes.label: Injection pressure regulator (IPR) contaminated or not sealing
Leaking high-pressure oil rail fittings, stand pipes or O-rings
Worn high-pressure oil pump
Low, wrong or aerated engine oil

symptoms: Hard starting, especially when hot
Lack of power and rough running
Check engine light

P2291.title: Injector Control Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking
P2291.description: P2291 judges pressure build-up while the starter is turning. On HEUI diesels the injectors only fire once injector control pressure has reached a minimum, so any leak in the pressurised oil circuit shows up as a long crank or a no-start; Wikipedia's Power Stroke article names a contaminated injection pressure regulator and failed high-pressure oil seals as typical no-start causes on the 6.0 L. Ford also reuses the code on its current common-rail diesels: the 2023 summary for the 3.0 L and 6.7 L sets P2291 when rail pressure stays under 14,000 kPa for 20 s of cranking. Ford's 2014 PCM code table lists the code as well. Unlike P2290, which watches the running engine, P2291 covers only the start phase.

causes.label: Leak in the high-pressure oil (HEUI) or fuel (common rail) circuit
Injection pressure regulator or rail pressure valve not sealing
High-pressure pump delivering too little at cranking speed
Low cranking speed from a weak battery or starter

symptoms: Engine cranks long or does not start
Starts only after repeated attempts
Check engine light after the start attempt

P2292.title: Injector Control Pressure Erratic
P2292.description: P2292 describes an injector control pressure that jumps around instead of sitting steadily below or above target. No manufacturer documents its detection logic publicly: Ford's 2014 PCM code table lists the code without a MIL marking, and the 6.0 L Power Stroke summaries only describe the steady checks P2284, P2288 and P2290. On a HEUI engine an unsettled pressure can come from air in the oil, an injection pressure regulator that sticks and releases, a failing high-pressure oil pump or a loose sensor connection. CARB requires diesel fuel pressure control, explicitly including hydraulic fluid, to be monitored. Drivers notice surging, stumbling or intermittent power loss. A pure dropout of the sensor signal fits P2287 better.

causes.label: Air in the engine oil (foaming, wrong oil, overfill)
Injection pressure regulator sticking intermittently
ICP sensor or its connector making intermittent contact
High-pressure oil pump starting to fail

symptoms: Surging or bucking under steady throttle
Intermittent power loss
Rough idle

P2293.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Performance
P2293.description: P2293 checks whether fuel pressure regulator B really controls rail pressure. In GM's 2018 diesel table regulator B is the rail pressure regulator valve; the code sets when, with that valve in charge, rail pressure rises above a calibrated ceiling of 67 to 217 MPa in 160 of 229 samples at 6.25 ms, Type A. VW's 2014 quick reference for the Passat, which still uses the older name regulator 2, flags a gap between commanded and measured pressure beyond plus or minus 1.5 MPa. GM preliminary information PIP5988 for the 2024 3.0 L Duramax (LZ0) advises replacing the high-pressure rail that carries the valve, not the pump, when P2293 appears alone or with P0089. P2294 to P2296 cover the electrical side of the same valve.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve sticking or worn (often replaced with the rail)
Rail pressure sensor reading wrong
Contaminated fuel affecting the valve
Engine control software issue

symptoms: Check engine light
Reduced power or stalling in severe cases
Hard starting

P2294.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit/Open
P2294.description: P2294 is the open-circuit check of the drive line to fuel pressure regulator B. GM's 2018 diesel ECM tests the low-side driver of the rail pressure regulator valve while the output is switched off: a voltage indicating more than 200 kΩ between signal and ground counts as open, and 44 failures in 88 samples at 6.25 ms set the code as Type B. VW's 2014 Passat quick reference uses a signal voltage between 1.40 and 3.20 V or an implausible signal pattern. Broken wires, a pushed-back connector pin or an interrupted valve coil are the usual findings. Without control of the valve the ECM cannot release rail pressure as intended and may limit power. P2295 and P2296 split shorts to ground and to supply.

causes.label: Broken wire in the regulator harness
Loose, corroded or pushed-back connector pin
Open coil in the pressure regulator valve
Faulty output driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Reduced power or emergency mode
Unstable idle or hard starting

P2295.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit Low
P2295.description: P2295 stands for the control line of fuel pressure regulator B touching ground. GM's 2018 diesel ECM detects it with its low-side driver switched off: if the measured voltage corresponds to 0.5 Ω or less towards ground, the sample counts as failed, and 44 of 88 samples at 6.25 ms confirm the fault as Type B. VW's 2014 Passat quick reference describes the same fault as a ground short, with a signal voltage below 1.40 V. Chafed insulation near the rail or pump, water in the connector and a shorted valve coil are typical findings. Because a grounded low-side line can keep the valve energised regardless of command, rail pressure may drift from target and the ECM may reduce power. P2296 is the high counterpart.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through to ground
Water or corrosion in the regulator connector
Shorted coil in the pressure regulator valve

symptoms: Check engine light
Rail pressure too high or unstable, reduced power
Rough running

P2296.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit High
P2296.description: P2296 is set when the control line of fuel pressure regulator B has contact with supply voltage. GM's 2018 diesel ECM checks this with its low-side driver switched on: if the line still shows a voltage equivalent to 0.5 Ω or less towards power, the sample fails, again with 44 of 88 samples and Type B. VW's 2014 Passat quick reference uses a signal voltage above 3.20 V and groups an open line with a battery-voltage short here. In that state the driver cannot pull the valve current through, so the valve stays unpowered and the ECM loses its means of holding the intended rail pressure; hard starting and reduced power follow. Look for the harness rubbing on a battery feed and for a damaged valve connector.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a voltage supply
Damaged or corroded regulator connector
Faulty output driver in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Hard starting or stalling
Reduced power

P2297.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2297.description: P2297 concerns the upstream oxygen sensor of bank 1 and the moment when fuel is cut on deceleration and the sensor should read almost pure air. Diesel calibrations compare the reading in overrun with a modelled value: GM's 6.6L LML faults a gap between measured and calculated value above 0.06 to 0.07, the 3.0L LZ0 a deviation beyond 5 percent (Type B). On the 2023 Jeep Gladiator 3.0L diesel, Stellantis TSB 25-002-24 checks the O2 adaptation after a coast-down and replaces the sensor above 0.0282. Bosch-based petrol engines read the code the other way: with all injectors firing, a signal looking like fuel cut-off sets it (Saab 9-5 2011 LDK: 4 s, Type B; GM 2005 V6 LP1/LY7: over 3.7 V for 10 s). GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists it for the LZ0; P2298 is bank 2.

causes.label: Upstream wide-band sensor aged or drifted (wrong reading in air)
Exhaust leak ahead of the sensor drawing in outside air
Air-mass or fuel model error (MAF, injector leakage, EGR) skewing the expected value
Engine software needing an update (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Usually no noticeable change in driving behaviour
Possibly stored with P0133 or fuel-quantity codes

P2298.title: O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2298.description: P2298 is the bank 2 version of P2297 and exists only on engines with two cylinder banks, each with its own upstream oxygen sensor. Three GM tables show the two readings of the code. The 2005 3.5L V6 (L66) tests during fuel cut-off with coolant above 69 °C and below 2,200 rpm, faulting a wide-band output above 4.5 V or below 2.9 V, over two drive cycles. The Bosch-managed 2005 V6 (LP1/LY7) works the other way round and flags a signal above 3.7 V for 10 s while every injector is firing and the target is richer than lambda 1.6. GM's 2024 tables (24OBDG07) set it for a lambda equivalent above 12 from the corrected pump current with the ceramic hotter than 655 °C, 10 s, two trips. No bulletin names P2298. Bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1.

causes.label: Bank 2 upstream wide-band sensor aged or contaminated
Exhaust leak on bank 2 ahead of the sensor
Damaged sensor lead or connector on bank 2

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Usually no noticeable change in driving behaviour
Bank 2 fuel trim values may look unusual

P2299.title: Brake Pedal Position/Accelerator Pedal Position Incompatible
P2299.description: P2299 means the vehicle has seen the brake and the accelerator pressed together in a way it treats as implausible; engine torque is usually cut as a brake-override measure. GM documents the check in the brake control module of 2020 models with a pedal travel sensor: the code sets when the travel signal is not zero while the accelerator is applied above 4.47 mph (7.2 km/h) for 0.12 s, Type A. An FCA parts tip states it is mostly caused by drivers resting their left foot on the brake and warns against replacing the pedal; many FCA flash bulletins, e.g. 18-007-14 for the Fiat 500, and Nissan bulletin NTB17-063 (Titan XD, Cummins 5.0 L) clear it by reprogramming. A misadjusted brake light switch can also trigger it.

causes.label: Driver resting a foot on the brake while accelerating
Control module software needing an update
Brake light switch or pedal travel sensor misadjusted or sticking
Floor mat or object keeping a pedal partly pressed

symptoms: Engine power drops while braking and accelerating together
Check engine light
Car does not respond to the accelerator for a moment

P229A.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
P229A.description: P229A is the low-pressure control-limit check for fuel pressure regulator B. In GM's 2018 diesel table regulator B is the rail pressure regulator valve; while it governs the rail in closed loop, the ECM compares setpoint and measured pressure and flags a deficit beyond about 13 MPa, using the same 640-of-800-sample window and Type B rating as the metering unit check P228C. The test pauses at low fuel level, ambient pressure under 60 kPa or ambient temperature below −7 °C. A valve that no longer seals, internal injector leakage or a pump short of delivery create the deficit. GM is the only maker found documenting P229A publicly. P229B is the overpressure case, P228B the stage that forces a shutdown.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve leaking internally
High-pressure pump delivering too little
Excessive injector leak-off
Restricted low-pressure supply or clogged filter

symptoms: Check engine light
Lack of power under load
Longer cranking times

P229B.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
P229B.description: P229B flags rail pressure that stays above target while fuel pressure regulator B should be holding it. GM's 2018 diesel table, where regulator B is the rail pressure regulator valve, runs this check with the valve in closed-loop control and under the same enable conditions as P229A (fuel level, ambient pressure and temperature), mirroring the overpressure test P228D of the metering unit, and rates it Type B. A valve that sticks closed or cannot open far enough, a drive signal that keeps it energised, or a rail pressure sensor reading high are the classic causes. If pressure keeps climbing to the absolute ceiling, P2293 follows. P229A is the deficit case, P228D the same fault seen through regulator A.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve sticking closed
Rail pressure sensor reading too high
Valve drive signal stuck on (wiring or module)

symptoms: Check engine light
Harder combustion noise
Reduced power in some cases

P229C.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
P229C.description: P229C means the learned correction for fuel pressure regulator B has reached its lower bound. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The matching check for regulator A is described by Ford for its 2023 diesels: the controller adapts at steady rail pressure of 600 bar or more and stores P228E or P228F when the adaptation would exceed roughly a 20 % sensor-slope error. On systems with two regulators, such as GM diesels with a pump metering unit (A) and a rail pressure valve (B), the B value describes the learned behaviour of that spill valve. CARB requires a monitor to report a pressure control that has used up its adjustment authority. Expect a lit MIL with little drivability effect; P229D is the upper bound.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve characteristic drifted
Rail pressure sensor characteristic drifted
Adaptation values not reset after a component replacement

symptoms: Check engine light
Usually no noticeable change in driving

P229D.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator B Exceeded Learning Limits - Too High
P229D.description: P229D reports that the learned correction for fuel pressure regulator B has climbed to its upper bound, the opposite of P229C. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, so its logic can only be inferred from the regulator A equivalent P228F: Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets that code after about 10 s when the controller adaptation passes a limit near a 20 % sensor-slope error, and Volvo and Mack link P228F on their truck engines to dirt that reached the high-pressure side. For regulator B, usually the rail pressure valve, a correction pinned at the top points to a valve that needs ever more drive to hold pressure, or a sensor out of calibration. CARB requires such exhausted control authority to be flagged.

causes.label: Rail pressure regulator valve worn or contaminated
Rail pressure sensor characteristic drifted
Contaminated fuel reaching the high-pressure side

symptoms: Check engine light
Occasional unstable rail pressure or rough idle

P229E.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P229E.description: P229E is the basic electrical fault of the second NOx sensor on bank 1, the one behind the SCR catalyst that shows how much NOx survives conversion. Its attached control unit checks the probe lines and passes the result to the engine computer over CAN. GM's 6.6L Duramax (LML) sets the code as Type A when an open or shorted status keeps arriving longer than 10 s, or 0.5 s in a later calibration. Ford's 3.0L and 6.7L diesels use it for shorts and opens on the Vs, COM, Ip1 and Ip2 lines and for a failed internal self-test of the sensor processor; VW's 2014 Touareg TDI for an error message or a validity ratio above 0.5. Volvo and Mack replace the outlet sensor, and Nissan bulletin NTB16-048 does the same on the 2016 Titan XD, adding an ECM update. P2200 is the front sensor.

causes.label: Internal failure of the outlet NOx probe or its control unit
Damaged lead between probe and sensor control unit (heat, chafing)
Water or corrosion in the sensor connector
Engine control software needing an update (Nissan Titan XD 2016, NTB16-048)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
No valid downstream NOx value in live data
SCR warning; catalyst efficiency check cannot complete

P229F.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P229F.description: P229F says the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 is electrically sound but its reading fails a plausibility test. Methods vary. GM's 6.6L LML waits for a burst of engine-out NOx and faults the sensor if its own value moves by less than 3 ppm (Type B); the 3.0L LZ0 watches the stability of the internal pump currents, failing above 0.5 percent unstable time. Ford checks offsets of roughly 30 ppm low or 50 ppm high and a missing rise on tip-in; VW's 2014 Touareg TDI checks offset, self-diagnosis results and oxygen plausibility. Volvo and Mack explain that P229F-64 can set when a fresh SCR leaves almost no NOx, so a single event is no proof of a bad sensor. Hino wants DEF quality and dosing checked first, and Ford warns that EGR cleaning fluids poison NOx sensors.

causes.label: Outlet NOx element drifted, slow or poisoned (e.g. sodium from cleaning fluids)
Poor DEF quality or faulty dosing that distorts downstream NOx
Harness or connector fault at the outlet sensor (Volvo/Mack P229F-64)
Engine or dosing software needing an update (several FCA, Hino, Mazda notices)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Often stored together with SCR efficiency code P20EE
Downstream NOx value implausible compared with the upstream sensor

P22A0.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A0.description: P22A0 reports that the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 sends a raw value below the smallest figure a healthy sensor can produce. Because the sensor talks over CAN, the test looks at the transmitted number rather than a wire voltage. GM uses minus 90 ppm on the 6.6L LML, on its 2017 small diesels (table 17OBDG04) and on the 3.0L LZ0, in each case Type B after two trips with dew point reached and supply in range; the LZ0 needs 100 failed samples in 200. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI faults below minus 105 ppm or a lambda signal under minus 0.2. GM bulletin 24-NA-094 puts P22A0 on the list cured by an LZ0 software update on 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500. A strongly negative value usually means element drift or an internal fault. P22A1 is the upper limit, P2202 the front sensor.

causes.label: Outlet NOx element drifted low or internally faulty
Engine software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)
Damaged lead between probe and sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Live data shows a negative downstream NOx value
SCR efficiency monitor does not complete

P22A1.title: NOx Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A1.description: P22A1 flags a raw value from the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 that is higher than anything plausibly left behind the SCR catalyst. GM's 6.6L LML uses 1,500 ppm, or 2,500 ppm in table 14OBDG10; the 3.0L LZ0 and the 2017 small diesels also use 2,500 ppm, Type B after two trips. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI uses 1,655 ppm or a lambda signal above 1.54. Volvo and Mack count P22A1 among codes that point to a damaged outlet sensor and replace that sensor alone. For Ram ProMaster vans, a 2025 Stellantis case (S2525000001) reports P22A1 together with P20EE, asks for standard diagnosis including the DEF condition and states that engineering is still looking for the root cause. GM includes the code in LZ0 software bulletin 24-NA-094. P22A0 is the lower limit, P2203 the front sensor.

causes.label: Outlet NOx sensor reading high due to internal damage
DEF quality or dosing problem raising real tailpipe NOx
Engine software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Implausibly high downstream NOx value in live data
SCR efficiency code P20EE stored alongside

P22A2.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A2.description: P22A2 describes a rear NOx sensor on bank 1 whose measuring circuit reports faults that come and go rather than staying present. Smart NOx sensors pass the state of that circuit (open wire, short or no error) to the engine computer over CAN, so brief, repeated fault reports fit this code. No manufacturer publicly documents a threshold for P22A2. The only trace is a Ford notice for 2015 to 2016 6.7L Super Duty trucks (SSM 45920, NHTSA index only) explaining that the code may stay stored after the actual fault has been repaired; CARB requires NOx sensors to be monitored continuously for circuit faults. Look for loose terminals, heat-damaged cable along the exhaust and water in the connector. P229E is the steady fault, P2204 the same pattern at the front sensor.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminals at the outlet NOx sensor connector
Harness along the exhaust damaged by heat or vibration
Sporadic internal fault in the sensor module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that may go out and return
Downstream NOx value dropping out briefly
Code remains stored after the root fault is fixed

P22A3.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A3.description: The ceramic element of a NOx sensor measures only after its built-in heater has brought it to several hundred degrees. P22A3 reports a break on the heater control side of the rear sensor on bank 1, behind the SCR catalyst. GM's 6.6L LML sets it when the sensor reports an open heater over CAN longer than 10 s, Type A. On the 3.0L LZ0 the heater control pin is tested for a missing load (80 failures in 160 samples), on the 2017 small diesels the H+ supply pin of the Gen 3.0 sensor; both Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip. Volvo and Mack read P22A3-13 as a probable outlet sensor failure, and GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists the code for an LZ0 software update. P22A4 and P22A5 are shorts, P22A6 the heater sense line, P2205 the front sensor.

causes.label: Heater element in the outlet NOx probe burnt through
Broken conductor between probe and sensor module
Software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Outlet NOx sensor never reports ready
SCR warning on the display

P22A4.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A4.description: P22A4 means the heater control line of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 has a short to ground, so the sensor module can no longer drive the heater as commanded. GM documents it on the 3.0L LZ0 as a ground short on the heater control pin, judged once dew point is reached and sensor supply exceeds 9.9 V, 80 failures in 160 samples, Type B after two trips. Its 2017 small diesels watch the H+ supply pin of the Gen 3.0 sensor instead, 20 failures in 40 samples. Volvo and Mack count P22A4 among codes that indicate a damaged outlet sensor, and GM bulletin 24-NA-094 adds it to an LZ0 software update for 2024 Silverado and Sierra 1500. Expect the MIL after two trips and no downstream NOx data. P22A3 is the open circuit, P22A5 a short to voltage, P2206 the front sensor.

causes.label: Heater element or probe lead shorted to ground inside the sensor
Probe lead insulation chafed against the exhaust or body
Software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Outlet NOx sensor stays not ready
SCR warning on the display

P22A5.title: NOx Sensor Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A5.description: P22A5 is the opposite of P22A4: the heater control line of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 has a short to supply voltage. The sensor module then cannot switch or regulate the heater, and the element risks running too hot or the module shuts the heater off to protect it. GM describes the check on the 3.0L LZ0 as a battery short at the heater control pin, 80 failures in 160 samples with dew point reached and supply above 9.9 V, Type B after two trips; the 2017 small diesels test the H+ supply pin of the Gen 3.0 sensor with 20 failures in 40 samples. GM bulletin 24-NA-094 lists P22A5 among codes an LZ0 software update clears on 2024 pickups. No public bulletin names a hardware fix. P22A3 is the open circuit, P22A4 the ground short, P2207 the front sensor.

causes.label: Heater circuit inside the sensor shorted to supply voltage
Probe lead or connector touching a powered conductor
Software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Heater switched off, outlet NOx sensor not ready
SCR warning on the display

P22A6.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A6.description: Besides the heater supply, a NOx sensor has a sense line through which its module measures the resistance of the heated element and so infers its temperature. P22A6 reports an electrical fault on that feedback line of the rear sensor on bank 1. GM's 3.0L LZ0 sets it for an open circuit at the HTemp pin, 80 failures in 160 samples, Type A after one trip; GM notes that the Continental Gen 3.5 sensor debounces electrical faults internally for 1.5 s. The 2017 small diesels use the same open-circuit check with 20 failures in 40 samples, also Type A. Volvo and Mack list P22A6 among codes that call for a new outlet sensor; GM bulletin 24-NA-094 names it Heater Feedback Circuit and covers it with an LZ0 software update. P22A8/P22A9 are shorts, P22A7 plausibility, P2208 the front sensor.

causes.label: Open heater sense conductor inside the outlet NOx probe or its lead
Water or corrosion in the probe connector
Software anomaly (GM 3.0L LZ0 2024, bulletin 24-NA-094)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Outlet NOx sensor not ready, no downstream value
SCR warning on the display

P22A7.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A7.description: P22A7 means the heater feedback of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 shows a heater that does not reach or hold its target, although no open or short is found. GM's 3.0L LZ0 and 2017 small diesels compare the measured heater resistance with its target once supply has been in range for 45 s and dew point passed 180 s ago (Type B); the 6.6L LML fails the sensor if its heater never reports set-point temperature. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI allows 180 s after dew point; Ford uses the code as a signal readiness check. Ford traced it on 2017 to 2020 6.7L Super Duty trucks to water in the NOx connectors (TSB 20-2067, new harness 14406) and on 2023 models to that harness chafing on the EGR cooler, with fuse F18 blown (SSM 51750/51791). Nissan's NTB16-048 replaces the outlet sensor.

causes.label: Aged heater or element in the outlet NOx probe
Water in the NOx sensor connectors (Ford 6.7L 2017-2020, TSB 20-2067)
Harness chafed on the EGR cooler with blown supply fuse (Ford 6.7L 2023)
Weak supply to the sensor module limiting heater power

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Outlet NOx sensor becomes ready late or not at all
Often stored with U029E or other NOx sensor codes

P22A8.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A8.description: P22A8 means the heater sense line of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 is shorted to ground; the sensor module uses that line to read the element temperature via its resistance. With that line pulled to ground, the module sees a temperature value it cannot trust and cannot regulate the heater properly. GM documents the test on the 3.0L LZ0: ground short at the HTemp pin, judged with dew point reached and sensor supply above 9.9 V, 80 failures in 160 samples, Type B after two trips; the Continental Gen 3.5 sensor debounces such faults internally for 1.5 s. GM's 2017 small diesels use the same check with 20 failures in 40 samples. No public bulletin names this code. P22A6 is the open circuit, P22A9 the short to voltage, P2210 the front sensor.

causes.label: Heater sense conductor shorted to ground inside the probe
Probe lead insulation damaged against exhaust or body
Water bridging pins in the probe connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Outlet NOx sensor not ready
SCR efficiency check does not run

P22A9.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22A9.description: P22A9 is the high-side twin of P22A8: the heater sense line of the rear NOx sensor on bank 1 has a short to supply voltage. The module then reads an element resistance that is far off and loses its temperature feedback, so it cannot hold the probe at working temperature. GM's 3.0L LZ0 looks for a battery short at the HTemp pin once dew point is reached and supply exceeds 9.9 V, 80 failures in 160 samples, Type B after two trips; the 2017 small diesels need 20 failures in 40 samples. In both cases the Continental sensor itself confirms an electrical fault before reporting it. No manufacturer bulletin mentions P22A9. A short often sits where the probe lead runs close to other powered wiring or where a connector has taken in water. P22A6 is the open circuit, P22A8 the ground short, P2211 the front sensor.

causes.label: Heater sense conductor shorted to supply inside the probe
Probe lead touching another powered conductor
Water bridging pins in the probe connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after two trips
Outlet NOx sensor not ready
SCR warning on the display

P22AA.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AA.description: P22AA covers a heater sense line on the rear NOx sensor of bank 1 that fails only now and then. The module uses this line to read the element temperature and keep the heater on target; if the reading drops out or jumps for short moments, the temperature control briefly loses its reference and the sensor may fall out of its ready state. No manufacturer publicly documents a threshold or a bulletin for P22AA, and GM, Ford and VW do not list it in their published tables. CARB asks for continuous monitoring of NOx sensor heater circuits, and smart sensors report the heater circuit state (open, short, no error) over CAN. In practice, check terminal grip, cable routing near hot parts and water ingress. P22A6, P22A8 and P22A9 are the steady faults, P2212 the front sensor.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminal in the probe connector
Lead near the exhaust cracked by heat or vibration
Intermittent internal contact fault in the probe

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that may come and go
Outlet NOx sensor intermittently not ready

P22AB.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AB.description: P22AB reports a break in the positive current control line of a wide-band probe mounted behind the catalyst or, on diesels, further down the aftertreatment on bank 1. On a Bosch-style five-wire probe this is the pump-current lead (IP/APE) through which the controller moves oxygen into or out of the pump cell. Chrysler lists the code for 2010-2012 Ram 2500/3500 pickups with the 6.7 Cummins in bulletins 25-004-12 and 25-002-14; the prescribed fix is new sensor connectors or an overlay harness before any sensor is replaced. GM names it in 21-NA-149 among faults from chafed harnesses on the 3.0 Duramax LM2. P22AC/P22AD cover low/high, P22B8 is bank 2, P2237 the upstream twin. The warning lamp comes on; the engine usually runs normally.

causes.label: Corroded, loose or poorly crimped terminal in the sensor or sensor-module connector
Pump-current wire broken or chafed through along the exhaust
Internal open circuit in the downstream wide-band sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading frozen or missing in live data
Related catalyst or aftertreatment monitors stay incomplete

P22AC.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AC.description: P22AC means the pump-current (positive current) line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe reads below its allowed window, usually because the wire touches ground or its insulation has worn through. GM includes the code in bulletin 21-NA-149 for 2019-2022 light-duty trucks and SUVs with the 3.0 Duramax LM2, where chafed engine wiring triggers a long list of faults; no public GM table gives a threshold. Not every maker uses this slot: Ford books a shorted lead on its upstream wide-band probes as P0131. Saab rates the upstream analog P2238 as a Type B fault. P22AB is the open-circuit case, P22AD the high one, P22B9 the bank 2 copy. Expect a lit warning lamp and stalled emission monitors rather than a change in driving.

causes.label: Pump-current wire chafed against the body or exhaust and shorted to ground
Internal short in the downstream wide-band sensor
Water or contamination bridging the connector pins

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen value pinned at an extreme in live data
Possible failed emissions inspection because monitors are not ready

P22AD.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AD.description: P22AD is the high-side fault on the positive current control line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe: the pump-current wire is pulled above its expected level, for example by contact with the heater feed or another supply wire. On Saab's 2010 9-5 the pump-current pins measure roughly 2.8 V at the plug, which gives a feel for the normal bias. GM lists the code in bulletin 21-NA-149 for the 3.0 Duramax LM2, again tied to engine harness chafing, but publishes no limit. Ford sends shorts to power on its upstream wide-band probes to P0132 instead of a dedicated code. The upstream analog is P2239 (Type B at Saab); P22AB is the open circuit, P22AC the low reading, P22BA the bank 2 version. The lamp is lit; driving normally feels unchanged.

causes.label: Pump-current wire shorted to the heater supply or another positive feed
Internal short between heater and pump cell in the sensor
Faulty sensor interface in the ECM or sensor module

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading implausibly high or fixed
Readiness monitors for catalyst or aftertreatment not completed

P22AE.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AE.description: P22AE points to an open reference voltage line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe, i.e. the lead of the Nernst (sensing) cell, called RE/UN by Bosch and VS by NTK. Through it the controller reads the cell voltage it regulates the pump current against, so a break leaves the oxygen value meaningless. Chrysler lists P22AE for 2010-2012 Ram 2500/3500 with the 6.7 Cummins; bulletin 25-003-13 found tin instead of gold terminals in five cavities of the 2011 sensor-module connector. For the upstream twin P2243, Ford, GM and Saab declare an open when the sensor voltage leaves 0.2-4.7 V and, at GM/Saab, the cell resistance exceeds 570 ohms. P22AF, P22B0 and P22B1 are performance/low/high, P22BB is bank 2. The lamp comes on.

causes.label: Corroded or wrongly plated terminals in the sensor or sensor-module connector
Broken Nernst-cell wire in the harness
Cracked or aged sensing cell with very high internal resistance

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen or lambda value invalid in live data
Other downstream sensor codes may be stored at the same time

P22AF.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22AF.description: P22AF is a plausibility fault on the Nernst-cell (reference voltage) side of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe: the wiring is intact, but the cell signal does not behave as the controller expects, for instance it cannot be held at its set point or drifts. Typical reasons are an aged cell whose resistance has risen above the roughly 300 ohms Bosch quotes for the LSU 4.9, soot or oil deposits, or a heater that keeps the element too cool. No maker documents this code publicly. CARB requires the OBD system to catch deterioration of voltage, impedance, current or offset of air-fuel sensors behind the aftertreatment before emissions rise too far. Siblings: P22AE open, P22B0/P22B1 low/high, P22BC bank 2, P2244 upstream.

causes.label: Aged downstream wide-band sensor with raised cell resistance
Soot, oil or coolant deposits on the sensing element
Weak heater or heater control that leaves the element too cold
High-resistance contact in the Nernst-cell circuit

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading sluggish or offset compared with the upstream sensor
Catalyst or aftertreatment monitor may report errors as a follow-up

P22B0.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B0.description: P22B0 says the reference voltage (Nernst-cell) line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe sits below its permitted range. On a Bosch LSU the Nernst cell is a high-impedance source that tolerates at most about 250 microamps, so a chafed wire touching ground drags it down at once. No maker documents this exact code publicly. Ford's upstream logic treats a cell voltage under 0.2 V as part of its open-circuit check and books shorted leads under P0131, which shows that makers split these faults differently. JLR lists the upstream analog P2245 in a bulletin on cracked sensors. P22AE is the open case, P22B1 the high one, P22AF the performance check, P22BD the bank 2 equivalent. The driver mainly sees the warning lamp.

causes.label: Nernst-cell wire shorted to ground through damaged insulation
Internal short in the downstream wide-band sensor
Moisture in the connector creating a leakage path

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen value implausible or unavailable

P22B1.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B1.description: P22B1 is set when the reference voltage (Nernst-cell) line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe reads above its valid range. Because the cell delivers only a few hundred millivolts across about 300 ohms, any contact with the heater feed or another live wire overrides it. A cracked ceramic letting the heater circuit leak into the cell can do the same. No maker publishes this code with a threshold; for the upstream sensor, Ford and Saab already treat a voltage above 4.7 V as an open reference line, while Ford sends shorts to power to P0132. CARB demands detection of out-of-range values on air-fuel sensors behind the aftertreatment. P22AE covers the open, P22B0 the low reading, P22BE bank 2 and P2246 the upstream twin.

causes.label: Nernst-cell wire shorted to the heater supply or another live wire
Cracked sensor ceramic leaking heater voltage into the cell
Faulty sensor interface in the ECM or sensor module

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading stuck at a limit

P22B2.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B2.description: P22B2 indicates an open negative current control line on the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe. This is the shared return of pump and sensing cell, the virtual ground (VM/IPN on Bosch, COM on NTK), which the controller holds at a mid-level bias of around 2.5 V. Chrysler lists the code for 2010-2012 Ram 2500/3500 with the 6.7 Cummins and repairs connectors and wiring first; GM names it in 21-NA-149 for the 3.0 Duramax LM2. For the upstream twin P2251, Ford sees an open return as a sensor voltage stuck near 1.5 V for 10 s, GM and Saab as 1.47-1.53 V with cell resistance above 570 ohms. P22B3/P22B4 cover low/high, P22BF bank 2. The warning lamp lights; drivability normally stays the same.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or pushed-back terminal on the return wire
Return (virtual ground) wire broken in the harness
Internal open circuit in the downstream wide-band sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading frozen near a fixed value
Aftertreatment readiness not set

P22B3.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B3.description: P22B3 reports the negative current control line, i.e. the virtual ground of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe, as too low. Normally the controller lifts this common return to a bias near 2.5 V (Saab measures that at the plug of its 2010 9-5) so that pump current can flow in both directions; a short to chassis ground collapses the bias and with it the measuring range. No maker documents this exact code publicly. Mitsubishi lists the upstream analog P2252 as a two-trip code for the 2022 Outlander, and Ford handles upstream shorts under P0131 instead. P22B2 is the open-circuit code, P22B4 the high one, P22C0 the bank 2 version. Apart from the warning lamp, the driver rarely notices anything.

causes.label: Return wire shorted to chassis ground through chafed insulation
Internal short inside the wide-band sensor
Faulty bias supply in the ECM or sensor module

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen value implausible or pinned

P22B4.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B4.description: P22B4 is stored when the negative current control line (virtual ground) of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe climbs above its intended bias. Because this return sits at a mid-level voltage rather than at chassis ground, a short to the heater feed or battery voltage is the classic trigger, sometimes via moisture or a heat-damaged connector. No maker documents this exact code publicly; Mitsubishi lists the upstream analog P2253 as a two-trip code for the 2022 Outlander, while Ford treats upstream shorts to power as P0132. CARB asks for detection of out-of-range values on such sensors. P22B2 is the open, P22B3 the low variant, P22C1 the bank 2 code. The lamp is on and the related emission monitors will not complete.

causes.label: Return wire shorted to heater supply or battery voltage
Heat-damaged or wet connector bridging pins
Internal heater-to-cell leakage in the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading erratic or at a limit

P22B5.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B5.description: P22B5 flags an open trim line on the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe. Bosch LSU probes carry a trimming resistor in the connector module, wired to pin 5 (RT/IA), that sets each sensor's individual characteristic; the controller reads it to scale the measured pump current. Lose that line and the oxygen value can still move, but with the wrong gain. Chrysler's wording speaks of the pump cell current trim of sensor 1/2 and lists the code for 2010-2012 Ram 2500/3500 with the 6.7 Cummins; after the wiring repair its road test compares both sensors during 10-second fuel cut-offs and allows no more than 4 % difference. Saab's upstream analog P2626 is checked in overrun below 750 °C and sets above 4.81 V. P22B6/P22B7 are low/high, P22C2 bank 2.

causes.label: Corroded or loose trim-line terminal in the sensor connector
Trim wire broken between sensor connector and ECM or sensor module
Open trimming resistor in the sensor's connector module

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen reading disagrees with the upstream sensor during fuel cut-off
Follow-up aftertreatment or catalyst faults possible

P22B6.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B6.description: By its name P22B6 is the low fault on the trim line of the bank 1 downstream wide-band probe, i.e. the lead to the calibration resistor in a Bosch-style sensor connector. GM's diesel tables use the slot differently: they set it when the oxygen value reported by the second NOx sensor falls below its physical minimum, less than -4 % in 200 of 250 samples in the 2016 table, with the engine in combustion mode and no NOx sensor fault pending. It is a Type B code with two trips. GM also lists P22B6 in PIP5468 for 2017-2018 Silverado/Sierra HD with the 6.6 L5P, where leaking charge-air ducting can set it, and in 21-NA-149 for the 3.0 LM2. P22B5 is the open, P22B7 the high counterpart, P22C3 bank 2. The lamp comes on.

causes.label: Faulty downstream NOx/oxygen sensor delivering an impossible oxygen value
Leaking charge-air cooler ducting (GM 6.6 L5P)
Trim or signal wire shorted to ground in the harness

symptoms: Check engine light
Negative oxygen percentage shown for the downstream sensor in live data
Possible additional boost or air-flow codes when charge air leaks

P22B7.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22B7.description: P22B7 is, going by its title, the high fault on the trim circuit belonging to bank 1's downstream wide-band probe. In GM's diesel tables (2016, 2018 and 2025 group 04) the code is a ceiling test on the oxygen value of the second NOx sensor: the 2016 table flags readings above 24 %, which is more oxygen than fresh air holds, in 100 of 200 samples. The test runs only while exhaust back-pressure stays below its limit, no exhaust brake is active and no NOx sensor pressure fault is pending; GM rates it Type B, two trips. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 lists it for the 3.0 Duramax LM2 alongside harness chafing. No public source gives a trim-resistor threshold. P22B5 is the open, P22B6 the low case, P22C4 bank 2. The lamp lights.

causes.label: Faulty downstream NOx/oxygen sensor reporting excess oxygen
Chafed engine harness affecting the sensor lines (GM 3.0 LM2)
Trim or signal wire shorted to a voltage source

symptoms: Check engine light
Downstream oxygen value above 21 % in live data

P22B8.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22B8.description: P22B8 is the bank 2 version of an open positive current control line on a downstream wide-band probe: the pump-current wire (IP/APE on Bosch) of the sensor behind the catalyst or aftertreatment on the second cylinder bank has lost continuity. It only exists on engines with two exhaust banks and a wide-band probe after each catalyst, which is rare. No maker documents this code publicly. Its bank 1 twin P22AB appears in Chrysler bulletins for the 6.7 Cummins Ram; for the upstream P2240, Ford separates an open pump lead from an open return by pulsing a reference current and checking whether lambda moves by more than 0.05. P22B9/P22BA are low/high, P22BB the reference line. The warning lamp is the main sign.

causes.label: Loose or corroded pump-current terminal in the sensor connector
Pump-current wire broken near the hot exhaust
Internal open circuit in the bank 2 downstream sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value missing or frozen

P22B9.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22B9.description: P22B9 means the positive current control (pump-current) line of the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe reads below its allowed band, most often because the lead has worn through and touches ground. No maker documents this code publicly, so the logic can only be inferred from the bank 1 and upstream relatives: GM lists P22AC for the 3.0 Duramax LM2 without a threshold, Saab treats the upstream P2238 as a Type B fault, and Ford books upstream shorts as P0131. CARB requires out-of-range detection on air-fuel sensors behind the aftertreatment. The fault needs a V or boxer engine with a wide-band probe after each catalyst. P22B8 is the open, P22BA the high variant, P22AC the bank 1 code. A lit warning lamp is usually the only symptom.

causes.label: Pump-current wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Internal short in the bank 2 downstream sensor
Water in the connector

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value at an extreme

P22BA.title: O2 Sensor Positive Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BA.description: P22BA is set when the pump-current (positive current control) wire of the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe is held above its normal bias, typically through contact with the heater supply or a damaged connector letting battery voltage in. No maker documents this code publicly. Related evidence comes from bank 1 and the front sensors: GM names P22AD for the 3.0 Duramax LM2 in a harness-chafing bulletin, Saab measures about 2.8 V on the pump pins of a healthy upstream probe and rates P2239 as Type B, and Ford reports upstream shorts to power as P0132. The code only applies to dual-bank engines with a wide-band probe after each catalyst. P22B8 is the open, P22B9 the low code, P22AD bank 1. Expect the warning lamp.

causes.label: Pump-current wire shorted to the heater feed or battery voltage
Heater-to-pump-cell leakage inside the sensor
Faulty sensor interface in the ECM

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value implausibly high

P22BB.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BB.description: P22BB reports an open reference voltage line on the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe, meaning the controller has lost the Nernst-cell signal (RE/UN on Bosch, VS on NTK) it needs to regulate pump current and compute oxygen content. No maker documents this code publicly. For the upstream bank 2 relative P2247, Ford flags an open reference lead once the sensor voltage leaves 0.2-4.7 V for 10 s, and VW's 2014 Touareg data book calls the same fault an open Nernst voltage below 0.25 V or above 4.80 V with cell resistance over 950 ohms. Its bank 1 twin P22AE is listed by Chrysler for the 6.7 Cummins Ram. Only engines with two exhaust banks and a wide-band probe after each catalyst can set it. P22BC-P22BE are the performance/low/high siblings. The lamp comes on.

causes.label: Corroded or loose Nernst-cell terminal in the connector
Reference wire broken in the harness
Cracked sensing cell or internal open in the sensor

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value invalid

P22BC.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BC.description: P22BC concerns the plausibility of the Nernst-cell signal of the wide-band probe fitted after the bank 2 catalyst. The leads test fine, yet the cell voltage that the controller uses as its set point drifts, reacts slowly or cannot be held, so the computed oxygen value loses credibility. No maker documents this code publicly, and none publishes a limit for its upstream relative P2248 either. The usual reasons are physical: an aged cell whose resistance has climbed well above the nominal 300 ohms of a Bosch LSU 4.9, deposits from oil or coolant, or a weak heater. CARB requires a downstream sensor to remain good enough to judge the catalyst. Siblings: P22BB open, P22BD/P22BE low/high, P22AF bank 1. The lamp lights and catalyst results may be withheld.

causes.label: Aged downstream wide-band sensor on bank 2 with raised Nernst-cell resistance
Oil, coolant or additive deposits on the sensing element
Heater output too low to keep the cell at working temperature
Contact resistance in the Nernst-cell terminal

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen reading lags behind or is offset from the other sensors
Catalyst monitor for bank 2 does not complete

P22BD.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BD.description: P22BD reports that the Nernst-cell (reference voltage) lead of the bank 2 post-catalyst wide-band probe sits below its valid window. Bosch allows the cell a load of only about 250 microamps, so a lead whose insulation touches ground, or moisture bridging the plug, pulls the signal down quickly. No maker documents this code publicly. Upstream practice shows how close low and open lie: VW's 2014 Touareg data book counts a Nernst voltage under 0.25 V with cell resistance above 950 ohms as an open circuit (P2247), and Ford sends shorts to ground on its front probes to P0151 for bank 2. JLR names the bank 1 front analog P2245 in a bulletin on probes cracked by water splash. P22BB is the open, P22BE the high case, P22B0 bank 1. Mostly only the lamp shows.

causes.label: Nernst-cell lead chafed through and touching ground
Water or corrosion creating a leakage path in the connector
Sensing element cracked by water contact on the hot probe

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value missing or at the lower end in live data

P22BE.title: O2 Sensor Reference Voltage Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BE.description: P22BE is stored when the reference voltage lead of the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe carries more voltage than a working Nernst cell can produce. A healthy cell produces well under one volt from a source of roughly 300 ohms, so contact with the heater feed, a 5 V line or battery voltage swamps it, and a cracked ceramic can let heater potential leak into the cell. No maker documents this code publicly. On upstream probes the top of the scale is already an open-circuit criterion: Ford and Saab react above 4.7 V, VW's Touareg above 4.80 V, while Ford files shorts to battery under P0152 for bank 2. Under CARB rules a secondary sensor must also be checked for readings outside its range. P22BB is the open, P22BD the low reading, P22B1 bank 1. The lamp comes on.

causes.label: Nernst-cell lead shorted to the heater supply or another live wire
Cracked ceramic letting heater voltage into the sensing cell
Faulty sensor interface in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen reading pinned at the upper limit
Heater codes for the same sensor may appear alongside

P22BF.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22BF.description: P22BF means the negative current control lead of the bank 2 post-catalyst wide-band probe has lost continuity. That lead is the common return of pump and Nernst cell (VM/IPN on Bosch, COM on NTK); without it neither cell has a reference and the signal freezes near its bias. No maker documents this code publicly. How an open return is spotted shows in the bank 2 front code P2254: VW's 2014 Touareg data book looks for a signal of 1.47-1.52 V with cell resistance above 950 ohms, and Ford for Bosch-type probes waits for 1.45-1.55 V lasting 10 s. Chrysler lists the bank 1 twin P22B2 for the 6.7 Cummins Ram and replaces connectors first. P22C0/P22C1 are low/high, P22BB the reference lead. The lamp lights; driving feels normal.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or pushed-out terminal on the return wire
Return wire broken by heat or vibration near the exhaust
Internal break in the sensor lead or element

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream oxygen value frozen at a constant reading
Further codes for the same sensor may be stored together

P22C0.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22C0.description: P22C0 flags the negative current control line (virtual ground) of the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe as too low. The controller deliberately lifts this return above chassis ground, around 2.5 V on Saab's 2010 9-5, which lets the pump cell be driven both ways; once the wire touches ground, that bias and the lean side of the measuring range disappear. No maker documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi lists the bank 1 front analog P2252 as a two-trip code on the 2022 Outlander without giving a limit, and Ford reports shorts to ground on the VM pin of its front bank 2 probes as P0151 rather than a dedicated code. P22BF is the open, P22C1 the high reading, P22B3 bank 1. Apart from the lamp, little changes for the driver.

causes.label: Return wire chafed against body or exhaust bracket, shorted to ground
Internal short from the sensor return to the housing
Faulty bias supply in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream reading cannot show lean values
Readiness for catalyst and oxygen sensor monitors stays open

P22C1.title: O2 Sensor Negative Current Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22C1.description: P22C1 covers a return line (virtual ground) reading too high on the bank 2 post-catalyst wide-band probe: the line is pushed above the mid-level bias the controller sets, which in practice means contact with the heater supply or battery voltage, often via a melted or wet connector. With the reference raised, the rich side of the scale is lost and the oxygen value becomes useless. No maker documents this code publicly. Mitsubishi names the bank 1 front analog P2253 as a two-trip code on the 2022 Outlander, and Ford's front-probe logic books shorts to battery on any Bosch pin as P0152 for bank 2. CARB expects out-of-range detection on secondary sensors. P22BF is the open, P22C0 the low case, P22B4 bank 1. The lamp lights; the engine runs on.

causes.label: Return wire touching the heater feed or another positive supply
Heat-damaged or wet connector bridging the return to a live pin
Internal leakage from heater to sensing cells inside the probe

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream reading stuck high or implausible

P22C2.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22C2.description: P22C2 reports an open trim line on the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe. Every probe ships with a calibration resistor in its plug (pin 5, RT/IA on a Bosch LSU) that corrects for spread in its diffusion gap; on Bosch probes it sits in parallel with the controller's sense resistor. Ford explains that if it opens, all pump current is forced through that measuring resistor, tilting the lambda curve, a small error near stoichiometry. No maker documents P22C2 publicly. Upstream on bank 2 it is P2629: VW's 2014 Touareg triggers above 4.81 V, Saab tests P2626 during overrun below 750 C, and Ford bulletin 17-2124 replaces the front probes of the 3.5 GTDI for P2626/P2629. P22C3/P22C4 are low/high, P22B5 bank 1. The lamp lights.

causes.label: Corroded or loose trim-resistor terminal in the sensor plug
Trim resistor or its lead open inside the sensor connector
Trim wire broken between connector and control module

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream lambda reads slightly off, most visibly away from lambda 1

P22C3.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22C3.description: P22C3 is the low fault on the trim (label resistor) circuit of the bank 2 post-catalyst wide-band probe. Ford's 2012 OBD summary shows how makers can read this for NTK probes: at each key-on the controller switches the heater off, samples a voltage divider and estimates the label resistor; a value too high is taken as a broken or grounded lead and sets the trim-low code (P2630 for the bank 2 front probe). The controller then falls back to the resistor rank stored in memory, so the reading stays usable but less exact. No maker documents P22C3 publicly, and GM reuses the bank 1 slot P22B6 for a NOx sensor oxygen check without a bank 2 equivalent. P22C2 is the open, P22C4 the high variant. The lamp lights.

causes.label: Trim wire chafed and shorted to ground
High-resistance or corroded trim terminal raising the measured resistance
Defective label resistor in the sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light
Code typically appears right after engine start

P22C4.title: O2 Sensor Pumping Current Trim Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P22C4.description: P22C4 is the high fault on the trim circuit of the bank 2 downstream wide-band probe. In Ford's key-on check of NTK label resistors, an estimated resistance that is too low means the line is shorted to power, which sets the trim-high code (P2631 for the bank 2 front probe); the stored resistor rank then stays in use. On Bosch-type probes a raised trim voltage looks much like an open: Saab and VW both trip their front trim code above 4.81 V, so makers may sort this fault into the open-circuit code. No maker documents P22C4 publicly, and GM's bank 1 slot P22B7 serves a NOx sensor oxygen ceiling with no bank 2 counterpart. Typical causes are a short to the heater feed or a damaged plug. P22C2 is the open, P22C3 the low case. The lamp lights.

causes.label: Trim wire shorted to the heater supply or another positive feed
Heat- or water-damaged sensor plug bridging the trim pin
Internally shorted label resistor in the sensor connector

symptoms: Check engine light
Bank 2 downstream lambda slightly off; heater codes may accompany it

P22C5.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Control Circuit/Open
P22C5.description: P22C5 flags an open or broken drive circuit for the turbocharger compressor outlet valve. That valve sits in the charge-air path downstream of a compressor and decides whether this compressor feeds the engine, for example in register or two-stage charging or next to an electric auxiliary compressor. While the output is switched off, the engine control module compares the voltage on its driver with the level expected for an intact load; a reading typical of a cut wire or an unplugged connector sets the code. California OBD rules treat such boost actuators as monitored output components. No manufacturer publicly documents P22C5 itself; Mercedes-Benz uses the related stuck codes P22C8 and P22C9 on the M256 engine. With the valve unpowered, the module usually limits boost and power.

causes.label: Valve connector loose, unplugged or corroded
Broken wire in the valve harness, often near hot turbo parts
Open actuator coil inside the compressor outlet valve
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power because boost is limited
Weak or delayed pull at the speed where the second boost path should join

P22C6.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Control Circuit Low
P22C6.description: P22C6 is stored when the control line of the compressor outlet valve sits at a voltage that is too low for the current command, which normally points to a short to ground somewhere between the module and the valve. Whether the valve then stays permanently energized or never moves depends on whether the engine control module switches the ground side or the supply side of the coil. The module checks this electrically and needs no driving test, so the code can appear right after start. In a twin-path or two-stage boost layout the valve is meant to open or close one compressor branch on demand; a grounded line therefore leaves that branch in a fixed state. No manufacturer publicly documents P22C6; the description rests on the CARB output-component rules and published two-stage designs. Expect limited boost and a lit warning lamp.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through and touching ground
Internal short in the valve actuator coil
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the connector
Damaged output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on soon after starting
Boost limited, engine feels flat under load
Possible blown fuse if the short pulls heavy current

P22C7.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Control Circuit High
P22C7.description: P22C7 means the drive line of the compressor outlet valve reads higher than the module expects, typically because the wire has a short to battery voltage or the coil draws excessive current while the driver is on. Modern output stages notice the overcurrent and switch off to protect themselves, so the valve then stops responding even though nothing is open. The valve itself belongs to the boost path of register, two-stage or e-compressor charging, where it controls whether a compressor delivers into the intake. Electrical checks like this run continuously under the CARB rules for monitored output components. No manufacturer publicly documents P22C7. Compared with the open-circuit code P22C5 and the low-voltage code P22C6, the search here focuses on rubbed wires touching a positive feed or a shorted actuator winding.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Shorted turns in the valve coil causing overcurrent
Replacement valve with unsuitable coil resistance
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Valve no longer switches, boost reduced
Code returns immediately after clearing

P22C8.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Open
P22C8.description: P22C8 is a functional fault: the compressor outlet valve stays open at a moment when the control strategy expects it shut, so pressure or airflow in the boost path does not follow the command. Mercedes-Benz uses it on the M256.8 inline six with its 48-volt electric auxiliary compressor. Bulletin LI09.41-P-078735 in its second version (March 2025) added P22C800 next to P22C900 for E, CLS, GLE and GLS 450, S 500/580 e and AMG 53 models and blames a jammed check valve in the charge-air pipe; the fix is a new charge-air line with integrated check valve. Listed symptoms are the warning lamp, weak output and faulty boost. Because the module must see the valve misbehave under suitable load, the code usually needs a test drive to confirm. P22C9 is the opposite case, a valve stuck shut.

causes.label: Check valve in the charge-air pipe jammed (Mercedes M256)
Oil film or deposits holding the valve flap open
Actuator or linkage no longer able to close the valve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Little or poor power output
Boost builds poorly or unevenly

P22C9.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Closed
P22C9.description: P22C9 says the compressor outlet valve did not open when commanded, so air from the compressor it controls cannot reach the engine and the expected boost is missing. Mercedes-Benz documents the code for the M256.8 six-cylinder: the first version of bulletin LI09.41-P-078735 (December 2024) covers P22C900 in the MRG3 engine control unit on models from 2019 to 2025 and traces it to a check valve in the charge-air pipe that is jammed shut; the charge-air line with integrated check valve is replaced. Symptoms listed there are the engine lamp, reduced output and a boost malfunction. The check runs only under operating conditions that call for the valve to open, so confirmation usually takes a drive under load. Unlike P22C8, the risk here is a blocked path in which a compressor works against a closed outlet.

causes.label: Check valve in the charge-air pipe jammed shut (Mercedes M256)
Valve actuator, vacuum or pressure supply unable to open the valve
Valve seized by deposits or corrosion

symptoms: Check engine light on
Noticeable loss of power under load
Boost malfunction, possibly with underboost code

P22CA.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Switching Valve Control Circuit/Open
P22CA.description: P22CA reports an open drive circuit for the compressor outlet switching valve. In two-stage or register boost systems the outlet flap is often moved by vacuum or pressure, and this electrically driven switching valve decides when that actuating medium reaches it; Ford's two-stage patent notes such valves may be worked electrically or by vacuum. With the circuit open, the switching valve stays in its rest position and the outlet flap no longer changes over. Nissan names the part on the Cummins 5.0 V8 diesel of the 2016 Titan XD (TC outlet switching valve, see P22CE), but no manufacturer publicly documents P22CA. The module detects the fault electrically with the output off, so it is independent of driving style. Check plug, harness and coil resistance first.

causes.label: Switching valve connector loose or corroded
Broken wire between module and switching valve
Open coil in the switching solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Boost changeover no longer happens, power limited
Hesitation when accelerating through the switching speed

P22CB.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
P22CB.description: P22CB is set when the control line of the compressor outlet switching valve shows too little voltage for the present command, most often because the wire or the solenoid has a short to ground. On a low-side driven solenoid such a short can hold the valve energized all the time, so the outlet flap it supplies with vacuum or pressure stays in its switched position whatever the rpm and load. The module spots the fault through its driver diagnostics without any special driving. The solenoid is a small part in the actuating line of the outlet flap and is usually inexpensive; the wiring near the hot turbo area deserves a careful look. No manufacturer publicly documents P22CB. If P22C6 is present as well, look for a shared harness section or connector.

causes.label: Control wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short in the switching solenoid
Water or corrosion in the solenoid connector

symptoms: Check engine light on
Boost path stuck in one mode, uneven power across the rev range
Reduced power at low or high engine speed

P22CC.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Switching Valve Control Circuit High
P22CC.description: P22CC indicates that the drive line of the compressor outlet switching valve carries more voltage or current than allowed, usually a short to a battery feed or a solenoid with shorted windings. The output stage of the engine control module then tends to shut down for self-protection, which leaves the switching valve unpowered and the outlet flap in its rest position. On register or two-stage charging this typically means the second compressor branch is no longer brought in or taken out as planned. The test is electrical and continuous, as CARB requires for monitored output parts. No manufacturer publicly documents P22CC. Measure coil resistance against the specification and check whether the wire touches a positive feed; replacing the module is a last resort.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Shorted windings in the switching solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Outlet flap no longer switches, power reduced
Fault returns as soon as the valve is commanded

P22CD.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Switching Valve Stuck Open
P22CD.description: P22CD is a plausibility fault: the engine control module commanded the compressor outlet switching valve shut, yet boost pressure, airflow or a position signal behave as if the switched path were still open. Because the switching valve feeds the actuator of the outlet flap, a mechanically stuck solenoid, a leaking control hose or a flap held open by the actuator all lead to the same result. In a sequential setup this can let charge air leak back through an idle compressor at low engine speed, so boost builds slowly. The check needs the operating point where the valve should be closed and is therefore confirmed during driving. No manufacturer publicly documents P22CD; Nissan uses the sister code P22CE on the Cummins 5.0 of the Titan XD. P22CE covers the reverse case.

causes.label: Switching solenoid mechanically stuck in the open position
Leaking, cracked or swapped control hose to the flap actuator
Outlet flap or its actuator unable to close

symptoms: Check engine light on
Sluggish boost build-up at low engine speed
Hissing or whistling noise from the intake side

P22CE.title: Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P22CE.description: P22CE is set when the compressor outlet switching valve was told to open but the boost system shows no sign that the switched path changed over. Nissan documents the code as TC Outlet Switching Valve Stuck Closed for the 2016 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 litre V8 diesel and its two-stage turbocharger. Bulletin NTB16-051 (May 2016) links it to operation at or below 0 °C and to hesitation on acceleration after an overnight indoor soak followed by a cold drive below -18 °C; the remedy is reprogramming the ECM. The revised NTB16-051a (June 2017) keeps P22CE in the list. Besides software, frozen or collapsed control hoses and a sticking solenoid are plausible causes. The driver notices weak pull while the second stage should come in.

causes.label: Engine control software reacting wrongly in cold weather (Nissan Titan XD bulletin)
Collapsed, kinked or frozen control hose to the outlet flap actuator
Switching solenoid stuck in the closed position
Insufficient vacuum or pressure supply for the actuator

symptoms: Check engine light on, mostly in cold weather
Hesitation when accelerating until the engine is warm
Weak pull in the speed range where the second stage should help

P22CF.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Control Circuit/Open
P22CF.description: P22CF points to an open drive circuit of the turbocharger turbine inlet valve, the exhaust-side valve that either lets gas skip the small first-stage turbine of a series two-stage system or isolates a second turbine in a parallel-sequential layout. GM's diesel OBD tables (17OBDG04 and 18OBDG04) group P22CF, P22D0 and P22D1 as the faults of the high-pressure turbine bypass actuator (HTB); while one is active, boost control leaves closed-loop operation. A GM patent on a series-sequential turbo shows this bypass valve with both a current sensor and a position sensor. With the circuit open the valve sits in its spring position, often causing slow boost or a power cap. No public source gives GM's thresholds for P22CF; the electrical check runs whenever the actuator is in use.

causes.label: Actuator connector loose, heat-damaged or corroded
Broken wire near the exhaust manifold or turbo
Open winding in the turbine valve actuator or its control solenoid
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power, boost control in fallback mode
Turbo lag or a missing second-stage push

P22D0.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Control Circuit Low
P22D0.description: P22D0 is logged when the drive circuit of the turbine inlet valve shows a voltage below the expected range, the classic sign of a short to ground in the wire or inside the actuator. GM lists P22D0 together with P22CF and P22D1 in the fault bundle of its high-pressure turbine bypass actuator in the 2017 and 2018 diesel OBD documents; any of them takes boost control out of closed loop. Because the exhaust valve sits right on the hot turbo housing, heat-brittle insulation that rubs through is a likely cause. Depending on how the driver is wired, the valve may then stay energized or never move, so exhaust skips the high-pressure stage at the wrong time or never. No public source gives GM's thresholds. P22D0 differs from P22CF by a short rather than a break.

causes.label: Heat-damaged wire rubbing through to ground
Internal short in the valve actuator or control solenoid
Damaged output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Power limited, boost too low or uneven
Code sets right after start without a test drive

P22D1.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Control Circuit High
P22D1.description: P22D1 tells you the drive circuit of the turbine inlet valve reads too high, which usually means a short to battery voltage or an actuator that draws overcurrent. GM assigns P22D1, along with P22CF and P22D0, to its high-pressure turbine bypass actuator in the 2017 and 2018 diesel OBD tables, and boost control drops out of closed loop when the fault is active. The GM patent on series-sequential turbocharging describes a current sensor on this valve, which is how an overcurrent can be seen directly. Once the driver protects itself and shuts down, the valve no longer follows commands. Compared with its siblings, the search concentrates on positive-feed contact and the actuator winding. No public source gives GM's threshold values for P22D1.

causes.label: Actuator wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed
Actuator winding shorted or mechanically jammed, drawing overcurrent
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power, boost control in fallback mode
Fault comes back as soon as the valve is driven

P22D2.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Stuck Open
P22D2.description: P22D2 means the turbine inlet valve stays open after the module asked it to close. In a series two-stage system, an open valve lets exhaust skip the small high-pressure turbine, so low-speed boost and response suffer.
