In a parallel-sequential system such as Jaguar's 3.0 V6 diesel, where valves keep the secondary turbo out of the exhaust stream and intake until about 2,800 rpm, an open valve feeds that turbo too early and raises pumping losses. The module detects the fault by comparing commanded and measured valve position or the boost response, so it needs a drive at the relevant operating point. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D2 with thresholds. Soot and a seized pivot are typical; vacuum-driven designs add leaking control lines.

causes.label: Soot or corrosion seizing the valve shaft in the open position
Leaking or detached control line on a vacuum-operated actuator
Actuator or linkage unable to close the valve
Position sensor reporting open although the valve moved

symptoms: Check engine light on
Noticeable turbo lag at low engine speed
Higher fuel consumption
Reduced power mode

P22D3.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Stuck Closed
P22D3.description: P22D3 is stored when the turbine inlet valve does not open on command. In a series two-stage layout all exhaust must then pass the small high-pressure stage even at high load, raising back-pressure and risking overboost or turbo overspeed, so the module caps power. In a parallel-sequential layout the second turbo never comes in. Stellantis documents the code on the 2026 Jeep Cherokee with the 1.6 litre turbo hybrid: bulletin 18-052-26 Rev. A (June 2026) states that P22D3-00 sets falsely on vehicles built from mid-December 2025 to late April 2026 and adds PCM software that disables it. On other vehicles, check for a valve seized by soot, a failed actuator or a lacking vacuum supply. P22D2 is the opposite, a valve stuck open.

causes.label: Engine software setting the code falsely (Jeep Cherokee 2026 bulletin)
Valve seized closed by soot or corrosion
Actuator, linkage or vacuum supply unable to open the valve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Power capped at higher engine speed and load
Possible overboost code alongside

P22D4.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor Circuit
P22D4.description: P22D4 is the general circuit fault of the sensor that reports how far the turbine inlet valve is open. Engineering literature explains why this valve, unlike most compressor bypass valves, has feedback: a Ford two-stage patent calls the high-pressure turbine bypass valve emissions-critical and therefore actively controlled with a position sensor, and a GM patent uses the measured opening to run the valve in position control. When the signal is missing or cannot be read at all, the module loses that feedback and typically switches to a fixed fallback position with reduced boost. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D4. The narrower sibling codes P22D6 and P22D7 name a too-low or too-high voltage; P22D4 is used when the fault cannot be assigned that precisely.

causes.label: Loose, heat-damaged or corroded sensor connector
Damaged sensor wiring near the turbo
Failed position sensor, often integrated in the actuator

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power, turbo valve held in a fallback position

P22D5.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P22D5.description: P22D5 is a plausibility fault of the turbine inlet valve position signal. The voltage stays inside its electrical limits, yet it does not match what the module expects, for instance the reading lags the commanded position, fails to reach the learned end stops or does not change when the valve is moved. CARB requires input sensors of this kind to be checked for rationality as well as for circuit faults. Since a GM patent describes the valve being run in position control with sensor feedback, a wrong but believable reading directly corrupts the valve setting and thus boost. Causes include a sensor drifting with heat, a slipped magnet or linkage, and a valve that moves sluggishly so that position and command diverge. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D5.

causes.label: Valve or linkage sluggish from soot, so position lags the command
Position sensor drifting or misaligned on the actuator
End positions not relearned after actuator replacement

symptoms: Check engine light on
Jerky or delayed changeover between turbo stages
Boost fluctuates under steady throttle

P22D6.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor Circuit Low
P22D6.description: P22D6 is set when the position sensor signal of the turbine inlet valve falls below its lowest valid voltage. Position sensors on such actuators normally work on a 5-volt reference with a signal that never reaches the rails in normal use, so a reading near zero means a lost reference, a signal wire shorted to ground or an internal sensor fault rather than a real valve position. The engine control module flags this electrically and quickly, without needing a test drive. It then ignores the reading and usually parks the valve in a safe position with reduced boost. Two-stage patents from Ford and GM describe exactly this kind of position feedback on the turbine bypass valve. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D6. Check the reference voltage at the plug first.

causes.label: 5-volt reference open or pulled down by another shorted sensor
Signal wire shorted to ground
Internal failure of the position sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power, valve in fallback position
Other sensor codes on the same reference circuit possible

P22D7.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor Circuit High
P22D7.description: P22D7 is logged when the position signal of the turbine inlet valve rises above its highest valid voltage. A reading pinned near the reference level usually comes from an open sensor ground, a signal wire touching the 5-volt reference or battery voltage, or a failed sensor element, not from the valve itself. Like its low-voltage counterpart P22D6, this is a pure circuit check that runs continuously and does not depend on load. Without valid feedback, the module can no longer run the valve in position control as described in the GM two-stage patent, so it typically fixes the valve and limits boost. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D7. Inspecting the ground pin and wiring near the hot exhaust side usually finds the fault faster than swapping the actuator.

causes.label: Open or high-resistance sensor ground
Signal wire shorted to the 5-volt reference or battery voltage
Internal failure of the position sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on
Reduced power, valve held in fallback position

P22D8.title: Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P22D8.description: P22D8 covers short dropouts or jumps in the position signal of the turbine inlet valve: the value leaps faster than the valve could physically move, or briefly disappears and returns. Such patterns typically come from a connector with fretting contacts, a wire breaking inside its insulation near the vibrating, hot turbo, or a sensor that fails under heat. Because the module uses this feedback to control the valve, as the Ford and GM two-stage patents describe, every glitch can make the valve hunt and boost wobble. The fault often appears only on rough roads or when the engine bay is hot, and may have vanished by the time the car is in the workshop. No manufacturer publicly documents P22D8. Wiggle testing with live data while watching the signal helps to find it.

causes.label: Loose or fretting contacts in the sensor connector
Wire breaking intermittently from heat and vibration
Position sensor dropping out when hot

symptoms: Check engine light on, sometimes only now and then
Boost surging or hunting
Brief loss of power on rough roads

P22D9.title: Cylinder 1 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22D9.description: P22D9 reports a broken control circuit at the gas injector of cylinder 1, the solenoid that meters CNG or LPG into the intake port whenever a bi-fuel or dedicated gas engine runs on the alternative fuel. The driver stage notices the break because no current flows when it switches on, or because the expected off-state voltage on its pin is missing. No maker publishes P22D9 itself: the TransEco AFCM list and Ford's 2014 code list only carry the Low/High pair P22DA/P22DB, and TransEco even files an open line under Low. GM's bi-fuel Silverado moves the injectors over to gas one by one starting with cylinder 1, so a break here tends to show up right at the changeover. Bi-fuel cars usually return to gasoline; a dedicated gas engine loses cylinder 1.

causes.label: Open solenoid winding in the cylinder 1 gas injector
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the gas injector
Broken wire or failed splice in the gas system harness
Defective driver stage in the gas or engine control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Engine changes back to gasoline or refuses to switch to gas
Misfire on cylinder 1 in gas mode (dedicated engines)

P22DA.title: Cylinder 1 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22DA.description: P22DA means the cylinder 1 gas injector control wire reads too low. TransEco Energy's DTC list for its CNG control module (AFCM v1.4) blames either a grounded wire or an open line, turns on the MIL in bi-fuel installations and reacts the same way it would to the matching gasoline injector fault. Ford's 2014 OBD code list carries P22DA as a MIL code as well. With a low-side driver, a control wire touching ground can keep the injector energized whenever its supply is live, so cylinder 1 may get gas without pause and run very rich; an interrupted wire leaves it without gas. P22DB covers the high side and P22D9 the plain open circuit. The gasoline injector of the same cylinder reports through P0261 instead.

causes.label: Control wire of the cylinder 1 gas injector chafed through to ground
Interrupted control wire or connector (logged as Low by some modules)
Water or corrosion in the injector connector
Faulty output stage in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Very rough running on cylinder 1 in gas mode, possibly rich misfire
Gas system switches back to gasoline

P22DB.title: Cylinder 1 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22DB.description: P22DB flags a control circuit of the cylinder 1 gas injector that stays too high. TransEco Energy's AFCM fault list traces it to a short to battery voltage, lights the MIL for bi-fuel use and applies the same fallback as for the gasoline injector fault; Ford's 2014 code list also marks P22DB for the MIL. When the line is held at supply voltage, the driver cannot pull it down, so the injector never opens and cylinder 1 receives no gas: a lean misfire on that cylinder in gas mode is the typical result, often together with P0301. Many output stages also shut off to protect themselves from the excessive current. A coil with shorted turns can look the same. P22DA is the low side, P0262 the code for the gasoline injector.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery or injector supply voltage
Shorted turns in the cylinder 1 gas injector coil
Output stage of the gas control module damaged

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Lean misfire on cylinder 1 in gas mode, often with P0301
Engine runs normally on gasoline

P22DC.title: Cylinder 1 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22DC.description: P22DC is meant for a cylinder 1 gas injector whose circuit is electrically intact but whose response looks wrong, such as a current trace that never reaches its peak or does not fall back to the hold level, or a coil whose resistance has drifted. A Ford patent on driving a second type of injector through an interface (US 8,161,946) describes this logic: the injector counts as degraded if it ignores on and off commands or stays at peak current. No vehicle maker publishes P22DC; TransEco and Ford's 2014 list stop at Low/High. A sticking injector is a plausible trigger, which is why GM's bi-fuel pickups filter the gas through a coalescing element that keeps oil and liquids away from the injectors. Expect a misfiring cylinder 1 or a return to gasoline.

causes.label: Cylinder 1 gas injector sticking from oil residue or debris in the gas
Injector coil resistance outside its specification
Weak supply voltage to the injector bank
Injector of the wrong type or impedance installed

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Uneven running in gas mode, misfire counts on cylinder 1
Higher gas consumption or switch back to gasoline

P22DD.title: Cylinder 2 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22DD.description: P22DD signals an interruption in the circuit of the cylinder 2 gas injector. On many systems that circuit is not driven by the engine computer: Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG trucks used a separate alternative fuel control module holding drivers for both injector sets, with heavier stages for the gas injectors because they draw more current. GM's 2014 bi-fuel Silverado likewise stores gas faults in its own CNG control module (bulletin PIP5181), so a scan tool has to read that module as well. No maker documents P22DD publicly; TransEco and Ford list only the cylinder 2 Low/High codes P22DE and P22DF, and TransEco assigns an open line to Low. Look for a burnt coil or a separated connector before blaming the module.

causes.label: Burnt-out or open coil in the cylinder 2 gas injector
Connector at the cylinder 2 injector loose or pulled off
Wire break between gas control module and injector
Failed injector driver in the separate gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Gas mode not available or ends shortly after switching
Misfire on cylinder 2 when running on gas

P22DE.title: Cylinder 2 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22DE.description: P22DE stands for a control line of the cylinder 2 gas injector whose voltage is too low. TransEco Energy's AFCM fault table blames a grounded or interrupted wire and turns on the MIL for bi-fuel vehicles; Ford's 2014 OBD code list includes P22DE as a MIL code too. California's OBD rule counts a bi-fuel car among alternate-fueled vehicles just for the periods it actually burns gas, so this monitor matters mainly in gas mode, and on gasoline the car normally behaves as usual. If the grounded wire keeps the injector energized, cylinder 2 is flooded with gas and the plug may foul; a separated wire starves it instead. P22DF is the high side, P22DD the open-circuit code, and P0264 belongs to the gasoline injector.

causes.label: Cylinder 2 injector control wire grounded on engine or body
Open wire or pin, reported as Low by modules like the TransEco AFCM
Shorted output transistor in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Rich misfire or fouled spark plug on cylinder 2 in gas mode
Gas operation interrupted, engine runs on gasoline

P22DF.title: Cylinder 2 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22DF.description: P22DF indicates that the control circuit of the cylinder 2 gas injector reads high, which TransEco Energy's AFCM table attributes to a short to power; MIL on for bi-fuel use. Ford's 2014 code list likewise flags P22DF for the MIL. A line stuck at supply voltage keeps the injector closed, so cylinder 2 burns no gas and misfires lean, while running on gasoline is unaffected. On GM's 2015 bi-fuel Impala the ECM drives the CNG injectors itself and, if it sees a fuel delivery problem in one system, changes over to the other, so the driver may only notice a switch back to gasoline. A coil with internal shorts can produce the same overcurrent. P22DE is the low side; P0265 is the high-side code of the gasoline injector.

causes.label: Cylinder 2 control wire touching a live supply wire
Internal short in the cylinder 2 gas injector coil
Driver protection in the control module tripping due to a fault

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Cylinder 2 misfires only on gas
Unexpected return to gasoline

P22E0.title: Cylinder 2 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22E0.description: P22E0 covers a cylinder 2 gas injector circuit that passes the plain open and short checks yet responds outside its expected window. California's OBD regulation asks for output components to be checked not only for circuit faults but also for a proper functional response; for alternate-fueled vehicles from 2004 to 2018 the gasoline rules applied unchanged, and from 2019 the maker submits its own monitoring plan. The Ford patent US 8,161,946 gives an example of such a functional check for an injector fed by an extra driver. No maker publishes P22E0 itself. Typical triggers are a sluggish or partly stuck injector, a coil past its specification or a driver that cannot deliver the needed current. Cylinder 2 then runs unevenly on gas.

causes.label: Cylinder 2 gas injector opening or closing too slowly
Coil resistance of the injector out of tolerance
Driver stage or supply unable to provide the required current

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Uneven idle on gas, cylinder 2 misfire counts
Fuel trim drifts in gas mode

P22E1.title: Cylinder 3 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22E1.description: P22E1 marks an open control circuit at the cylinder 3 gas injector. Circuit continuity checks of this kind run all the time: California's OBD rule defines continuous monitoring as always enabled with at least two samples per second, so a break is caught within moments once the gas system is in use. No maker documents P22E1 openly. TransEco's AFCM list and Ford's 2014 code list give cylinder 3 only the Low/High codes P22E2 and P22E3, and TransEco counts an open line as Low. On GM's bi-fuel pickups the gas injectors sit on separate rails with hoses leading to nozzles at each intake runner, and their wiring runs along those rails; a pulled connector after work in that area is a common reason. Bi-fuel cars carry on with gasoline.

causes.label: Cylinder 3 injector connector left off or not latched after service
Open coil in the cylinder 3 gas injector
Wire broken where the harness runs along the gas rail

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Gas mode switches off soon after changeover
Cylinder 3 misfire on dedicated gas engines

P22E2.title: Cylinder 3 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22E2.description: P22E2 is logged when the control circuit of the cylinder 3 gas injector reads low. In TransEco Energy's AFCM table the cause column says shorted to ground or open, the MIL comes on in bi-fuel systems and the reaction copies that for a gasoline injector fault. Ford's 2014 code list lists P22E2 as a MIL code. Because a grounded control wire can leave the injector energized, cylinder 3 may be flooded with gas; the catalyst then gets unburnt fuel, and prolonged driving in gas mode is a bad idea. With a broken wire the cylinder is simply starved. Typical spots are chafe points against brackets or the intake manifold. P22E3 is the high side and P22E1 the pure open-circuit code; the gasoline injector uses P0267.

causes.label: Cylinder 3 control wire rubbed through against a bracket or the manifold
Broken wire or terminal in the cylinder 3 injector circuit
Shorted driver output in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Cylinder 3 runs rich or misfires in gas mode
Smell of unburnt gas at the exhaust

P22E3.title: Cylinder 3 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22E3.description: P22E3 tells that the cylinder 3 gas injector circuit is held high. TransEco Energy's AFCM list names a short to power, MIL on for bi-fuel use, and Ford's 2014 code list also ties P22E3 to the MIL. With the line stuck at supply voltage the injector cannot be switched on, so cylinder 3 gets no gas and misfires lean. In GM's bi-fuel Silverado layout the ECM calculates the pulse widths while a separate fuel injector control module passes them to the gas injectors, so the fault can sit in the wiring between that module and the injector, in the injector itself, or in the module output. Gasoline operation remains normal. P22E2 is the low side and P0268 the high-side code of the gasoline injector.

causes.label: Cylinder 3 control wire shorted to a 12 V feed
Shorted turns in the cylinder 3 gas injector
Faulty output of the injector control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Lean misfire on cylinder 3 in gas mode, often with P0303
Noticeable loss of power on gas

P22E4.title: Cylinder 3 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22E4.description: P22E4 points to a cylinder 3 gas injector whose circuit works but whose electrical behaviour does not match the command. Peak-and-hold gas injectors first draw a high opening current and then a lower holding current; Ford's patent US 8,161,946 treats an injector that stays at peak or ignores commands as degraded and reports this back to the engine computer. No maker documents P22E4 publicly. The code is distinct from pressure problems: GM's bi-fuel pickups regulate gas to roughly 896 kPa ahead of the rail, and a wrong rail pressure has its own sensor codes. Here the injector or its driver is suspect, often after oil or debris from the gas has made the armature stick. Cylinder 3 then runs unevenly on gas.

causes.label: Armature of the cylinder 3 gas injector gummed up by oil or debris
Injector coil aged or overheated, resistance out of range
Weak driver output or poor supply ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Intermittent cylinder 3 misfire on gas
Rising gas consumption

P22E5.title: Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22E5.description: P22E5 is the open-circuit code for the cylinder 4 gas injector; on four-cylinder gas engines it is the last injector of the set. The driver sees no current when it switches the injector on. No maker documents P22E5 in public sources: TransEco and Ford's 2014 list stop at the cylinder 4 Low/High codes P22E6 and P22E7, and TransEco files an open line under Low. Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG trucks show a typical layout where gas enters through sleeves in the gasoline injector seats, with the gas injectors driven by a separate module, so connectors sit close to hot engine parts. Expect a switch back to gasoline on bi-fuel cars and a dead cylinder 4 on dedicated gas engines. P0204 is the gasoline counterpart.

causes.label: Open coil in the cylinder 4 gas injector
Heat-damaged or brittle connector near the exhaust side
Broken wire in the cylinder 4 injector circuit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Gas mode unavailable, car runs on gasoline only
Cylinder 4 dead on a dedicated gas engine

P22E6.title: Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22E6.description: P22E6 reports a low signal on the cylinder 4 gas injector control wire. TransEco Energy's AFCM table gives short to ground or open as the cause and turns the MIL on in bi-fuel installations, keeping the same failure response as for gasoline; Ford's 2014 code list carries P22E6 with the MIL as well. On Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG system the control module would only start the engine on gas once rail pressure reached about 517 kPa, so a failed gas start alone does not prove an injector fault: check for this code first. A grounded line can hold cylinder 4 permanently open and flood it; an interrupted one leaves it dry. P22E7 is the high side, P22E5 the plain open circuit, and P0270 the gasoline injector code.

causes.label: Cylinder 4 control wire grounded through damaged insulation
Separated terminal or broken wire in the cylinder 4 circuit
Damaged driver output in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Cylinder 4 runs rich or cuts out on gas
Engine stays on or returns to gasoline

P22E7.title: Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22E7.description: P22E7 says the control circuit of the cylinder 4 gas injector reads high. TransEco Energy's fault table blames a short to power and lights the MIL for bi-fuel use; Ford's 2014 code list also marks P22E7 as a MIL code. The injector then cannot open and cylinder 4 misfires lean whenever gas is selected. Timing matters for diagnosis: GM's 2015 bi-fuel Impala starts on gasoline below about -20 °C and only moves to CNG once coolant reaches 50 °C, so on such cars the fault may appear only after warm-up. Check the wire for contact with a live feed and measure the injector coil for internal shorts. P22E6 is the low side; P0271 is the corresponding code for the gasoline injector of cylinder 4.

causes.label: Cylinder 4 control wire in contact with a 12 V circuit
Cylinder 4 injector coil with internal short
Output stage of the controlling module defective

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Cylinder 4 misfire only after the switch to gas
Reduced power in gas mode

P22E8.title: Cylinder 4 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22E8.description: P22E8 applies when the cylinder 4 gas injector circuit is complete but the measured response lies outside the plausible range, for instance an opening current that rises too slowly or a hold phase that never settles. No vehicle maker documents P22E8 openly; the published lists from TransEco and Ford end at Low/High. Gas quality is a frequent background factor: GM fits a coalescing filter with a 6 micron element in its bi-fuel pickups because contaminants and liquids in the gas can damage the injectors, and the filter has to be drained and replaced at intervals. A neglected filter can therefore show up as this code. Cleaning rarely helps; the injector or the complete rail is usually replaced, then a drive on gas confirms the repair.

causes.label: Cylinder 4 injector fouled by oil or liquids, often from a neglected gas filter
Aged injector coil with changed resistance
Low system voltage during cranking or at idle

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Rough idle on gas, smooth on gasoline
Gas mode ends after a while

P22E9.title: Cylinder 5 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22E9.description: P22E9 is the open-circuit code for the cylinder 5 gas injector and can only appear on engines with five or more cylinders, such as the V6 of GM's bi-fuel Impala or the 6.0-litre V8 of its bi-fuel Silverado and Sierra. The driver detects the break because current is missing when the injector is commanded on. No maker documents P22E9 publicly; TransEco's AFCM list and Ford's 2014 code list only use P22EA and P22EB for cylinder 5, and TransEco treats an open line as Low. On V engines the injector wiring of each bank often runs in its own harness branch, so check the cylinder 5 branch from the module to the injector. Bi-fuel vehicles fall back to gasoline; P0205 is the gasoline counterpart.

causes.label: Open coil in the cylinder 5 gas injector
Loose connector in the harness branch for this bank
Open driver output in the gas or injector control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Engine returns to gasoline after switching to gas
Cylinder 5 misfire if gas operation continues

P22EA.title: Cylinder 5 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22EA.description: P22EA stands for a low voltage on the cylinder 5 gas injector control wire, a code limited to engines with at least five cylinders. TransEco Energy's AFCM table points to a grounded wire or an open line, lights the MIL in bi-fuel use and applies the gasoline injector fault response; Ford's 2014 code list, written for V8 engines among others, keeps P22EA as a MIL code. A control wire resting on ground can energize the injector without pause, so cylinder 5 may run far too rich and its spark plug may foul; with an open line it misses gas instead. Inspect the wire along the rail of the affected bank first. P22EB is the high side, P22E9 the plain open circuit, and the gasoline injector reports P0273.

causes.label: Cylinder 5 control wire shorted to ground along the gas rail
Interrupted wire or terminal, flagged as Low by some modules
Shorted output stage in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Cylinder 5 runs rich or misfires in gas mode
Fouled spark plug on cylinder 5

P22EB.title: Cylinder 5 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22EB.description: P22EB reports that the cylinder 5 gas injector control circuit is too high, which TransEco Energy's AFCM list attributes to a short to power with the MIL on for bi-fuel use; Ford's 2014 code list likewise carries P22EB for the MIL. The injector stays closed, so cylinder 5 burns no gas and misfires lean, usually logged together with P0305. Gas injectors pull more current than gasoline injectors: Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG documentation notes that their drivers had to be stronger because of the extra heat, which also means a shorted coil quickly overloads the output. Measure the coil resistance and look for chafing against a live feed. P22EA is the low side; the gasoline injector of cylinder 5 reports P0274.

causes.label: Cylinder 5 control wire chafed against a supply wire
Overheated cylinder 5 gas injector with shorted turns
Overloaded driver output in the gas control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Lean misfire on cylinder 5 in gas mode, often with P0305
Normal running on gasoline

P22EC.title: Cylinder 5 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22EC.description: P22EC is the plausibility code for the cylinder 5 gas injector circuit on engines with five or more cylinders: wiring and coil pass the basic checks, but the injector does not respond as commanded. California's OBD rule requires such output components to be checked for a proper functional response, and from model year 2019 the maker of an alternate-fueled vehicle submits its own plan for which monitors apply. Ford's patent US 8,161,946 describes one way to do it, judging an injector by whether its current follows the peak-and-hold pattern. No maker publishes P22EC itself. A sticking armature, a heat-aged coil or a weak driver are the usual suspects. Bi-fuel cars may keep running on gas with a rough cylinder 5 or drop back to gasoline.

causes.label: Sticking armature in the cylinder 5 gas injector
Heat-aged coil with drifting resistance
Driver or supply not delivering the full opening current

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Rough cylinder 5 on gas or return to gasoline
Fuel trim on the affected bank drifts in gas mode

P22ED.title: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22ED.description: P22ED marks an open control circuit at the cylinder 6 gas injector, the last injector on six-cylinder engines like the 3.6-litre V6 of GM's 2015 bi-fuel Impala, where the ECM drives the CNG injectors directly. Current is missing when the injector should open, so the module records the break. No maker documents P22ED openly: the TransEco AFCM table and Ford's 2014 code list give cylinder 6 only P22EE and P22EF, and TransEco reports an interrupted line as Low, so the same fault may appear as P22EE on such systems. The Impala's ECM changes to the other fuel when one system cannot deliver, so the driver mostly sees gasoline operation and the MIL. Check coil resistance and connector first. P0206 is the gasoline counterpart.

causes.label: Open coil in the cylinder 6 gas injector
Loose or corroded connector at cylinder 6
Broken wire between control module and cylinder 6 injector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Vehicle runs on gasoline although gas is selected
Cylinder 6 misfire on dedicated gas engines

P22EE.title: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
P22EE.description: Cylinder 6 alternative-fuel injector drive line stuck low — short to ground. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

causes.label: Short to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Harness chafing through insulation

symptoms: Check engine light on
Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Increased fuel consumption
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P22EF.title: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
P22EF.description: Cylinder 6 alternative-fuel injector drive line stuck high — short to B+. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

causes.label: Short to B+
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Check engine light on
Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Increased fuel consumption
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P22F0.title: Cylinder 6 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Range/Performance
P22F0.description: Cylinder 6 alternative-fuel injector is electrically OK but its response (current ramp, dwell, peak voltage) is off-spec — typically winding ageing.

causes.label: Winding ageing
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor mounting loose - signal damping

symptoms: Check engine light on
Misfire or rough idle on the affected cylinder
Increased fuel consumption
Possible fuel smell or smoke from exhaust

P22F1.title: Cylinder 7 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22F1.description: The particulate matter (PM) sensor heater on diesel after-DPF systems does not reach or hold the calibrated operating temperature within the expected time. Without proper heating the PM sensor cannot be regenerated and read correctly.

causes.label: PM sensor aging
Increased heater resistance

Harness chafing through insulation

P22F5.title: Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit/Open
P22F5.description: The drive circuit for the cylinder 8 alternative-fuel injector is open. Bi-fuel vehicles have a second set of injectors for CNG, LPG, or hydrogen — separate from the petrol/diesel injectors.

Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P22F7.description: Cylinder 8 alternative-fuel injector drive line stuck high — short to B+. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

P22F8.description: Cylinder 8 alternative-fuel injector is electrically OK but its response (current ramp, dwell, peak voltage) is off-spec — typically winding ageing.

P22F9.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22F9.description: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

causes.label: Sensor aged or protection cap clogged
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P22FA.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response High to Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FA.description: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 responds too slowly when NOx concentration falls (typically observed when SCR dosing increases). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

causes.label: Sensor aged
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P22FB.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Sensing Element (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P22FB.description: The wide-band sensing element of the NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 1 reports an internal performance fault — typically poisoning, condensate damage, or end of service life.

causes.label: Element poisoned or end of life
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P22FC.title: NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P22FC.description: NOx sensor on bank 1 sensor 2 responds too slowly when NOx concentration rises (typically observed when SCR dosing is reduced or stopped). The sensor has aged or its protection cap is clogged.

P22FD.title: NOx Sensor Performance Slow Response High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P22FD.description: The downstream NOx sensor on bank 1 (post-SCR) responds too slowly when NOx levels fall after a reductant injection event. The control unit measures the time between commanded reductant dose and the resulting NOx drop and finds it exceeds the diagnostic threshold, indicating an aged sensor element.

causes.label: NOx sensor element aged or thermally damaged
SCR efficiency reduced (catalyst aged or contaminated)
Reductant injector dosing drift

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P22FE.title: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2
P22FE.description: NOx Sensor Sensing Element Bank 1 Sensor 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

causes.label: Sensor element poisoned by silicone, sulphur or oil ash
Thermal shock from condensate (cold start with wet exhaust)
Sensor at end of service life

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
AdBlue/DEF level or quality warning
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
Failed emissions inspection (NOx)

P22FF.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P22FF.description: The temperature sensor at the SCR catalyst inlet reports a value below the threshold needed for efficient ammonia conversion. Below roughly 180-200 °C the SCR cannot reduce NOx and reductant injection is suspended; if this is detected continuously the ECU sets the fault.

causes.label: Temperature sensor drifts low or has shifted resistance
Short-trip operation - exhaust never reaches operating temperature
Exhaust heater or heat-management strategy not active

symptoms: Check engine light on
Failed emissions inspection
Possibly slightly increased fuel consumption
Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load
